text: My favorite PC game of all time!

The only guaruntees in TF2 are the following:
1. Lenny spamming.
2. Sentries, everywhere.
3. Inadequate "team" mates.
4. Too many spies.
5. Too many snipers.
6. No medics.
7. Random krits, no less than 408 times per round.
8. The phlog.
9. The phlog.
10. Well-timed autobalance.
Most fun I've ever had the pleasure to be a part of, and if you haven't played this game yet, give it a chance.

*Insert thrilling TF2 Music here*
You kill the medic, you keep going, a demo pick, kill the enemy scout, kill the soldier, kill the mother♥♥♥♥ing pyro, kill the heavy, kill the spy, kill the engi, you run to last, you have 10 seconds to capture the point else your team loses.
But then. A mighty creature called "The gibus sniper". It charges. and. it bodyshots. You are dead.
*Sad music comes here*
You let your team down. Everyone hates you.
You are done. you grab the rope. but then. the mighty gaben comes... whats that? a gibus. you wear it. you're happy. Your life is complete.
Welcome to team fortress 2. After nine years of development, bodyshots are still a thing.

AS many people would say about this game being one of the awesome(R) free to play games  I can agree on that as well people can describe it in further detail better than I can but I'll bring out the main points on why I like TF2 as a free to play game.
-Its not a basic shoot em up It explains variety with certain classes other than regular shoot em up games where only the weapon differs from the game not the players nor the play style of them. Instead they use a class system which allows you to play classes differently than others for the scout you run fast making you a good hit and run type of strategy while the heavy has a lot of health and is a powerhouse up close. Each class has their weaknesses which is a good thing so I like that.
-The customization is ok obviously you can get better things if you pay BUT that does not effect the playstyle nor does it give an advantage to the other player (Not including weapons cause those are commonly found and accessable to all)
-The updates are also cool but sometimes you need money to participate in some which kinda sucks but sometimes its not al about the money they can release new weapons, hats and even maps that you can get.
OVERALL: this is a great game expecially coming from the free to play section it is worth checking out for yourself and is unique among alot of shooters which makes it even better I highly recommend this game.

Tf2 is an inspirational take on fps in itself. It has a cartoony art style and is full of randomness and hilarity. While some view it as just another game with guns, Tf2 does it differently.
Tf2 includes:
-Unique class structure
-good balance in classes (no one class can be considered the best, each class has its strengths and weaknesses. The devs are also constantly making changes and balancing maps and items)
-good balance in maps and respawn times; maps are also pretty huge with tons of flank routes and side areas
-multiple weapons for each individual class, making tons of different combinations and playstyles
-Its hilarious most of the time from the cosmetics to the ragdolls to the players, etc
-Most of the community is pretty nice (you'll occasionally run into the guy who has to chug painkillers to soothe his raw throat after he screams for 15 minutes)
The worst parts of Tf2:
-Griefers and hackers (If you're on an official Valve server, VAC will ban them but it takes forever for it to actually work so just leave the game instead)
-people don't often kick hackers themselves
-people also ingore votekicks most of the time, making griefing all the more easy
-Your skill is most often perceived by others on what cosmetics you have (you can use this to your advantage in some ways though)
-The game starts a bit slow, you get new weapons based on how much you play in a row, and this sometimes deters people from the game
-Some weapons are better than others, and some are complete garbage
Neutral:
- bugs and glitches galore, however this is part of the experience. Graphical gliches are funny, and gameplay ones usually serve to entertain rather than to annoy. Most bugs get fixed within days however, so no need to worry too much.
-Updates are far and few between but they're usually pretty good when they happen and the devs are very dedicated
I have had a lot of fun with Tf2 over the years. It is my most played game my far, and I don't intend to stop (completely) anytime soon. Make sure to take breaks though, as the game can get boring after a while. But the time it takes you to get bored is usually almost a year's time, so it has that benefit. All in all, Tf2 is a highly addictive, fast paced, and class based shooter that will suck you in and never let you leave.
Get this game, play it for 9 months, take a 3 month break, then repeat. Have fun with your new life that you can never escape from its grasp. You are welcome.

Team Fortress 2 is going to be 10 years old in October so I might as well make a review while I can. This game was very interesting from the start, unlike most FPS games in 2007 it had 9 unique classes with their own weapons, later down the line when we started getting weapons, maps and hats the community was born. People say that the community is the only thing that keeps TF2 alive, while the community is huge and for the most part it does that should take away from the game, the community has done a lot for TF2 and if it wasn't for the community this game would be dead like Team Fortress Classic. In it's lifetime TF2 has gotten a lot of updates, the fandom loves to bash on the Love&War, Tough Break, and Meet(Meat) your(vs) Match updates because Love&War introduced skins to the stock weapons, Tough Break added more skins to the default weapons and Meet your Match had gotten rid of the quick play option and added Casual and Competitive modes. Despite that this a very exhilarating game and it's been Free to Play since 2011 and I can't recommend it enough.

Team Fortress 2 (TF2) is the sequel to the game that put class-based, multiplayer team warfare on the map. TF2 delivers new gametypes, a signature art style powered by Valve’s next generation animation technology, persistent player statistics, and more. Unlike other "class-based" games that offer a variety of combat classes only, Team Fortress 2 packs a wild variety of classes which provide a broad range of tactical abilities and personalities, and lend themselves to a variety of player skills. Play as the flame-throwing Pyro, the room clearing Heavy, or the Spy, a master of disguises. Other classes include: Scout, Sniper, Medic, Engineer, Demoman, or Soldier. In my view this game is a master piece of the FPS genre and easily the best F2P game around. 8 different and very unique classes create a lot of interesting gameplay scenarios and allow the flexibility to play the game according to your particular play style, this is further enhanced with a wide variety of maps and game modes and is still being supported with frequent high quality new content. In terms of visuals, well on a technical side this game may be showing it's age somewhat but due to the game's very distincitve art and visual style it is still absolutely wonderful to look at and in my view  Graphics that are limited on a technical level but are none the less combined with a inspired art design, look better than half of the unispired triple A mediocrity that comes out now a days. Overall absolutely brilliant game, probably my choice for best FPS of all time and as it is Free to Play there is no reason why you should not give this game a try.
5/5 in my view.

Before I start this, I just want to say that I think TF2 itself is the best FPS I've ever played. Sure, the gameplay itself has some kinks, but it's a really fun game. I started this summer when my friend got me into playing it, and it was fun for a while.
But I noticed as time went on and I got better (I'm not saying I'm good, but I wasn't always at the bottom of the scoreboard) that more and more things made me angry. As I got used to playing the game, that people would either be so good at the game that they were impossible to kill, or so bad they would just run at the enemy team by themselves spraying and praying with the Sniper's SMG. As an example, I mainly play Engineer, who can build a sentry turret that eventually becomes powerful enough to take down pretty much any enemy who walks into it in seconds. But, when I built it, someone else would just come and put their sentry down beside mine. This isn't a random occurence, it happens twice per game with mutliple people. Or, on the flip side, you would just have a Sniper on the enemy team with a really rare sniper rifle who gets a headshot every single time he shoots his weapon... Which is also a common thing to happen in public games.
I would look at chat, and I would just see kids with terrible spelling calling someone stupid, or someone spamming their own special bind every time the die. That Sniper I talked about before? Sometimes, he has to type "REKT" in chat everyime he kills someone.
Any attempt to talk or yell at these people is met with either silence or some stupid response similar to "U MAD BRO?" It's as if more than half of the community is just out to make people angry.
To top it of, the past updates for the game have just been senseless nerfs and buffs (One universally hated example is the Phlogistinator, which completley encourages senseless gameplay and was BUFFED, despite the community calling for it's banishment from the game) and what appears to be cash grabs in the form of "Give us money for challenges in the game".
TF2 is a great game, and I still play it often, but at this point, I wouldn't recommend it. Many old players with over 5000 hours have quit, simply because they're tired of this. I hope one day I can come back and edit this review into something positive, but the odds of that is the equivalent of getting into a pub without someone intentionally ruining the game for everyone else.

I would have written a positive review for Team Fortress 2 when it was in its hay day (about 4-5 years ago). Unfortunately, this game is far past its shelf life. I, personally, am completely against the free-to-play business model in videogames, which overall benefits the company more than the player. TF2's shift to free-to-play was not a welcome one in my eyes, and it was too bad I couldn't receive a refund for it. Regardless, TF2 doesn't necessarily punish players for not paying for weapons and cosmetics - but when I see more store content than actual meaningful gameplay changes or additions, I begin to get suspicious... and eventually frustrated.
As TF2 ages and the fanbase further disperses to spending their funds elsewhere, I predict TF2 will continue on this downward slide into more f2p purchases and less actual content. Simply put: its current state is "meh", and it will get progressively worse. I'd recommend not investing in this game.

Достаточно интересный шутер с большим количеством режимов и карт, которые может создать любой игрок.
Необычная мультяшная графика, смешные насмешки, неповторимые праздники, огромное количество косметики, а так же оружия. Игра часто обновляется и внеё всегда добавляют что-то новенькое. Я могу сидеть и играть в эту игру часами.
В этой игре есть 9 неповторимых классов! И каждый из них уникален и особенный для любого игрока. У каждого из них есть своя тактика, свои преимущества и недостатки перед другими классами. Не стоит забывать про командную работу, это самое главное в игре! Игроки-одиночки чаще всего остаются ни с чем.
Ну и конечно же здесь есть свои  минусы:
- большое количество детей на серверах.
- баги/глюки.
- есть тролли, которые будут пытаться подловить вас на этих самых багах и крашить сервера.
- читеры/хакеры.
- игра занимает много памяти.
- частые лаги, для тех у кого медленный интернет.
Не бывает идеальных игр, но, не смотря на это, игра все равно заслуживает того, чтобы зайти в неё и сыграть часок другой.
И соверешенно не важно есть у вас друзья в Steam или нет Вы всегда можете встретить интересную компанию в этой игре.

I have by far never had as much fun with a game as Team Fortress 2. The different classes that you can main and ignore for 90% of the time have different play styles and weapons. The weapons aren't just direct upgrade, direct upgrade, etc, but suit different people's play styles, and have their cons and pros to make them balanced (okay, maybe not so much for the new Phlog, but for the majority their cons balance them out). Okay, there are some SERIOUSLY underpowered weapons that either used to be OP but were nerfed heavily by GabeN to the point where they're useless, or Volvo weren't thinking right when they made the weapon's stats. But besides that, there's not really a best or worst weapon. It just depends on what suits you the most.
Now onto hats, F2Ps, and P2Ps. Let's just say that the Premium/P2P TF2 community likes hats. Annnnnd also likes to torture all the poor wild Gibus F2P families, who just want to protect their little Gibus babies and build their nests [G.E.W.P]. Sorry to all my fellow P2Ps who for some reason hate all F2Ps, they're innocent. Anyways, back onto hats. Ah, yes. Lord GabeN's way to farm money from us. How do I know that? With every major update, Valve adds a whole bunch of new hats to get people to buy them so they receive more and more money. And the real big hats that we premium players like to get are Unusuals. In case you don't know, Unusuals are versions of specific hats in the game that have a certain effect on them, like Scorching. These types of hats are very rare to unbox from crates, and are often very high in price both on the Community Market and in trading. Most decent ones are around $70 and up. However, there is one that is priced ridiculously high that I could mention (cough, Burning Team Captain, cough). Luckily, most aren't as expensive as that. Another way to get an Unusual is by finding an exploit/glitch and sending it to Valve or something. They then allow you to choose from any unusual you like, and any effect, although maybe except for and Unusual Ghastly/Ghostly Gibus. Speaking of the Gibus, players wearing it are often associated with being noobs/newbies. Because of their associating, pro players or fairly decent ones will occasionally wear the Gibus so people underestimate them, resulting in a bunch of kills. Why do all the P2Ps think the Gibus is a noob hat, you ask? Mainly because anyone can get it on their first day from either completing the achievement to dominate another Gibus player legitimately, or just use SAM or go on an achievement items server. Phew, I'm done with this part. Wait, do I have to do more? Fine.
There are a few things you should know about trading. First of all, you need to be a P2P, meaning you bought something from the Mann Co. Store. No, you don't have to buy the $99.99 Something Special for Someone Special. You just need to buy something over 10 cents. Like a cheap weapon. Remember, it has to be from the Mann Co. Store, not the Community Market. Okay, another thing you need to know is the item prices. If you don't, someone could scam you out of an item that they want. One website you can use for price lists is backpack.tf. Another way someone could scam you is by switching the item they're going to give you with something cheaper in price, but looks similar. Also, they could impersonate one of you friends. They say that you're going to need to give said item to your friend at some point. Then later on, they say that you need to trade said item to your friend  and they use the same profile name and picture as your friend. So once you do the trade, THEY receive the items and run of with them. I'm probably missing another way people can scam you, since I rarely trade, but some Youtuber probably said it. Honestly, these people are just messed up and only care about taking other players' items and selling them on the Community Market. They're too scared about losing their items and can't trade legitimately, etc, bla. Oh wait, this thing is turning into more of a guide than a review... Play as the flame-throwing Pyro, the room clearing Heavy, or the Spy, a master of disguises. Other classes include: Scout, Sniper, Medic, Engineer, Demoman, or Soldier. TF2 features the most advanced graphics of any Source-based game released to date – and the most exciting class-based action ever created.

My best TF2 experience was between 2012/2014. I played tf2 all the time then, and I loved the game so much. And why you may ask? Because everyone was playing the actual game. While today if you go on a trade server, they are packed with noobs who don't know how to play the game, tryhards who are always on a rampage, and pros who want to show off their items. Almost every server in the "PLAY MULTIPLAYER" section is empty.
Next problem: Campaign Passes.
Back in 2013 until gun mettle, if you wanted to join a campaign, you just had to pay a dollar for 1 ticket. And that was for MVM (Man Versus Machine). Now, you have to pay 6 Dollars for the entire campaign. And when you finish these easy contracts, you get a weapon skin of a stock weapon, and then you get a crate which you need to spend $2.50 on to open. When you open it, you will most likely get a terrible weapon.
Back To MVM:
MVM was when you got a ticket to play a game and went on a server. You would get upgrades to upgrade your weapons.     When that's done, you press F4 and wait for the round to start. You have to kill the incoming robots to prevent them from deploying a bomb in your base.
Workshop:
So far, VALVe doesn't make that many updates anymore. They let people in the workshop create weapons which are unrelated to the game and it's timeline (1970's). The old workshop items before Gun Mettle were better, because they fit in the timeline and most of them were appropriate for their recommended stats. They were also very original.
Conclusion:
Stay away from the game because it is a pile of♥♥♥♥♥♥ For new people, you're too late. And also because there's only noobs and pros, which means no average player in between, like me. If you want to play a game, play something like Garry's Mod and download tf2 addons and mods from the workshop. They haven't been updated in years, so they'll give you the vintage tf2 background.

This game is so many things for me; but most important to me; is its the most wonderful time waster ever. You might play a few games and not really get anything; or you might play it and see its beauty. Who can say what'll happen when you find yourself on koth_harvest_final for the first time.
Classic Rock and this game have one basic thing in common: after all this time; its still good, and still looked at for inspiration. I mean, look at Overwatch. Its what would happen if you made Tf2 into a moba. Blizzard has original ideas everyone. So does Valve though. See any skinned weapon for more information Valve being orginal.
Now; we get into some gripes. I've played this game for over 900 hours. I've placed more time in this game than any other game period. Valve does not listen to the community that has kept this game going long after its expected life span. Look at the workshop for Tf2. There's so much content they could add at any time; so many hats to profit off of; so many new weapons; maps, and effects, that they're just not adding in. Its just sixteen different ways to change a stock rocket launcher or whatever. That's just wasteful, and an actual shame. They look at all this stuff; and all these ways to change it; and they say "No, we like it how it is." They didn't even do a neat halloween event last year.
C'mon guys. You like money right?

At the end of the day; the only thing that call kill Tf2 is Valve. That's it. Forever. As long as servers exist people will keep right on playing it; trust me. I have by far never had as much fun with a game as Team Fortress 2. The different classes that you can main and ignore for 90% of the time have different play styles and weapons. The weapons aren't just direct upgrade, direct upgrade, etc, but suit different people's play styles, and have their cons and pros to make them balanced (okay, maybe not so much for the new Phlog, but for the majority their cons balance them out). Okay, there are some SERIOUSLY underpowered weapons that either used to be OP but were nerfed heavily by GabeN to the point where they're useless, or Volvo weren't thinking right when they made the weapon's stats. But besides that, there's not really a best or worst weapon. It just depends on what suits you the most.
Now onto hats, F2Ps, and P2Ps. Let's just say that the Premium/P2P TF2 community likes hats. Annnnnd also likes to torture all the poor wild Gibus F2P families, who just want to protect their little Gibus babies and build their nests [G.E.W.P]. Sorry to all my fellow P2Ps who for some reason hate all F2Ps, they're innocent. Anyways, back onto hats. Ah, yes. Lord GabeN's way to farm money from us. How do I know that? With every major update, Valve adds a whole bunch of new hats to get people to buy them so they receive more and more money. And the real big hats that we premium players like to get are Unusuals. In case you don't know, Unusuals are versions of specific hats in the game that have a certain effect on them, like Scorching. These types of hats are very rare to unbox from crates, and are often very high in price both on the Community Market and in trading. Most decent ones are around $70 and up. However, there is one that is priced ridiculously high that I could mention (cough, Burning Team Captain, cough). Luckily, most aren't as expensive as that. Another way to get an Unusual is by finding an exploit/glitch and sending it to Valve or something. They then allow you to choose from any unusual you like, and any effect, although maybe except for and Unusual Ghastly/Ghostly Gibus. Speaking of the Gibus, players wearing it are often associated with being noobs/newbies. Because of their associating, pro players or fairly decent ones will occasionally wear the Gibus so people underestimate them, resulting in a bunch of kills. Why do all the P2Ps think the Gibus is a noob hat, you ask? Mainly because anyone can get it on their first day from either completing the achievement to dominate another Gibus player legitimately, or just use SAM or go on an achievement items server. Phew, I'm done with this part. Wait, do I have to do more? Fine.
There are a few things you should know about trading. First of all, you need to be a P2P, meaning you bought something from the Mann Co. Store. No, you don't have to buy the $99.99 Something Special for Someone Special. You just need to buy something over 10 cents. Like a cheap weapon. Remember, it has to be from the Mann Co. Store, not the Community Market. Okay, another thing you need to know is the item prices. If you don't, someone could scam you out of an item that they want. One website you can use for price lists is backpack.tf. Another way someone could scam you is by switching the item they're going to give you with something cheaper in price, but looks similar. Also, they could impersonate one of you friends. They say that you're going to need to give said item to your friend at some point. Then later on, they say that you need to trade said item to your friend  and they use the same profile name and picture as your friend. So once you do the trade, THEY receive the items and run of with them. I'm probably missing another way people can scam you, since I rarely trade, but some Youtuber probably said it. Honestly, these people are just messed up and only care about taking other players' items and selling them on the Community Market. They're too scared about losing their items and can't trade legitimately, etc, bla. Oh wait, this thing is turning into more of a guide than a review... Umm, I don't exactly want to be typing here for hours and hours, so I'll just say something quick. This game is pretty fun to play with all the different ways, and uh.... I have by far never had as much fun with a game as Team Fortress 2. The different classes that you can main and ignore for 90% of the time have different play styles and weapons. The weapons aren't just direct upgrade, direct upgrade, etc, but suit different people's play styles, and have their cons and pros to make them balanced (okay, maybe not so much for the new Phlog, but for the majority their cons balance them out). Okay, there are some SERIOUSLY underpowered weapons that either used to be OP but were nerfed heavily by GabeN to the point where they're useless, or Volvo weren't thinking right when they made the weapon's stats. But besides that, there's not really a best or worst weapon. It just depends on what suits you the most.
Now onto hats, F2Ps, and P2Ps. Let's just say that the Premium/P2P TF2 community likes hats. Annnnnd also likes to torture all the poor wild Gibus F2P families, who just want to protect their little Gibus babies and build their nests [G.E.W.P]. Sorry to all my fellow P2Ps who for some reason hate all F2Ps, they're innocent. Anyways, back onto hats. Ah, yes. Lord GabeN's way to farm money from us. How do I know that? With every major update, Valve adds a whole bunch of new hats to get people to buy them so they receive more and more money. And the real big hats that we premium players like to get are Unusuals. In case you don't know, Unusuals are versions of specific hats in the game that have a certain effect on them, like Scorching. These types of hats are very rare to unbox from crates, and are often very high in price both on the Community Market and in trading. Most decent ones are around $70 and up. However, there is one that is priced ridiculously high that I could mention (cough, Burning Team Captain, cough). Luckily, most aren't as expensive as that. Another way to get an Unusual is by finding an exploit/glitch and sending it to Valve or something. They then allow you to choose from any unusual you like, and any effect, although maybe except for and Unusual Ghastly/Ghostly Gibus. Speaking of the Gibus, players wearing it are often associated with being noobs/newbies. Because of their associating, pro players or fairly decent ones will occasionally wear the Gibus so people underestimate them, resulting in a bunch of kills. Why do all the P2Ps think the Gibus is a noob hat, you ask? Mainly because anyone can get it on their first day from either completing the achievement to dominate another Gibus player legitimately, or just use SAM or go on an achievement items server. Phew, I'm done with this part. Wait, do I have to do more? Fine.
There are a few things you should know about trading. First of all, you need to be a P2P, meaning you bought something from the Mann Co. Store. No, you don't have to buy the $99.99 Something Special for Someone Special. You just need to buy something over 10 cents. Like a cheap weapon. Remember, it has to be from the Mann Co. Store, not the Community Market. Okay, another thing you need to know is the item prices. If you don't, someone could scam you out of an item that they want. One website you can use for price lists is backpack.tf. Another way someone could scam you is by switching the item they're going to give you with something cheaper in price, but looks similar. Also, they could impersonate one of you friends. They say that you're going to need to give said item to your friend at some point. Then later on, they say that you need to trade said item to your friend  and they use the same profile name and picture as your friend. So once you do the trade, THEY receive the items and run of with them. I'm probably missing another way people can scam you, since I rarely trade, but some Youtuber probably said it. Honestly, these people are just messed up and only care about taking other players' items and selling them on the Community Market. They're too scared about losing their items and can't trade legitimately, etc, bla. Oh wait, this thing is turning into more of a guide than a review... Tf2, where to start? It's a great fast paced FPS that will require a lot of concentration. It has odd but working economy that works by scraping or selling weapons for metal and using metal to buy hats and taunts, or you can just go to the market and purchase most items for cheap. The game itself has "ok" graphics (it's not FarCry 4) and I can't wait for a source 2 graphical update but it still gets away on a good note because of its cartoony style. You can play for free for as long as you want (that's not saying the community won't scrutinize you for it) and later purchase something cheap off the MannCo store to get the full hat/trading experience with a large amount of backpack space. Updates aren't bad but some are pretty lackluster. In-game you have 9 classes to choose from (scout, pyro, engineer, spy, soldier, medic, heavy, demoman, and sniper). You will come to find which class you play best with and you learn to use that class to boost your team to victory. A good team is a mixed team. Overall TF2 is one of my favorite games and will keep playing for years to come I reccomend this to anyone who likes fast paced FPS games.

Longevity is tough for competitive shooters. Hardly a month goes by without new virtual arenas cropping up and enticing you into some fresh conflict, and only a few popular games manage to sustain active player bases even a year after their initial release. And then there's Team Fortress 2. Released in 2007, this class-based classic is still going strong well into its seventh year, thanks largely to its lively and creative community. Since GameSpot's original TF2 review, the game has benefited from numerous updates and made the jump to a free-to-play business model. So how well is Team Fortress 2 faring in 2014 among the current crop of competitors for your time and money?
The short answer is, it's holding up very well. The core action pits two teams of players against each other in a battle to capture points, move a cart, or steal a briefcase. The objective is always very straightforward; it's the interplay between the nine playable classes that makes things so varied and interesting. The speedy scout, the militant heavy, the diligent engineer, the conniving medic, the pesky sniper, the sneaky spy, the feisty pyro, the explosive soldier, and the even-more-explosive demoman all have unique weapons, attributes, and abilities that complement each other and clash in myriad ways. Encounters can vary widely depending on the match type and the makeup of each team, and this unpredictability is crucial to TF2's long-standing appeal.

Note that, I allready made a review of this game. But that was back when I didn't really have that much experiance with this game. So, now that I have more hours than usual piled into this game. I may as well give some really honest thoughts and some basic guidelines for people who want to get this game.
First off, it's entirely different to games like, battlefeild, Call of Duty and other general FPS games. So If your coming from one of those games, (Most likely from COD) your going to have to adjust to the new enviroment of Tf2. I know... that sounds hard, but seriously all you need to do is at least try.
But honestly, if you can get past the differances between all of those games and TF2 you'll find a great game. It's teamwork baised gameplay, the personality to it all...
OH! I should have mentioned that. The classes of Tf2 aren't your ordinary Soldiers and hired guns ooooooh no. Valve made it so that these guys WILL be embeded in your mind to the point that you don't want to forget them. From the Insane personality of the Medic, or cocky and immiture nature of the Scout and of course, the ever so famous Heavy, with his absalotely HALARIOUS dialouge.
Also, something else that makes TF2 Special, is the different weapons. You see the Weapons aren't so much upgrades, more like they are side grades and can change the play style of the current class your playing as.
The only things I can really complain about are pretty much personal stuff. However there IS also one major gripe I have with the game. And that is with one of it's core concepts, THE RANDOM CRIT SYSTEM. The reason I dont like this system is because, I could be kicking♥♥♥♥♥and then all the sudden a Soldier comes along and shoots a crit rocket and wipes me out in one shot.

And the fact that the game drops items such as class weapons, hats, clothes, and more makes in endlessly enjoyable and unexpecting. I myself, have played this game for years, on Xbox 360 (there is no variety as the game has never updated) and even before it was Free to play, and I'm obviously still obsessed. A must have for the esteamed Steam/PC gamer. 100% recommend.

If you find some form of excitement about attacking a French Spy with his own arm while wearing a hat that's on fire, this is probably the game for you.
But seriously, Team Fortress 2 is a unqiue, enjoyable FPS directed towards a wide audience. The game introduces a sense of silliness while also maintaining a healthy dose of competiveness in the game. After playing the game for three years, I have had a good experience with the community. There is a lot of creative items in the workshop that sometimes make it into the game and many forms online that had help players with any problems you encounter.
The graphics are nice to look at and aren't too demanding on your system. The classes (characters) and maps have a nice cartoon-ish, yet detailed, design.
The main cons I can think of is that you might have some preformance issues, depending on your system. There's also the daunting hitreg that can really screw up your shot, and the fact that there is a heavy reliance on other members on your team, which can make or break the round (though that can usually be fixed with good teamwork anyway).
There's also the fact that your wallet will be empty sometimes. Depending on the update. (It's worth it, I swear. Eating is overrated anyway.)
Anyway, I won't ramble on any longer. It's a good game and the pros outweigh the cons pretty easily. Plus I've spent over a thousand hours on this game, and I wouldn't mind doubling that amount in the years to come.

Tf2, where to start? It's a great fast paced FPS that will require a lot of concentration. It has odd but working economy that works by scraping or selling weapons for metal and using metal to buy hats and taunts, or you can just go to the market and purchase most items for cheap. The game itself has "ok" graphics (it's not FarCry 4) and I can't wait for a source 2 graphical update but it still gets away on a good note because of its cartoony style. You can play for free for as long as you want (that's not saying the community won't scrutinize you for it) and later purchase something cheap off the MannCo store to get the full hat/trading experience with a large amount of backpack space. Updates aren't bad but some are pretty lackluster. In-game you have 9 classes to choose from (scout, pyro, engineer, spy, soldier, medic, heavy, demoman, and sniper). You will come to find which class you play best with and you learn to use that class to boost your team to victory. A good team is a mixed team. Overall TF2 is one of my favorite games and will keep playing for years to come I reccomend this to anyone who likes fast paced FPS games.

Summary:
If I had to summarize Tf2 in one sentence, I'd say it's one of the most entertaining, balanced, and relaxing games to play.
Pros:
1. Great community
The Tf2 community is very friendly, and you can always find people to play with and hang out with on servers, from group hosted events to just chilling out with your friends.
2. Balanced classes
The balance between classes is another thing that makes this game the way it is. There is a counter for pretty much any weapon, so it's a battle of skill and prediction.
3. Everlasting entertainment
It's almost impossible to get bored of this game because of the hundreds of weapons and styles to play each class that exist, from trolling engies to tryhard soldiers to spawncamping demos. There's also hundreds of maps and gamemodes to play as well, so the fun never ends.
Cons:
No cons.
Rating:
All in all, hugely recommended for any experienced or new gamers. Try it out, and I guarantee you won't be dissapointed!

The first thought most people have when they hear 'first-person shooter' usually revolves around games like Call of Duty or Halo.  Tea Fortress 2, however, still manages to this day to outshine any of those.  We're talking about a multi-class, team-based shooter with unique, *mostly balanced weapons, awesome maps and gamemodes, fun taunts to tickle the pickle, and hundreds upon hundreds of cosmetic items.  It is virtually impossible to play TF2 without crossing paths with a complete stranger and leaving as friends.  The game manages to be serious and fun at the same time.
It just has a breathtaking personality and identity of its own, and that's all I could have ever asked for.

A game for anyone, young and old, you come together and just have a silly time shooting hilarious characters!
I have been playing TF2 for many years now over several accounts, I have been involved in high stakes trading, competitive scene as a subby and just your every day Vintage Targe collector! Over the years I would have no doubt over 3000 hours in the game, which really speaks a lot for it's quality. How many games can you honestly say you have spent over 200 hours playing and have yet to get bored. (not many).
Since Day 1 of the Orange Box, Valve has done a great job pushing new and exciting updates to keep the userbase happy and wanting more. Rarely has balance been an issue and game breaking exploits are patched within the week. Valve really went the extra mile to preserve Team Fortress 2 as the pinnacle of casual, fun and competitive First Person Shooters for so long (and it isn't slowing yet!).
I first started playing on an old HP laptop which shows how impressively optimized the game is for any system and any player from any household to pick right up. With mods, skins and now, regular missions and operations, TF2 Continues to reel in an audience with it's whacky humour and all around good times.
You can't get a better, more polished multiplayer experience than this. Each time you connect to a server is a whole new bag of gags waiting to be opened. New weapons and maps keep things minty fresh.
TF2? PLOT??
Yes! Sure, at it's heart, Team Fortress 2 is a pure multiplayer shenanigans sh!tup but Valve begun writing back stories and histories for each of our favourite mercs ranging from Themed updates (War! Update, my god!) to full Comic books detailing the (mis)adventures of the 9 chums we have shot/beat/punched and mini-sentried countless times.
Speaking as a guy who has played tf2 in 640x480 on DX6 modes using fps configs right up to using a config to juice up the game I can say at any graphical fidelity you play at, you will have a great visual experience. The game doesn't stray away from it's cartoony artstyle.
- IGN
Like it, love it, loathe it or leave it, Team Fortress has been and will continue to be both the entry level multiplayer shooter and at the ceiling of a PC gamer's library. I don't see things slowing down for quite some time and in all honesty I hope it doesn't.

Overwatch is a team-based multiplayer first-person shooter video game developed and published by Blizzard Entertainment. It was released in May 2016 for Microsoft Windows, PlayStation 4, and Xbox One.
Overwatch puts players into two teams of six, with each player selecting one of several pre-defined hero characters with unique movement, attributes, and abilities; these heroes are divided into four classes: Offense, Defense, Tank and Support. Players on a team work together to secure and defend control points on a map and/or escort a payload across the map in a limited amount of time. Players gain cosmetic rewards that do not affect gameplay, such as character skins and victory poses, as they continue to play in matches. The game was launched with casual play, while Blizzard added competitive ranked play about a month after launch. Additionally, Blizzard has developed and added new characters, maps, and game modes post-release, while stating that all Overwatch updates will remain free, with the only additional cost to players being microtransactions to earn additional cosmetic rewards. badge thing

Team fortress 2 is probably my favorite PC game, the lastability is through the roof and there are thousands of servers and the games still high popularity means it's easy to find low ping games with lots of players.
Not only does it have awesome solid first person shooter game play but all the classes are vibrant, distinct and funny leading to more enjoyable, varied and funny game play. The environments are varied and colorful and there are plenty of game modes to choose from and a huge amount of mods.
Every two or so months a large update is released adding new levels, weapons and other customization so the games keeps getting extended. There is a large amount of weapon and cosmetic variation available but you need to either buy these first or find then steadily while playing the game. The many weapon options do allow you to adjust and optimize your play style but all these weapons are variants not upgrades of the default options, meaning new players aren't overwhelmed by older players who have better weapons.
As with any online game there is the problem of noobs getting smashed by more experienced players, not because of better weapons but better play styles and skill. This can make it hard to get into the game to start with, plus the huge amount of levels, modes and distinct classes to choose from can make the game overhearing to beginners.

I have been playing TF2 for many years now over several accounts, I have been involved in high stakes trading, competitive scene as a subby and just your every day Vintage Targe collector! Over the years I would have no doubt over 3000 hours in the game, which really speaks a lot for it's quality. How many games can you honestly say you have spent over 200 hours playing and have yet to get bored. (not many).
Since Day 1 of the Orange Box, Valve has done a great job pushing new and exciting updates to keep the userbase happy and wanting more. Rarely has balance been an issue and game breaking exploits are patched within the week. Valve really went the extra mile to preserve Team Fortress 2 as the pinnacle of casual, fun and competitive First Person Shooters for so long (and it isn't slowing yet!).
I first started playing on an old HP laptop which shows how impressively optimized the game is for any system and any player from any household to pick right up. With mods, skins and now, regular missions and operations, TF2 Continues to reel in an audience with it's whacky humour and all around good times.
You can't get a better, more polished multiplayer experience than this. Each time you connect to a server is a whole new bag of gags waiting to be opened. New weapons and maps keep things minty fresh.
TF2? PLOT??
Yes! Sure, at it's heart, Team Fortress 2 is a pure multiplayer shenanigans sh!tup but Valve begun writing back stories and histories for each of our favourite mercs ranging from Themed updates (War! Update, my god!) to full Comic books detailing the (mis)adventures of the 9 chums we have shot/beat/punched and mini-sentried countless times.
Speaking as a guy who has played tf2 in 640x480 on DX6 modes using fps configs right up to using a config to juice up the game I can say at any graphical fidelity you play at, you will have a great visual experience. The game doesn't stray away from it's cartoony artstyle.

Overwatch is a team-based multiplayer first-person shooter video game developed and published by Blizzard Entertainment. It was released in May 2016 for Microsoft Windows, PlayStation 4, and Xbox One.
Overwatch puts players into two teams of six, with each player selecting one of several pre-defined hero characters with unique movement, attributes, and abilities; these heroes are divided into four classes: Offense, Defense, Tank and Support. Players on a team work together to secure and defend control points on a map and/or escort a payload across the map in a limited amount of time. Players gain cosmetic rewards that do not affect gameplay, such as character skins and victory poses, as they continue to play in matches. The game was launched with casual play, while Blizzard added competitive ranked play about a month after launch. Team fortress 2 is probably my favorite PC game, the lastability is through the roof and there are thousands of servers and the games still high popularity means it's easy to find low ping games with lots of players.
Not only does it have awesome solid first person shooter game play but all the classes are vibrant, distinct and funny leading to more enjoyable, varied and funny game play. The environments are varied and colorful and there are plenty of game modes to choose from and a huge amount of mods.
Every two or so months a large update is released adding new levels, weapons and other customization so the games keeps getting extended. There is a large amount of weapon and cosmetic variation available but you need to either buy these first or find then steadily while playing the game. The many weapon options do allow you to adjust and optimize your play style but all these weapons are variants not upgrades of the default options, meaning new players aren't overwhelmed by older players who have better weapons.
As with any online game there is the problem of noobs getting smashed by more experienced players, not because of better weapons but better play styles and skill. This can make it hard to get into the game to start with, plus the huge amount of levels, modes and distinct classes to choose from can make the game overhearing to beginners.

TF2 an amazing game for anyone that likes a fun FPS. This game has many promotional and achievement items that are cool! Not only this, if you didnt really like this game you can spend only a couple dollars on mvm tickets and earn botkillers or an australium (gold weapon). This is really cool (and rare) considering that if you spent only 4 dollars you can sell the australium gun for 30 (the least amount of money an australium is sold for) up to around $100. This games community is mostly supportive, and the gameplay itself is an amazing mix between creative sci-fi weapons and a first person shooter realistic game (excpet for the fact that you can't scope unless you're a sniper and can't sprint). Even with those few flaws this game is very fun and packs hours of gameplay with friends and by yourself when your bored of other games. Not only is it multiplayer it has its own version of a zombie mode called MVM (Mann VS Machine) where you and 5 friends or online players go aggainst waves of robotic versions of your classes. With enough missions for hours of free bootcamp and missions for mann up mode (where you can earn the botkillers and australium guns that I mentioned earlier). Overall a pretty damn good game that valve has given to us.

TF2 an amazing game for anyone that likes a fun FPS. This game has many promotional and achievement items that are cool! Not only this, if you didnt really like this game you can spend only a couple dollars on mvm tickets and earn botkillers or an australium (gold weapon). This is really cool (and rare) considering that if you spent only 4 dollars you can sell the australium gun for 30 (the least amount of money an australium is sold for) up to around $100. This games community is mostly supportive, and the gameplay itself is an amazing mix between creative sci-fi weapons and a first person shooter realistic game (excpet for the fact that you can't scope unless you're a sniper and can't sprint). Even with those few flaws this game is very fun and packs hours of gameplay with friends and by yourself when your bored of other games. Team Fortress 2 is the best game I've ever played. Over the last three and a half years I've clocked up 666 hours on Badwater and Dustbowl. I've stabbed, shot, cloaked, crafted, traded and unlocked my way to a backpack full of awesome weapons and hats. Where Team Fortress 2 is now, with its ridiculous weapons, headgear and recipes, is a long way from the lean multiplayer shooter it launched as.
And now it's free. Imagine people on servers freezing at the news: the Red Scout's fish flopping in his hand, the Blu Soldier raising his frying pan, about to crown a Pyro before stopping and looking around. All this? Free? Really?
It's difficult to comprehend. Fortyeight maps, nine classes, most of the weapons: Valve are giving them away for nothing. All you need is a Steam account. With that you have a free account for TF2: you get a 50-slot backpack to hold your stuff, access to all the standard items, and limited crafting (no rare items).
To upgrade to premium (everyone who bought the game is a premium user), with 300 backpack slots and access to all weapons and full trading, all you need to do is buy one item from the microtransaction store. The cost of the cheapest items (such as the Soldier's replacement rocket launcher, the Direct Hit) is 29p. That the dearest item, a pack containing all the weapons and apparel of the most recent update, costs £59, is of no consequen
Even though Valve make money from sales, they've provided a number of ways of getting items for free. You can unlock weapons for every class through achievements. You get weapons given to you through random item drops. If you don't like what they've given you, you can use the crafting system to smelt the weapons into raw material for weapons you do want. Or you can trade. Simply playing the game will give you ample rewards. It's the best example of F2P I can think of. There's no splitting of the community, either: new maps and game modes are always free.

This games diversity and possibilities are endless. With it's many gamesmodes and a server browser, you can find just about anything in this game. This game has a solid matchmaking system, usually "reserved" for newer players. Until competetive is implemented into the game itself, many great players stick to the server browser and UGCLeague, the TF2 competetive scene.
Although this game is Free to Play, it doesn't offer a pay to win feature. And that is saying a lot to something that can offer such amazing mechanics and replayability. There are many base gamemodes that everyone can try in this game, such as Payload, Control Point, and Attack & Defense, which can offer many different play styles and strategies. An amazing pro that will be throwin into the mix of great things with this game is it's customizability. From hats to weird taunts, this game will always grab your attention.
There are a few cons that you have to be wary of. The major cons are Random Critical Hits and Spawn-camping. Random Critical Hits or Random Crits are random bursts of damage which do significant amounts of damage, and based on the skill of your or the enemy team, it could be easy for either to spawncamp. A few minor cons are poor mic quality and not-so-frequent stalemates.

Probably the best Free to Play game that I've ever had. Team Fortress 2 is the main reason why I downloaded Steam in the first place, which has introduced me to many other fantastic PC games (and sales of course!). In case you didn't know, Team Fortress 2 is a class-based multiplayer FPS that was developed by Valve in 2007. There are 9 classes to choose from that all have their own unique weapons, strengths, weaknesses, items and personalities. They can all be customized with different cosmetic items like hats as well as weapons for different playstyles like the rocket jumper which helps the Soldier launch him self up in the air without taking damage. Despite being a multiplayer-only game, the characters in this are much more interesting than most other shooters.
TF2 definetly is not a pay to win game. You can earn all of the weapons without spending money by getting item drops, which are pretty common. Most other cosmetic items you can get from drops but they are much more rare. But I don't have a problem with this as they dont affect gameplay at all. All it takes to unlock other features like trading and more backpack space is to purchase one item from the Mann Co store. This could be less than a dollar. The only thing that I would criticise with the f2p model is that many of the weapons and cosmetic items in the Mann Co store are pretty overpriced.
There are modes in the game like Capture the Flag, King of the Hill, Payload, Attack/Defense and Control Points. In all of these modes, teamwork is essential to winning the objective which is why it is important for your team to balance the classes out so that everyone has their own role. Be sure to check the server browser as it offers many different custom servers with their own interesting game modes and maps.
Despite the game being made in 2007, the visuals have aged pretty well due to the non-realistic cartoony style of the graphics. TF2 also has a very high playbase today due to Valve adding tons of new features overtime. For a while, Valve focused to much on adding hats rather than different weapons but it seems like they are noe deliverng better updates. More modes and maps would be nice though. If you look at the console versions of this game (barely been updated since it was released), you can see how far TF2 has come. As long as the game keeps on being updated to stay fresh, there is no need for a sequel.
This is my most played game on Steam and there is a reason for that. If you don't have it yet, I absoloutley reccomend you get if you have a computer from the last decade or now. It's free so there's no harm in trying it. Without this, I would probably never have Steam. So overall, I give Team Fortress 2 a 10!

I've had... an interesting history of TF2 (as you can tell by my hours), while I did enjoy the game for its gameplay, well written characters and fun maps, and I still have the odd thoughts of playing the game again, it suffers some major issues that drives me away from the game over and over.
While TF2 has a decent community (Well for steam standards cause 90% of all communities are pure cancer) the large majority is dumb.
Why?
Because they complain about Valve's business practices on the game while FUNDING the thing they hate, why do I know they do this? Because I was once part of the large majority, I'll admit there were updates I didn't take part in like the horrid Electric Boogaloo update or the 6th Halloween update (Well I played it, but didn't buy♥♥♥♥♥♥from the store)
But I took part in the Gun Mettle update which killed one of the major reasons I liked TF2 which I'll explain later, but yet I bought that stupid pass to get a coin.
So because of the majority, more updates that lack actual interesting new content are becoming more common, and new free content became less and less common... which kinda comes into my next point.
A lot of TF2's updates have been free to enjoy or free to some extent, like MvM and its updates allowing you to play for free, but pay to win prizes, however as time passed Valve kept adding paywalls to more updates for no reason except to make your wallet dry... here is a prime example and a small history lesson.
The original Halloween event added 2 free hats you could get, one all year round, while the other was obtained during Halloween.
The 2nd Halloween event added 16 hats and 1 Halloween weapon reskin you could get, with all 16 and weapon being free from grabbing gifts and crafting.
The 3rd Halloween event added 35 hats and 2 Halloween weapon reskins, again all of them can be earned for free via drops and crafting!
The 4th Halloween event added 32 hats and 1 Halloween weapon reskin, and again all of them can be earned for free!
The 5th Halloween event and best event in TF2 history added 102 Hats, AND YOU COULD EARN EVERY SINGLE ONE FOR FREE IF YOU WERE LUCKY! I got a massive amount of them in my inventory and even to this day, this was easily the one of the most fun events due to the map itself and grabbing gifts.
Then the 6th Halloween event added 50 new hats... with you only being able to get 6 of them with a gift by logging in, then another gift via achievement, while the rest you have to pay for... really Valve, you offered the entire past events for free THEN HAVE THE BALLS to paywall a majority of the 6th Halloween event? That's disgusting, and it really♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥me off when I played it.
It was like being invited to a Party for free each year, have my fun, and I could grab all the prizes I want as long as I was playing the game and then leave, then all of a sudden when I go the next year, I get banned from getting prizes until I pay up, and not cheaply mind you, TF2’s pricing for items in the shop is more expensive them most indie steam games, regardless of the quality of the item.
This paywall woke me up, at a really good time, as I started to play less of TF2 and didn't want to spend near the amount of money I wanted into the game... right after the 6th event it was the EOTL update... Great SFM, but the update REQUIRED you to pay to play due to the new duck minigame and cosmetics which were locked behind crates.
Then Gun Mettle came which while added "new" maps, the large part of the update was the
update pass where you could earn skins and CRATES YOU HAVE THE PAY TO UNBOX!
After the success of Gun Mettle, Tough Break and Invasion came, each copying the exact same thing as Gun Mettle, adding "NEW" maps, doing some crappy balancing, and forcing passes down our throats to actually take part in the update, then having the balls to shove pay2open crates exclusive to the passes down our throats too.
Now you might be saying "M8, your just a salty cheapo" while I might be a bit, here is the main thing.
Paying was optional, you could take part in the newest update for free in the past, like crafting the newest hat, weapon or playing on the actual new non community map, like with every update from September 2010 up until Screamfortress 2014, you could earn nearly everything for free, today nearly all the NEW content added in a update his hidden behind a paywall, and some are hidden behind 2 paywalls… ♥♥♥♥ off Valve.
I have no problems with TF2 becoming more competitive at all, but here are my main issues...
1. When TF2 was shifting to a more competitive formart starting with the Gun Mettle update, weapons that are "Unfit for competitive" were being reworked or nerfed so they can be used in competitive, and a ton of fun weapons are being killed and wiped of the map because of this! Like the Bison for Soldier and the Shortstop with it's ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ shove.
2. It's killing a lot of the community servers due to Matchmaking replacing the server browser.
3. Competitive is broken with actual competitive matches being a rarity.
4. The game wasn't designed to be competitive in the first place, as a majority of the classes are unfit for competitive use, like the Heavy.
5. "Drop in and Drop out" is gone, it's now "Wait for a game... maybe leave due to unbalanced teams and wait again"
6. Hahahahahahahaha VAC in competitive, now that's a joke.
So those are my main issues, I would list more, but steam won't let me, If you want to know any more reasons why I downvoted TF2, your more then welcome to ask in the comments.
Overall TF2 is a good game, great in fact, and I do miss playing it, but so many things are just holding it back, it's a shell of its former self.
*Just a note, this is my 300th review... god I need a life.*

I know I haven't really played a lot of this game, but the time that I have played was AWESOME! It features 9 people you can play as; each one having its own unique capabilities. Such as the Soldier, you can blow yourself up 75 feet in the air with a ROCKET LAUNCHER and NOT DIE!? HOW AWESOME IS THAT??!!? Also comes with a shotgun and a shovel for melee. The sniper: a great person to play as when at a high, and/or secluded spot; you can shoot enemies quickly to make a good sized dent in their health, or wait for a charged shot that will deal devastating damage. You also have an SMG and a machete for close quarters. The Heavy: a powerful hunk of brawn, your default weapon is a powerful, though inaccurate minigun. His weapons are meant mainly for defensive purposes and can kill an enemy in their tracks when close. You also have a shotgun and powerful fists. The Medic: a lot will depend on you when playing as him. Use your Medi-Gun to heal your teammates and deploy an Uber-Charge on them and greatly increase their damage and make them invincible for a short period of time. Also comes with a Bone Saw and a Syringe Gun. The Scout: this character is very quick and can double jump. He's one of the best people for Capture-The-Flag matches. While he has a relatively low health, he makes up for it all in speed. Comes with a Bat, a Pistol, and a Scatter gun. The Pyro: Use your flamethrower to light enemies on fire, dealing damage for a short time. Also has a Shotgun and Fire-Axe for secondary weapons. The Engineer: build sentry guns to do the dirty work for you (sentries can be upgraded to level 3), build dispensers to supply teammates with health and ammo, and make teleporters to help them quickly get to the battle scene. The Engineer comes with a Shotgun, Pistol, And a Wrench to upgrade stuff and hit bad people with. The Demo-Man uses a Grenade Launcher and Stickybomb Launchers to blow things up. His secondary weapon is a bottle... go figure. The Spy: disguise yourself as the enemy of your choice and stab them with a knife later (this will remove your disguise). You can also turn Invisible for a while by clicking the right mouse button. Also comes with Sappers to dismantle enemy buildings, and a revolver. Well, that's all of them. And there are TONS of other upgrades you can get besides the ones I mentioned. You can just wait for them to appear randomly, or buy them with real money at the Mann. Co. Store. Of all the games I have (though I own few), this tops all. And the best part? It's free! So no complaining you didn't get your money's worth. Like I said, it's a great game. You can play with bots or multiplayer. Or do the "Man VS Machine," where you survive waves of crazed robots trying to kill you (pretty exciting). 69/10 would blow things up again.

The game is a good fps which is both an excellent gateway to first person shooters and a host for competative games. However, you will start off with bad stuff, and all you need to do to get the full experience is to buy ANYTHING from the ingame store with legal tender. ANYTHING. Which means that you can pay 99 cents for an achievement item or tool and still get a premium account! However, if you choose to stay f2p, or if you wear pyrovision goggles or a ghostly gibus, you will get underestimated and discriminated by the p2ps of this game. Please, for your mental health, please buy SOMETHING from the mann co. store so that f2ps and p2ps will understand each other. One of the negative aspects of this game is the fact that many community servers do not have a voting system, which means that if VAC doesn't detect a hacker, and the hacker is playing on a server that doesn't have a vote system, then the hacker is home free and at ease to keep his 15+ headshot killstreak alive. The other thing that I noticed about the community is the players with australium, unusual, etc. weapons tend to look down upon other players for NOT having the items that they have, and so, they act like self-centered asshats, no pun intended. If you spot a hacker, tryhard or p2p troll, please either leave the server, report via F7 or simply votekick if the server has a voting system. Everything else is pretty good, considering that bought weapons are either untradable or expensive, and cosmetics have no effect on gameplay. That is about as balanced as it gets. The classes are balanced, but there has been some abuse from the Phlogistinator recently as of the Tough Break update December 2015-2016. Lots of things need buffs such as the engineer and some weapons need nerf such as the Phlog or the Degreaser. Please use this information to keep this project and community safe, happy and balanced.

That leaves two possibilities:
- The game is really that good.
- I might need rehab.

Fast-paced, distinctive and exciting. A decent, cartoonish, class-based, FPS multiplayer; with an easily approachable gameplay. It might get too repetitive from time to time, but then again, it's free-to-play and constantly updated. It's worth a shot, though I would keep it more casual rather than competitive.

I'm going to keep things "short and sweet". Team Fortress 2 or better known now as TF2 and TF:GO, is an excellent game that is aimed at the casual and competitive side of players. There are tons of game modes for you to join and play (my personal favorite being playoad) and there are even more custom game modes within the community servers (my first server as well as the first 1,000 hours of this game being purely Saxton Hale). The Classes There are 9 different classes for players to choose from ranging from Scout, Solder, Pyro, Demoman, Heavy, Engineer, Medic, Sniper, and Spy. This give the player a chance to mess around with the different classes, a more dynamic playstyle, and synergy beteween the different classes (such as the Heavy working with the Medic). Gameplay Now, onto the game itself and how it differentiates itself from the traditional first person shooter. The guns themselves are very unique in the way that they can be considered "pea shooters" (ugh, I hate this term but it does fit). The guns will do large amounts of damage at close range and it will start to "fall off" at long distances. This means that your gun will become ineffective after a certain range and will often require more than one clip in order to finish off an enemy. So, often times players will have to come in close to the enemy to enage and thats where the skill comes in because players will need to judge the distance of their target and make their shots count in order to finish them off. When first playing, players will start off with the "stock weapons" (default weapons) and will get dropped new weapons over time. The weapons consist of a primary, a secondary, and a melee weapon. These weapons will differ depending on the class and the damage output will be different for each. Onto the Critical Hits or "crits". Critical Hits is basically when a weapon gets a random chance at dealing CRAZY amounts of damage and is aimed for the casual players having a change of killing the skilled players. Cosmetic Items Not only do players have the option of using a vast amount of different weapons, but players can also customize their classes with hats, paint, and outfits as a way of looking unique. Each item can be worth a few cents, to a couple thousand dollars depending on the rarity of the item. I ♥♥♥♥ing love this because I can trade for different items and shoot people in style ;D. Community Servers - Prop Hunt -Saxton Hale (Favorite <3) -The Hidden Mod -Team Fortress 2 Classic -Parkour (incredible) -Zombie Mod -Trade servers -Crit servers -Zero Gravity servers And a bunch of other cool♥♥♥♥♥♥ Seriously, check this stuff out. The Community With three years of experience over my head, I can safely say that the community consists of mostly friendly players. Everyone gets along pretty well, however you do have the people who either, A) Hate on the Free To Play Players, B) Judge people based on their inventory, or C) Are just a total♥♥♥♥♥♥to others. Luckily this rarely happens (at least in my case) and I end up just having fun and making new friends. Lastly, you can change the hud for this game as well as skins for various items, or skins for the game, by installing stuff into your TF2 customs folder. I won't go into much detail on this but its something that makes Team Fortress 2 even more special. FOR THOSE WHO HAVE TROUBLE RUNNING TF2 BECAUSE OF SEVERE FPS DROPS I RECOMMEND YOU GO AND GOOGLE CHRIS' CONFIG. It will make the game look noticebly worse, but will improve FPS a lot (I went from 60fps all the way to 200fps with this thing). This concludes my review. I know I left a bunch of things out, but I will be adding stuff on as I go because the community and Valve will be adding a ton of new things to the game (hopefully an official competitive scene WITHOUT CRITS). I hope this review helps and peace.

I bought this game seven years ago, can you believe that? It's been such a long time. Back then I got incredibly lucky. My local toys store labeled the game wrong and I was able to buy it for only 5 euros. I have to say, even though Team Fortress 2 became free to play in 2011, it was still worth every penny I'd spent on it. It's just good fun, in my opinion. I personally don't like realistic shooters. I don't like shooting people much. But the cartoony style and the absolutely chaotic and silly personality of the game make it unrealistic enough for me to enjoy.
That's also the thing I consider the game's best attributes; the unique style. Taken together with the amazing voice acting, unique characters, huge amount of items and personalization abilities.. this game just has a lot of ways to be enjoyed.
The amount of mods and gamemodes people have created for this game keep it interesting, even after seven years. The normal game already has about six different gamemodes, but the unofficial servers have even more gamemodes to enjoy. Versus Saxton Hale, Deathrun, Tennis etc.. there's always something different to enjoy.
Even after seven years I still come back to this game to enjoy myself.

For half a year Team Fortress 2 was my main and favourite game. Back then I would have said that TF2 is the best game in all time. Those days are looong gone. I used to play this game with a friend. We were laughing our asses off all day and night, we were having the time of our life. One day my friend told me that he is leaving the game, selling any items and hats. I started playing  alone. For some time, it stayed as fun as before. But after a month it had lost it's 'magic'. Something felt different. Don't get me wrong, this may be the best FPS games ever created. It has everything:  somewhat untoxic community, varieties of gamestyles, 9 classes to choose from, tons of weapons, balanced mechanics, wide array of maps... But the game wasn't different. Yet, or the first time I was bored while playing Team Fortress 2. This game was the best before my friend left. Giving the game 'yes'or 'no' was a struggle. At the end I gave it a 'yes' only for the good memories I had. Still, no game had matched the fun of sleepless nights and days spent in this game with my buddy, doing our shenanigans. I sold my items and hats and continued on my path. Believe me, playing Team Fortress 2 with friends is THE BEST and THE FUNNIEST gaming experience you will ever get. I know this review will be lost in the countless others, but for those who read it, I hope it was helpful.

well I guess its time to write a real review for this game.
The game is quite difficult to get into because of the skill ceiling ( the highest imo) . This is the only game you can have 500 hours in and still have no idea what you are talking about. Pubs are alright but the real fun of this game is when you put in the effort to get good at the many high skilled mechanics. For example, Rocket jumping is my favorite you can spend hundreds of hours in a jump server because of the Infinite skill ceiling. Which offers a huge advantage over players who can't very well. Then the game offers an amazing 3rd party comp scene COMPLETELY different from the regular pubs. This is the side of tf2 people don't know unfortunately because it can be the most rewarding with 6v6 game with no ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t mechanics like other games, just straight skill based shooting.
The biggest tip I Can give you is just stick with it and learn the advanced mechanics early and don't waste your time on pubs and trade servers or silly mods because that stuff gets stale real quick and offers no payoff in the end.
If you have a friend that had a bad experience it's just because they didn't understand the game and didn't have this great review. :)

I bought this game seven years ago, can you believe that? It's been such a long time. Back then I got incredibly lucky. My local toys store labeled the game wrong and I was able to buy it for only 5 euros. I have to say, even though Team Fortress 2 became free to play in 2011, it was still worth every penny I'd spent on it. It's just good fun, in my opinion. I personally don't like realistic shooters. I don't like shooting people much. But the cartoony style and the absolutely chaotic and silly personality of the game make it unrealistic enough for me to enjoy.
That's also the thing I consider the game's best attributes; the unique style. Taken together with the amazing voice acting, unique characters, huge amount of items and personalization abilities.. this game just has a lot of ways to be enjoyed.
The amount of mods and gamemodes people have created for this game keep it interesting, even after seven years. The normal game already has about six different gamemodes, but the unofficial servers have even more gamemodes to enjoy. Versus Saxton Hale, Deathrun, Tennis etc.. there's always something different to enjoy.
Even after seven years I still come back to this game to enjoy myself.
9/10

Yet, or the first time I was bored while playing Team Fortress 2. This game was the best before my friend left. Giving the game 'yes'or 'no' was a struggle. At the end I gave it a 'yes' only for the good memories I had. Still, no game had matched the fun of sleepless nights and days spent in this game with my buddy, doing our shenanigans. I sold my items and hats and continued on my path. Believe me, playing Team Fortress 2 with friends is THE BEST and THE FUNNIEST gaming experience you will ever get. I know this review will be lost in the countless others, but for those who read it, I hope it was helpful.

well I guess its time to write a real review for this game.
The game is quite difficult to get into because of the skill ceiling ( the highest imo) . This is the only game you can have 500 hours in and still have no idea what you are talking about. Pubs are alright but the real fun of this game is when you put in the effort to get good at the many high skilled mechanics. For example, Rocket jumping is my favorite you can spend hundreds of hours in a jump server because of the Infinite skill ceiling. Which offers a huge advantage over players who can't very well. Then the game offers an amazing 3rd party comp scene COMPLETELY different from the regular pubs. This is the side of tf2 people don't know unfortunately because it can be the most rewarding with 6v6 game with no ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t mechanics like other games, just straight skill based shooting.
The biggest tip I Can give you is just stick with it and learn the advanced mechanics early and don't waste your time on pubs and trade servers or silly mods because that stuff gets stale real quick and offers no payoff in the end.
If you have a friend that had a bad experience it's just because they didn't understand the game and didn't have this great review. :)

How To Make Meatloaf w/ Relish:
Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F.
Coat a skillet with a 2-count of oil and place over medium heat. Saute the onion, garlic, and bay leaves for a few minutes to create a base flavor. Throw in the red peppers and cook them for a couple of minutes to soften. Now add the tomatoes; adding them at this point lets them hold their shape and prevents them from disintegrating. Stir in the parsley, ketchup, and Worcestershire; season with salt and pepper. Simmer the relish for 5 minutes to pull all the flavors together. Remove it from the heat; you should have about 4 cups of relish.
Place the torn white bread in a bowl and add the milk to just barely cover, swish the bread around in the milk and let it sit while you get the rest of the ingredients for the meat loaf together.
This is where you get your hands dirty! In a large mixing bowl, combine the ground beef and pork with 1 1/2 cups of the tomato relish, the eggs, and thyme; season with salt and pepper. Squeeze the excess milk from the bread and add the soaked bread to the meat mixture. To test, fry a small "hamburger" patty of the meatloaf until cooked; the patty should hold together but still have a soft consistency. Taste the patty for seasoning.
Lightly oil a cookie sheet. Transfer the meat mixture to the center of the cookie sheet and form into a log about 9 inches long and about 4 inches wide. Coat the top of the meatloaf with another 1/2 cup of the tomato relish. Lay the bacon across the top lengthwise.
Bake the meatloaf for 1 to 1 1/2 hours until the bacon is crisp and the meatloaf is firm. Rotate the meat loaf while it's baking every now and then to insure that the bacon browns evenly. Remove the meatloaf from the oven and let it cool a bit before slicing. Serve with the remaining tomato relish on the side. Unbelievably moist!

First, I suggest you BUY the full game if possible.  It has many gamemodes that have so much variety, and once you factor in the helpful "how to" servers for the difficult things like rocket/stickybomb/sentry jumping, becomes far more entertaining than first appears.  The drop system leaves entertainment in seeing what you might get from the system, and trading gives chances to get something from others as well.
Second, I advise any who decide to play on servers to try many different types of servers.  Achievement servers are useful for getting that one last achievement to milestone, and the "uber upgrade" and MvM 10-player servers give even more variety than you might expect to those who would rather not spend extra money on the game if they choose to.
Third, if you decide to join the Team Fortress 2 gamers, I advise you to not worry about being called a newb.  There are friendly players out there that don't mind showing you how to do things better, and those who decide to be mean also teach in their own way how to play by showing how they play it.
In summary, I wholly recommend this game and add that it is more fun than appears.
