3 Years Ago, I first joined Steam. The first ever game I bought was TS:2012. The second one ever was this one. Oh man I've had hours of fun with this game. I think this was the best F2P game you could get. Its so simple too. Now, lets get on to the game itself.
------------------------------------------
Team Fortress 2 is a simple FPS game that can give you hours of fun. You can choose between 9 classes, each with their own distinct and unique personalities. There are many gamemodes to choose from, and there are tons, and tons of community made gamemodes, like Slender Fortress 2 and Prop Hunt. The most fun one in my book is Deathrun. There are tons of maps and even more by the community.
The biggest thing about the game is character customization. You can add taunts, hats, shirts, glasses, pants, and many more. There even is the feature of the Steam Market, where you can buy taunts, hats, shirts, etc. Its also kinda the same with weapons, as you can go to the internet and download skins for the weapons, if you dont like how it currently looks ingame.
Overall, Team Fortress 2 is another great Valve game using the Source engine. It gives hours of fun, with support and updates once a month. If you are sick of Call of Duty, Battlefield, or Medal of Honor, come play this cheesy, hilarious, addicting game that will keep you playing 24/7.

Before I begin I want to say I had over 3000 hours on this game legit on my other account that was hijacked.

I recommend it to any people who are new to pc gaming or just want to have a fun time in general. On youtube there are many tutorials, featuring many aspects on how the game works, plays out, and the "econonmy" inside Team Fortress 2. Even though the community can be sometimes annoying and ignorant, you can easily find people to play and have genuine fun with. Just get it, its f2p you dont need to buy anything, although if you do you will gain a premium "pass" allowing you to get better and more items in the game.

I first experienced TF2 on PS3's orange box and it was the game my brother and I played the most.  I'm still fairly new to the PC version since I've only recently gotten a computer powerful enough to run it, and I can say with certainty that it does take some getting used to.  I'm probably among a small minority that prefers the vanilla TF2 experience with the basic weapon loadout since the commentary would suggest that they already put a lot of thought in balancing the character's original loadout.  However, The game can still be enjoyed despite occasionally being killed by some random never-before-seen weapon but I have some faith that the new weapons and abilities still have their own pros and cons. I mostly play with basic weapon loadouts but will experiment once in a while with new weapons, even though I inevitably resort to the ones I'm most familiar with.
Hands down my favorite thing about the game is the unique character classes and the cold-war esque settings.  Visually the game is beautiful (and gory) but there's something about that Norman Rockwell art style that sets this game apart from other shooters.  The classes are balanced well for the most part and depending on the battlefield layout, there is always a tactical choice to best approach a situation using another character if need be.  Scout is my favorite class but it's fun to experiment with other characters when the need arises.
As a n00b to most online FPS games, there are plenty of foul-mouthed opponents and even teammates who hold nothing back if you happen to perform poorly in a match, so expect to be victim to many a slur from veterans.  Apart from the sometimes negative player interactions, most of the time it's all in good fun.  I honestly am not into it for the hats, cards, new weapons etc, and I would be perfectly content if the only map available was CTF 2fort, but there is TONS of variety to folks who have the time and interest in such things.

Wow Team Fortress Two.
I just want to start by saying this is by far the best free to play game you can possibly get, despite its annoying developers and negeltful developers. I know this is a 9 year old game, but it holds up so well due to an extremely active community and very well balanced and designed core gameplay.
{If you dont give a♥♥♥♥♥♥about the community, skip the next two paragraphs}
At this point, the community basically makes updates for the game, but the people in this community are the most talented and hard working people ever. They make maps weapons and even cosmetics. Its impressive how valve allows the players to make the game however they want with some guidelines of course.
The devs only really pay attention when people scream and cry but that's fine, considering how busy valve is at every single waking moment. Despite what most people say, this community is actually full of great people and wonderful content creators, once you brush away the crappy eltist scum that covers the surface.
Okay now for the gameplay.
Despite the 500 hours ive put in this game, i am still terrible, but i have made an immense amount of progress from when ive started. This game's skill ceiling is so high, that is goes out into the stratosphere and then some. There is so much depth to just the basic mechanics like rocket jumping, having game sense, flanking, knowing when to pop uber, when to overextend (almost never) and when to wander on your own. I have never even touched the competitve scene, and can say without any doubt that this game is so deep even at a casual level. There is an enormous amount of content this game has to offer and i dont think i will ever stop playing this until my hours hit the thousands. Its one of the only games i play when i have a free moment. This game is so huge, that you dont even have to play the normal game modes to get hundreds of hours of entertainment out of them. Since the community is so hardworking, there are many different game modes that valve never made and even single player maps to play by yourself.
There is literally no reason to not at least try this game considering how addictive it is, and how much you can do in it. Also, advice for new players, do all of the tutorials please. Look up a guide or two so you dont look like a bumbling idiot like i was. Every single person, even the dude with hats coming out of his♥♥♥♥♥ has started the game at the lowest level so dont worry about it!
tl;dr This is a very good point and shooty team game that is deeper than ur mum's fat rolls and has a community more active than the bacteria living on your body right now.

Not too sure what to write here so heres a recipe for Pancakes instead
Ingredients:
1 1/2 cups all-purpose flour
3 tablespoons sugar
1 tablespoon baking powder
1/4 teaspoon salt
1/8 teaspoon freshly ground nutmeg
2 large eggs, at room temperature
1 1/4 cups milk, at room temperature
1/2 teaspoon pure vanilla extract
3 tablespoons unsalted butter, plus more as needed
Now to make it
1. In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, sugar, baking powder, salt, and nutmeg.
2. In another bowl, beat the eggs and then whisk in the milk and vanilla.
3. Melt the butter in a large cast iron skillet or griddle over medium heat.
4. Whisk the butter into the milk mixture. Add the wet ingredients to the flour mixture, and whisk until a thick batter is just formed
5. Keeping the skillet at medium heat, ladle about 1/4 cup of the batter onto the skillet, to make a pancake. Make 1 or 2 more pancakes, taking care to keep them evenly spaced apart. Cook, until bubbles break the surface of the pancakes, and the undersides are golden brown, about 2 minutes. Flip with a spatula and cook about 1 minute more on the second side. Serve immediately or transfer to a platter and cover loosely with foil to keep warm. Repeat with the remaining batter, adding more butter to the skillet as needed.
6. Procedure for adding fruit to pancakes: Once the bubbles break the surface of the pancakes, scatter the surface with sliced or diced fruit, or chocolate chips, nuts, etc. Flip with a spatula and cook for 1 minute more, being careful not to burn toppings.

At this point, the community basically makes updates for the game, but the people in this community are the most talented and hard working people ever. They make maps weapons and even cosmetics. Its impressive how valve allows the players to make the game however they want with some guidelines of course.
The devs only really pay attention when people scream and cry but that's fine, considering how busy valve is at every single waking moment. Despite what most people say, this community is actually full of great people and wonderful content creators, once you brush away the crappy eltist scum that covers the surface.
Okay now for the gameplay.
Despite the 500 hours ive put in this game, i am still terrible, but i have made an immense amount of progress from when ive started. This game's skill ceiling is so high, that is goes out into the stratosphere and then some. There is so much depth to just the basic mechanics like rocket jumping, having game sense, flanking, knowing when to pop uber, when to overextend (almost never) and when to wander on your own. I have never even touched the competitve scene, and can say without any doubt that this game is so deep even at a casual level. There is an enormous amount of content this game has to offer and i dont think i will ever stop playing this until my hours hit the thousands. Its one of the only games i play when i have a free moment. This game is so huge, that you dont even have to play the normal game modes to get hundreds of hours of entertainment out of them. Since the community is so hardworking, there are many different game modes that valve never made and even single player maps to play by yourself.
There is literally no reason to not at least try this game considering how addictive it is, and how much you can do in it. Also, advice for new players, do all of the tutorials please. Look up a guide or two so you dont look like a bumbling idiot like i was. Every single person, even the dude with hats coming out of his♥♥♥♥♥ has started the game at the lowest level so dont worry about it!
tl;dr This is a very good point and shooty team game that is deeper than ur mum's fat rolls and has a community more active than the bacteria living on your body right now.

Here I am, sliding face-first into the abyss that only Gaben himself knows.

So.
Team Fortress 2.
For those of you who are looking for a long and meaningful review, you'll be half disappointed. This will not be long, but I hope It will be meaningful to you who are reading this.
Basically, this is another First Person Shooter (FPS for those newbies) that actually encourages teamwork and strategy through nine classes. You also have 3 weapons, a primary (your signature weapon) and secondary (usually pistol or fancy gadget) and a melee weapon (SHOVELS WOOOOO).
This game has an interesting gameplay, as there are 9 classes.
The Scout, mobile yet weak, primary as a shotgun.
The Soldier, an all-round class, with a splash dmg but slow Rocket Launcher.
The Pyro, with the flamethrower
The Heavy with a minigun, tanky but very slow
The Demoman, with a grenade launcher that fires bouncy bombs and a sticky bomb launcher
The Sniper. Nothing much else to say.
The MEDIC. One of the most important, has a gun for healing.
The Engineer. builds cool stuff like a sentry gun and dispenser for health and ammo.
The Spy, that can cloak, 1-hit stab people, and destroy what the engineer builds (Before you decide this guy is pretty hard to play in PvP but i daresay i'm decent).
There are many gameplay modes that are self explanatory.
OH AND PEOPLE THERE ARE NO EXTRA DMG FOR HEADSHOTS UNLESS YOU'RE A SNIPER.
SO- pros.
1. THERE IS NO PAY TO WIN. Every hour or so you can find a weapon ( for people that buy something) or you can get different weapons in achievements. I love that these weapons are BALANCED and you can find a unique combination that fits for you. If you're not a p2p, good for you- the community for some reason hates you guys (and i understand why) but you don't need a good weapon to REKK DEM SCRUBS. You can scrap weapons to make metal which you can combine with other weapons to make "better (not really)" weapons. The only things that you might want to pay for are hats, which are expensive to craft.
2. IT ENCOURAGES TEAMWORK. I cannot say this enough. If you want to win, you have to coordinate with the team. This can get you some good online friends, however this is not easy- i'll explain later why.
3. EASY GAMEPLAY AND MECHANICS. It's really simple, and once you understand you can play very well. Remember- a gun is a tool- you're the one who uses it, and that's what matters.
4. RARELY MANY HACKERS. It's not often you find a hacker, but you'll notice them when you find one. just report them (if you have good morals and they're on your team) or leave the server.
CONS.
1. COMMUNITY IS CANCER. if you join a community server (or just any server) you will find rude and stubborn players EVERYWHERE (see Pro #2). There is a mechanic called "sprays" where you can spray paint a decal- any picture that you want to upload. YOU KNOW WHAT THAT MEANS. Keep this away from immature audiences. While you rarely find sexual sprays, it's REAL BAD if you do. Also, lots of swearwords for you squeamish people.
2. OH WAIT I LIED.
This, i guess, was a relatively long review. Remember that youtube movies or any website with a link or survey attatched to it is probably a guy who wants to rob you. Keep this away from young people. When playing, keep a cool demeanor at all times.
TL:DR
Easy to play, not pay2win, but VERY bad for young people.

I started to play this game at September 2011 an will try to make a short review.
Classes:
They are 9 classes to choose and every class has differents skills. Example there is a heavy with 300 life, slow but strong, he carrys a minigun, shotgun and his fists. The opposit would be the scout, he is very fast but only has 125 life and carry only a shotgun, pistol and a bat. They are also a Soldier, Pyro Demoman, Engineer, Sniper, Medic and Spy.
Wepons/Cosmetic
All wepons are balanced. No op classes exist like wepons. But they are more wepons then the standards, every wepon has itself cons and pros. There is a wepon called like pain train, you can capture objetiv faster BUT you lose resitence against bullets. You also dont have to buy them in the store, you can find wepons randomly. Every week you might find 8 - 12 items, You can find hats who change your look, wepons to change them and crates. You can open crates with a key, the key can bought in the shop or being traded by the Community. You can find strange wepons there, who counts your kills or Unusual hats who has different effects.
Gameplay:
They are 2 Teams called BLU (Builders League United) and RED (Reliable Excation Demolition) who fights always against them. They exist tons of maps by the community and by valve. They are still updates to hold the game alive. You can join Valve server where are most new players or find a server by the Community where you mostly find very good players.
Mods:
They are currently many mods from valve and from the community.
Payload: You have to push the bomb to the Fin to win.
Capture the point: They are 5 points you have to capture them all to win.
King of the hill: The team who holds the point is going to win the game.
Capture the flag: You have to capture the other "intellegent"
Attack/Defense: Its like Capture the Point but blue can only capture and red can only defense
Hale: 1 Player is a very strong character and must kill all other players on the server to win (no respawns)
Deathrun: 1 actived traps and the other players have to go to the end to win (no respawns)
and more...
Comic:
This game can give you alot feeling about it. If you are really interested in the game/history, you really should read the comics. They have humor and cost nothing. It also give you alot knowledge about the game. You may find tons of Easteregg in it. Vavle really put few things in it and you might guess the next update :-)
My Point
Its free, the community is fine, they are tons of mods, still get updated, a real free to play,... You really have to try it atleast they game.

Team Fortress 2 is a multiplayer team based first-person shooter, released on Octomber 10 2007 in the Orange Box bundle by Valve Corporation. It's a sequel to Team Fortress Classic, released in 1999. In this game, you have 9 classes/characters with different abilities and utilities, advantages and disadvantages, making the game and the balancing like a rock-paper-scrissors game. The 9 classes are sepparated in 3 categories: Offense: Scout, Soldier and Pyro; Defense: Demoman, Heavy and Engineer; Support: Medic, Sniper, and Spy.
The game has many gamemodes such as Capture The Flag, Payload, Control Points, King Of The Hill and such, with over 100 different official maps. The game consists in 2 teams: RED and BLU, every player has the color of their respective team. A team can have up to 12 players, making a full server have 24 players. The game beeing Free To Play, you can play it any time, as much as you want. When you start the game as a F2P player, you will have some limitations. Once you pay for litteraly anything you want, no matter the price from Mann Co. Store, you will have a Premium account and the limitations are off. Team Fortress 2 regulary updates and every once in a while, the game gets a big update, with new content and rebalancing weapons. Every class is customisable, you can change the weapons, which you can drastically change the course of the game. Every class can have a set of cosmetics, you can personalise every character as you want, for exemple, you can make The Demoman into a knight, you can make The Medic a stereotipical crazy evil doctor and soo much more. TF2 has one of the best, if not the best, community on Steam. People are making content as new weapons, maps, cosmetics in Workshop and they can be added to the game, keeping the game alive and relevant. Team Fortress 2 makes 10 years this Octomber and the player base is more stabile than most of the new F2P games.
Overall, Team Fortress 2 is a huge game in terms of content. It's a fun and casual game, the competitive side is also avalible. I absolutely love this game and I absolutely recomand you to try it and play it. It will take you a while to learn the basics, but once you got the game's idea, you will love TF2.

Having played Team Fortress 2 for years spanning pre-vintage items and stranges to now, this game has been a wonderful experience. Although seemingly repetitive from a fresh point of view, the game itself and the mechanics changes every so often (with updates). While this might annoy people at times, this forces players to change and adapt new strategies, loadouts and more each time thus creating a dynamic and rich experience.
The game play of Team Fortress 2 is also unlike other games. Whereas in some games, certain classes could overcome many other classes; Team Fortress 2 has sought to balance the prowess of each class. For example, Spys are prone to Pyros. Pyros are easy targets for soldiers. Soldiers are often sniped by a sniper and Spys often backstab snipers. No class is ever overall "the best" which is why players have to train themselves to be used to a certain class and have different playing styles for each class. It takes time to find the right class for a person and to master the game means having to spend time with each class to work out your own personal playing style. Something other games don't often give.
Different game modes and maps also spice things up for players. Modes such as control point forces players to be vigilent while Payload maps require teams to work together to push (or pushback) a cart to certain checkpoints to win. The maps themselves has been created in order for teams to have balance. This means that maps often have different routes to certain objective points and must be used accordingly in order to keep a hold or attack the opponent through these routes. For example, at the start of the map, wide open spaces and side-road routes allows the attacking team to get a foothold to push the cart. Meanthile towards the end of each Payload map, there are usually sections that are covered where engineers can place sentries that shoot anyone who gets close to the end goal of the cart. The way maps are made often forces teams to use a different strategy in the early game and late game.
Team Fortress 2 also has a busy trading environment where in game weapons can be turned into Scrap metal and this Scrap can be used as currency to purchase or trade for other goods. The Team Fortress 2 trading market spans from simple basic weapons to ludicrisly expensive hats, stranges and keys; all of which has an actual price in real world currency (when converting things to the values of Keys). If a player were savvy enough to play the trading game; it is possible to start off with nothing and end up with an inventory worth hundreds ( or thousands ) of $$$ in hats. The community which powers the trading scene sets the prices of items accordingly. Unfortunately the market is also prone to real-world economics such as supply and demand as well as inflation. When I started playing Team Fortress 2, keys were worth 3.33Ref. Now it's almost 18Ref. Pretty crazy but with the amount of Refined (Ref) metal floating in the market, it's value would eventually plummit; bringing the price of everything up.
Bringing everything together, Team Fortess 2 is a sublime game with a wonderful community. Game mechanics are unlilke any other and you could be sure that each time you would log in, your experience would be different from the last. The lack of popularity compared with other "shooter" games such as CS:Go is quite unfortunate as players in Team Fortress 2 can get extremely competitive at times and the game does have small glitches here and there. Nevertheless, the game is a gem in a batch of repetitive shooter games and it's something that people should give a go. I have had a blast playing this game and it has been amazing to experience each changes that the game has made throughout the years. I hope you'll also have a great time when you give it a try!

I got this game in March of 2015. In December of 2015, I have logged in over a thousand hours. Not all of them were me actively playing, since I tend to keep it running in the background of my computer. My gosh, this game is fun. The weapons, the characters, the maps, the cosmetics- This game is the reason I got Steam in the first place. My best friend Cyros had already been playing for a few months and coerced me to get it. I don't regret it at all. The only major problem with this game really has nothing to do with the game itself, but rather it's community. TF2 has a large, versaitle community, with all sorts of different types of players. Unfortunately, the ones you come across most often in public servers tend to be rude, both to their team and to the enemy. I'm talking about those guys that make lewd jokes, racist comments, and are basically just a one big void of unintelligent, crude jokes.
Other than them, this game is fun. At least it's free to download, so you can just go ahead and give it a try. If you like it, yay! If not, that's completely fine!

The game is constantly updated with new and fun things to do, i've noticed that most of the weapons in the game requre careful use of ammo and are not able to be sprayed, this keeps the game fresh, the battlefield isn't a mess of bullets, each class has weaknesses and strenghs to other classes and that helps reenforce the team aspect of the game, the teams that win are the teams that can be diverse and effective.
The only things i dislike in TF2 is that i find it difficult to stick to a class and focus on it due to each classes various weaknesses, but that might be just me.
The one major gripe i have however is that weapons and cosmetics are rediculousy overpriced, something that has no effect on gameplay should NOT in any game cost 10 freaking dollars, i guess in game purchases are expected from a free game, but holy crap 10 dollars? in my case i had to hunt for cheap cosmetics on the marketplace and resort to getting strange weapons from the market, as they tend to be MUCH cheaper. The strange weapons seem to be flat out better too since they count kills and various other statistics, so it confuses me how they are cheaper then non-strange weapons.
Other than that, TF2 is extremely fun, deep and enjoyable, if you dont want to pay for weapons, they drop randomly in game, however the better items drop more commonly if you have purchased something from the store first. The game is free to start, so if you have 15 gigabytes of storage on your computer (hopefully) i Highly recommend this game as a must have.

Other than them, this game is fun. At least it's free to download, so you can just go ahead and give it a try. If you like it, yay! If not, that's completely fine!

You've heard a lot of noise about this game - people who love it, people who loathe it. People who thought it died five years ago, and are confused about why they haven't received invitations to the wake. Here's some news for those of you who've been hiding under rocks for five years - Team Fortress 2 is still played, it's still great, and it's still totally free!
I don't think Team Fortress 2 is the best game ever made - but it's got just the right combination of awesome monetisation model, flexible gameplay and moddability that you could arguably play TF2, more TF2 and nothing but TF2, and never actually run out of things to do. Furthermore, the game can run on a toaster or a beast, and get the best out of both.
It would be disingenuous of me to pretend the game's got nothing wrong with it. The game balance tends to shift a fair bit after every major update - usually to the chagrin of a large number of very, very, very noisy teenagers. Why are they so very, very, very noisy? Probably because they care about the game that much.
And you should too. >:)

Good for beginners and veterans. It's a free to play first-person shooter with 9 unique classes: Scout, Soldier, Pyro, Engineer, Demoman, Heavy, Medic, Sniper, and Spy. Because of how different the playstyles are, winning requires teamwork and cooperation between all players.
Newer players can jump into the game with the most balanced weapons [stock] and go onto a public server, or learn the control with training and practice against bots. However, players who have played the game for a while will have collected new weapons which change the game and how each class is used.
Even though it is free to play, there is a pay wall. Free to play players can only hold up to 50 items in their packback as well as not being able to have cosmetics other than the achievment items. It's worth mentioning that there are more than 50 weapons in the game, so if you want the full experience of the game, it is best to become a pay to play player.
As a pay to play user you can now get all cosmetics and tools and you have a backpack with 300 slots that can be expanded with backpack expanders, (expanders add 100 extra slots). All you have to do to become pay to play is spend $0.50 in the in-game "Mann Co." store.
So if you want to play casually and don't think you will keep playing this for a while, you can have fun as a F2P. But if you want to keep playing for a couple years and want to get the best experience you can pay as little as $0.50 to become P2P.
All-in-all, it's a fun and unique game.
Edit: Casual has since replaced quickplay. Casual matches you into a game as opposed to joining a game-in-progress. (Although, you still have the potential to be matched into a game-in-progress.)
Despite what others may say, casual is very similar to quickplay, so I'm not going to change my review, as the game hasn't changed all that much.
The only difference is that match queues can sometimes take a while if you're searching for a mode or map that is unpopular, as it requires a certain amount of players to start a match.
It's still a fun game. And even though the way matches are made has changed, the gameplay has not, and it's gameplay is still great.
Edit II: I nominated this game for the test of time award. Let's be real here, the game is over 9 years old and has kept the same core throughout its entirety. A core that remains great today. While I may have only played the game for about 1.5 years, that's a good amount of time to say that I'm still having a great time, just as I did when I first started playing the game.
It's a great game with a great core, and I hope it wins.

Longevity is tough for competitive shooters. Hardly a month goes by without new virtual arenas cropping up and enticing you into some fresh conflict, and only a few popular games manage to sustain active player bases even a year after their initial release. And then there's Team Fortress 2. Released in 2007, this class-based classic is still going strong well into its seventh year, thanks largely to its lively and creative community.
The core action pits two teams of players against each other in a battle to capture points, move a cart, or steal a briefcase. The objective is always very straightforward; it's the interplay between the nine playable classes that makes things so varied and interesting. The speedy scout, the militant heavy, the diligent engineer, the conniving medic, the pesky sniper, the sneaky spy, the feisty pyro, the explosive soldier, and the even-more-explosive demoman all have unique weapons, attributes, and abilities that complement each other and clash in myriad ways. Encounters can vary widely depending on the match type and the makeup of each team, and this unpredictability is crucial to TF2's long-standing appeal.
When you come out of the gate as a heavy with a medic in tow, you're a formidable offensive force, but if a spy loops around to backstab the medic and you round the corner on a pyro, it can all come undone in a matter of seconds. Snipers can cover expected enemy paths, but rocket-jumping soldiers have a knack for finding alternative routes and raining explosive death from above. You may think you have a comparatively weak scout dead to rights, only to be stunned by a baseball and beaten to death. As you watch your giblets splatter on the ground and see a freeze-frame of your gleeful killer, it's hard not to chuckle at the sheer variety of ways you can meet an untimely demise. And the humorous quips, ridiculous outfits, and histrionic announcer help cultivate this lighthearted tone.
Of course, this core dynamic has persisted for most of TF2's life span, so if you stopped playing it a few years ago and come back for a few matches, you'll find things are very familiar. Learning the ropes and getting the hang of your chosen role is still a gratifying experience, and mastering advanced techniques doesn't just make you deadlier; it gives you more options for how to approach combat. Keeping your options open is still valuable too, because being flexible with your choice of character can help you avoid ending up on a catastrophically imbalanced squad. It is Team Fortress, after all.
But though there is much that has remained constant about the core game, there have been some notable changes over the years, as well as regular infusions of new weapons and items. Of the hundreds of things available in the online store, some can be unlocked through play, while others must be purchased with actual money. From small doodads that cost less than a dollar to massive bundles that cost hundreds, there's a wide range of ways to customize your experience.
Many of the items offer nothing more than a playful twist on the game's already cheeky cartoon aesthetic. You can buy hats, shirts, shoes, and other cosmetic gear to dress up like a character from Adult Swim or don spooky seasonal garb that you can wear only during Halloween or a full moon. Even if you don't fancy shelling out for any of this stuff, it's fun to see some visual variety as you try to light your opponents on fire.
Other weapons have more of an impact, like the ones that give your character a new chargeable and expendable power. The scout can build hype, which turns his usual double jump into a triple, quadruple, or quintuple jump, and the soldier can build rage, which allows him to rally his nearby teammates to do extra damage. Skills like these have more of a meaningful impact on the action, bringing something new to the table that your enemies must contend with. And then there are the totally out-there loadouts, like the one that turns the grenade-launching demoman into an extra from the movie Braveheart.In addition to the cosmetic options, there are a lot of weapons and items that offer small buffs or subtle tweaks to your attributes. Depending on which healing gun the medic equips, for example, he can imbue himself and his targeted ally with extra damage resistance or enable himself to match the speed of his target. Differences like these don't do much to change the core action, but they do give experienced players substantial room for strategic variation.
These options broaden the field of viable strategies, which helps keep combat lively and varied. And fortunately, none of the purchasable weapons or items tip the scales unfairly towards those willing to pay. Buffs and bonuses usually come with caveats, and the weapons that bestow new abilities are usually unlocked for free. For this review, I spent some money on goofy hats and some of the stranger weaponry on offer, like the pyro's flamethrower that actually shoots bubbles and rainbows. It was fun to play with the new gear, but I still found myself switching my loadout between free and paid weapons regularly to adapt to the match situation.
The biggest divergence from the game's origins comes in the cooperative mode, Mann vs. Machine. In it, you and a few other human players must prevent hordes of robotic incarnations of TF2's classes from delivering a bomb to your base. The money you earn from destroying robots can be spent on mid-match upgrades to your attributes and weaponry, which can be crucial to success. Even on the easiest level, the robot legions are fierce enough to test the mettle of an unorganized team. This is a mode where carefully planned weapon choices and defensive strategies can mean the difference between succeeding and having to try, try again. You can play this mode for free, but you won't be eligible to earn rare prizes or complete challenges unless you pay a dollar for a Tour of Duty ticket. Though it lacks the frenetic unpredictability of competitive play, the cooperative mode can still provide satisfaction for those dedicated enough to see it through.
But competition is the real draw, and the Team Fortress 2 community can certainly be competitive. On some servers, you might be berated for unwitting breaches of etiquette, while on others, you might be welcomed with helpful tips and ubercharges. You can even ask for help on certain servers and be paired up with another player who is willing to give you some tips through chat. The community around TF2 is an intriguing one, not just for their deep knowledge of and passion for the game, but for their creative efforts in designing new weapons, items, and maps that have since become part of the experience. It feels like a community of curators, without whom the game may well have dwindled away and passed into obsolescence years ago.
Staying relevant even a year after release is rare for a competitive shooter, and yet, here's Team Fortress 2, still lively after seven years in the business. At times it feels like the same game you could have played back then, and at other times it feels like no one will ever quite nail class-based shooter competition the way TF2 does. The experience has evolved over the years without compromising what made it so great in the first place, so though your free-to-play options may have increased considerably in the past few years, there are few that do it as well as Team Fortress 2.

It was the last minute before the round ended, The last control point needed to be defended by the RED team and stop the BLU team from capturing it. Sentry guns were beeping and shooting rockets, soldiers were liquefying the ground with blown up body parts, and mercenaries were running all over the place with low health calling for the medic. Conga conga conga! Everyone froze. Why was there music playing in the middle of a war? As the mercenaries turned their heads to face the source of the happiness, a delighted look struck the players. They saw a dancing group of people from RED and BLU laughing and singing. Both teams suddenly dropped their weapons and started Congaing. Engineers sat together and drank beer while the other people high-fived or started bashing their heads together for the fun of it. Welcome to Team Fortress Two, a game that you can do whatever you want, whenever you want. The fight can change into a party in the blink of an eye. TF2 (for short) is a massively multiplayer game with over 10 different game modes. It has great graphics and sounds that keep you sitting in your seat to keep playing. The unique part of TF2 is that it's also a hat simulator, where players care about their cosmetics as much as their skill.
In Team Fortress 2, it's all about teamwork. The nine classes you can play offers a diverse environment to fight with strategy and skill. Where will you find a game with a maniac trapped in a fire suit with inhuman thoughts of fantasy land filled with enemies he burned. An American Patriot who carries a rocket launcher to blow people apart and created his own army because he was denied to fight with the army in WWII. A Russian warrior who spins up his minigun and eats sandwiches all day. A drunk Scottish cyclops who drinks on the job, blowing up everything he sees. A Bostonian runner with his high ego and a shotgun to run and gun. A Texas engineer that relies on his sentry to kill everyone in it's path. A sneaky Frenchman spy to disguise as an enemy and backstab them for their trust in him. An Australian assassin that sits to headshot all day and throws pee at people. And finally, a crazy scientist who invents his own medicine to heal his teammates. When all these nine classes work together, they create the ideal team that will win.
The game modes determine the fun. It gives each unique classes another part of how to play. For example, the scout which runs the fastest of all the classes is naturally aggressive. In different game modes like attack and defend, where BLU team captures points and RED defends them until the time limit, the scout on RED team has to play defensively to protect the control point. If players want to take it to the next step, they can join competitive teams instead of Pubs (regular valve servers). There are many kinds of competitive formats from 2v2 to 9v9. Not only the gameplay is important, much of TF2 is about trading. Many players trade weapons, taunts, and cosmetics fun to explore the depths of this game. The AI in TF2 knows what players want to do, so it has commands that are easy to understand and efficient. The AI also has commands you can type in the console to maximize game experience. The TF2 game modes offer a variety of fun as well as the AI which will make things easier to maneuver.
Do many games look fake to you? In TF2, the graphics can support a wide variety of computers; from slow ones to fast ones. These graphics are so good, you'll feel the game is real and not cartoony. Not only that, but if you lower your graphics, you'll still feel the game and your slow computer can run it. TF2 has explosions, bullets, balloons, confetti, you name it! With it's great graphics, players are able to see and distinguish everything from afar. Not only are the graphics great, but it also has great sounds. When you run into the battlefield, you'll hear enemies and teammates, you'll hear rockets and Spys up down left and right. The game also features it's own songs from the Valve Orchestra which is pretty amazing. Each class has their own songs and you'll be able to hear them in the start. You can talk to your teammates in game with the voice chat or use voice commands that help coordinate your team. Overall, the graphics and sounds both feature great gameplay and hypnotize you into the game.
TF2 is funny. Dating back to the beginning, it had a storyline about two brothers fighting for no reason, named Redmond and Blutarch. These brothers hired the TF2 mercenaries to fight for them and that’s the plot of the game. Even though TF2 doesn’t have campaign mode, one can read its comics from the TF2 website and the story goes on which shows players the characters’ backstory and lets them in on how the characters are like in person. The comics also informs us players about the upcoming updates to get us hyped about the game. Comics show us an even more in depth perspective of the game by showing us the Administrator and Miss Pauling, characters that aren’t on any side but monitor games. We see stories of how the Demoman lost his eye and what the game displays Halloween. These game comics give the game a nice backstory to get players to know what Team Fortress is about.
Another part that makes TF2 interesting is the community. Team Fortress 2 has a great community that helps new players and pushes this game to its limits. There is a steam workshop which players create items for the game and can earn money for doing so. This way Valve (creators of TF2) understands how players feel and we can contribute to our own game we love. Another aspect is the Source Filmmaker (SFM for short) Not only does TF2 host competitions for fighting, they host competitions for making the best short film. These films are entertaining and make people devote more of their lives to TF2.
The best part of Team Fortress is the virtual hats. Many people invest into buying these virtual cosmetics for TF2 because we are peer pressured by all the hat wearers in the game to buy and look the best. We gamers take these hats very seriously and many websites have been dedicated for buying, selling, and trading TF2 items. TF2 has a big community for hats and nobody with the right TF2 mindset wants to look plain. This makes TF2, TF2. How many games do you come across with more than 1100 cosmetics! This gives every player a chance to be unique in their own way and display their backpack full of hats.
TF2 is serious and also a laugh at the same time. Players full of fun can taunt all day and nobody would care that the game is coming to an end, or players will try to kill everyone and win. There aren’t many objectives in the game, and when you have one, you don’t have to do it. You won’t rage as much and it’ll be like relaxing; sometimes you try, sometimes you have fun.
In brief, Team Fortress 2 is a great game that offers so much - from the game modes to the hat simulation. All the nine years in development has certainly been worth the wait. In TF2, you’ll deal with a diverse mixture of classes, game modes, graphics and sounds, hats, and a great community. Overall, I would rate this game a 95% for all the great work everyone has put into it. I can’t stop playing!

Longevity is tough for competitive shooters. Hardly a month goes by without new virtual arenas cropping up and enticing you into some fresh conflict, and only a few popular games manage to sustain active player bases even a year after their initial release. And then there's Team Fortress 2. Released in 2007, this class-based classic is still going strong well into its seventh year, thanks largely to its lively and creative community.
The core action pits two teams of players against each other in a battle to capture points, move a cart, or steal a briefcase. The objective is always very straightforward; it's the interplay between the nine playable classes that makes things so varied and interesting. The speedy scout, the militant heavy, the diligent engineer, the conniving medic, the pesky sniper, the sneaky spy, the feisty pyro, the explosive soldier, and the even-more-explosive demoman all have unique weapons, attributes, and abilities that complement each other and clash in myriad ways. Encounters can vary widely depending on the match type and the makeup of each team, and this unpredictability is crucial to TF2's long-standing appeal.
When you come out of the gate as a heavy with a medic in tow, you're a formidable offensive force, but if a spy loops around to backstab the medic and you round the corner on a pyro, it can all come undone in a matter of seconds. Snipers can cover expected enemy paths, but rocket-jumping soldiers have a knack for finding alternative routes and raining explosive death from above. You may think you have a comparatively weak scout dead to rights, only to be stunned by a baseball and beaten to death. As you watch your giblets splatter on the ground and see a freeze-frame of your gleeful killer, it's hard not to chuckle at the sheer variety of ways you can meet an untimely demise. And the humorous quips, ridiculous outfits, and histrionic announcer help cultivate this lighthearted tone.
Of course, this core dynamic has persisted for most of TF2's life span, so if you stopped playing it a few years ago and come back for a few matches, you'll find things are very familiar. Learning the ropes and getting the hang of your chosen role is still a gratifying experience, and mastering advanced techniques doesn't just make you deadlier; it gives you more options for how to approach combat. Keeping your options open is still valuable too, because being flexible with your choice of character can help you avoid ending up on a catastrophically imbalanced squad. It is Team Fortress, after all.
But though there is much that has remained constant about the core game, there have been some notable changes over the years, as well as regular infusions of new weapons and items. Of the hundreds of things available in the online store, some can be unlocked through play, while others must be purchased with actual money. From small doodads that cost less than a dollar to massive bundles that cost hundreds, there's a wide range of ways to customize your experience.
Many of the items offer nothing more than a playful twist on the game's already cheeky cartoon aesthetic. You can buy hats, shirts, shoes, and other cosmetic gear to dress up like a character from Adult Swim or don spooky seasonal garb that you can wear only during Halloween or a full moon. Even if you don't fancy shelling out for any of this stuff, it's fun to see some visual variety as you try to light your opponents on fire.
Other weapons have more of an impact, like the ones that give your character a new chargeable and expendable power. The scout can build hype, which turns his usual double jump into a triple, quadruple, or quintuple jump, and the soldier can build rage, which allows him to rally his nearby teammates to do extra damage. Skills like these have more of a meaningful impact on the action, bringing something new to the table that your enemies must contend with. And then there are the totally out-there loadouts, like the one that turns the grenade-launching demoman into an extra from the movie Braveheart.In addition to the cosmetic options, there are a lot of weapons and items that offer small buffs or subtle tweaks to your attributes. Depending on which healing gun the medic equips, for example, he can imbue himself and his targeted ally with extra damage resistance or enable himself to match the speed of his target. Differences like these don't do much to change the core action, but they do give experienced players substantial room for strategic variation.
These options broaden the field of viable strategies, which helps keep combat lively and varied. And fortunately, none of the purchasable weapons or items tip the scales unfairly towards those willing to pay. Buffs and bonuses usually come with caveats, and the weapons that bestow new abilities are usually unlocked for free. For this review, I spent some money on goofy hats and some of the stranger weaponry on offer, like the pyro's flamethrower that actually shoots bubbles and rainbows. It was fun to play with the new gear, but I still found myself switching my loadout between free and paid weapons regularly to adapt to the match situation.
The biggest divergence from the game's origins comes in the cooperative mode, Mann vs. Machine. In it, you and a few other human players must prevent hordes of robotic incarnations of TF2's classes from delivering a bomb to your base. The money you earn from destroying robots can be spent on mid-match upgrades to your attributes and weaponry, which can be crucial to success. Even on the easiest level, the robot legions are fierce enough to test the mettle of an unorganized team. This is a mode where carefully planned weapon choices and defensive strategies can mean the difference between succeeding and having to try, try again. You can play this mode for free, but you won't be eligible to earn rare prizes or complete challenges unless you pay a dollar for a Tour of Duty ticket. Though it lacks the frenetic unpredictability of competitive play, the cooperative mode can still provide satisfaction for those dedicated enough to see it through.
But competition is the real draw, and the Team Fortress 2 community can certainly be competitive. On some servers, you might be berated for unwitting breaches of etiquette, while on others, you might be welcomed with helpful tips and ubercharges. You can even ask for help on certain servers and be paired up with another player who is willing to give you some tips through chat. The community around TF2 is an intriguing one, not just for their deep knowledge of and passion for the game, but for their creative efforts in designing new weapons, items, and maps that have since become part of the experience. It feels like a community of curators, without whom the game may well have dwindled away and passed into obsolescence years ago.
Staying relevant even a year after release is rare for a competitive shooter, and yet, here's Team Fortress 2, still lively after seven years in the business. At times it feels like the same game you could have played back then, and at other times it feels like no one will ever quite nail class-based shooter competition the way TF2 does. The experience has evolved over the years without compromising what made it so great in the first place, so though your free-to-play options may have increased considerably in the past few years, there are few that do it as well as Team Fortress 2.

CoD fanboys, watch out! This game is beast, and possibly one of the best online shooters I have ever played. Let's give it the rundown.
-Gameplay-
Smooth controls, good ping buffering, GREAT fps. This game is perfection for any computer. Seriously, I have a office computer with a decent graphics card, and this game runs 60fps every time. This is a game everyone can play, everyone can learn, and many can master.
-Community-
How do I explain this? Well, there's good and there's bad. People will have nicknames and names to call others because they don't wanna spend the 50 frickin cents to buy premium. A F2P they say. People can still be nice, but it's always in their gameplay. A lot of times the chat bar will be a flame war of some type, and people will kick others just because they don't like said person. Yeah... it's annoying. Just ignore it. Useful hint for new players! DONT HURT HOOVIES. Hoovies are creatures (Heavies) that are peaceful and rarely carry their weapon (Minigun) and prefer to crouch walk with GORU or KGOB. Leave em' be, and they may give you a sandvich. Shoot them, and their whole tribe will attack you. Your choice.
-Weapons and Classes-
This game is NOT pay to win, morover pay to look like you took a hat and infused it with magic. Just wanted to mention that. There are hundreds of weapons to choose from, and you can customize them with paint, killstreak counters, names and descriptions. The nine classes you can play as all have strengths and weaknesses, so in all honesty, this game is well balanced.
-Overall-
I have gotten more people to hate me in this game than all others i've ever played, but I have so much fun I don't give a darn. This game is wonderful, bright, colorful, maniacal, and CoD hating, and I would hope that everyone that sees this plays it.

In team fortress 2 there are 9 classes, each with there own unique talents, heres a description of all of them.
Born and raised in Boston, Massachusetts, the Scout is a fast-running scrapper with a baseball bat and a snarky 'in-your-face' attitude. He is the fastest unassisted character you can play as. His Double Jump leaves slower opponents struggling to keep up and helps him navigate the terrain while dodging oncoming projectiles.
The Soldier is a crazed, jingoistic patriot from America's heartland. Tough and well-armed, he is versatile, capable of both offense and defense, and a great starter class to get familiar with the game.
The Pyro is a mumbling pyromaniac of unknown origin who has a burning passion for all things fire related. As shown in Meet the Pyro, the Pyro appears to be insane and delusional, living in a utopian fantasy world known as Pyroland.
The Demoman is a drunk-swilling demolitions expert from the Scottish town of Ullapool, and is one of the more versatile members of the team. A master of explosives, the Demoman strategically deals indirect and mid-range combat and massive splash damage.
The Heavy Weapons Guy, more commonly known as the Heavy, is a towering hulk of a man that hails from the USSR. He is the largest and possibly most dangerous class in Team Fortress 2. Boasting the most default health and devastating firepower from his trusty Minigun
The Engineer is a soft-spoken, amiable Texan with an interest in all things mechanical. He specializes in constructing and maintaining Buildings that provide support to his team, rather than fighting at the front lines, making him the most suitable for defense.
The Medic is a Teutonic man of medicine. While he may have a tenuous adherence to medical ethics, he is nonetheless the primary healing class of the team. Although the Medic's Syringe Gun and Bonesaw aren't the greatest weapons for direct combat, he can typically still be found near the front lines, healing wounded teammates while trying to stay out of trouble.
Hailing from the lost country of New Zealand and raised in the unforgiving Australian outback, the Sniper is a tough and ready crack shot. The Sniper's main role on the battlefield is to pick off important enemy targets from afar using his Sniper Rifle and its ability to instantly kill a target with a headshot (with some exceptions). He is effective at long range, but weakens with proximity, where he is forced to use his Submachine Gun or his Kukri. As a result, the Sniper tends to perch on higher grounds or in hard-to-see places, where he can easily pin down enemies at chokepoints.
The Spy, hailing from an indeterminate region of France, is an enthusiast of sharp suits and even sharper knives. He relies on stealth and trickery to aid his team. Using a unique array of cloaking watches, he can render himself invisible or even fake his own death, leaving unaware opponents off-guard.

Overall, it is one of my most loved games in my library, and I doubt I'll ever hold a game in such a high regard ever again.

Team Fortress 2 is a lightheated shooter in a sea of call of duty,csgo,battlfield and more recently battlfront and rainbow six siege. It activly parodies the hyper violence and compertition of these games. Best of all you can jump into it without spending anything
The game has a total of 9 classes each with important roles to play for their team. First the scout has insane mobilty and a cockey anoying personalty.He can distract harass and keep pressure on the objective. The soldier can do burst damadge with his rockets and fly around with concussion jumps. He is a high Dps class and is a favorite among many. The pyro can light people on fire and reflect projectiles. He can cause panic and counter explossives. The heavy is the back bone of any push and hails from russia. He can take a beating and give one too. The engie can place sentry guns teleporters andvdispensers. His sentry provides area denial and the teleporter wins games. The medic is my personal favorite class and keeps his team fighting. The ubercharge is hudge and a medic makes a big diffrance to survablty.
The sniper can headshot and charge his shots. Even an overhealed hevey will fall to the snipers headshots. The sniper can take out anyone but takes a lot of skill. The spy can turn invisable and disguise as an enermy. He can be difficult to play but can destroy a sentry nest.
The games main game mode is payload but outers include: King of the hill,Controll points,Manpower,player destruction and lots more. The game has hundreds of achivments, tons of weapons and hats.
all in all, The game is really fun and great value for money.

Easily one of, if not the, best free-to-pay games on the market. It's a breath of fresh air from all of the other first person shooters that all have gritty realism and vulgar twelve year olds, with its cartoony graphics and humorous lore. There are more ways to play than just the nine classes presented to you, which in themselves are all completely different in their styles of gameplay as well. You have the scout, who had low health and average-damaging weapons, but is easily the fastest class overall. The heavy, who has very high damage outputs and high health, but is incredilby slow. The engineer can build structures to support the team, while having medicore weapons of his own. The demoman is average all around, but uses explosives which do lots of damage but hurt him as well and has a very slow reload speed. On top of all of this, unlockable weapons can give you a completely new style of gameplay. For example, the Demoman can get a sword and sheild, which turns you into the amighty demoknight, decapitating foes left and right. Overall a great game.
In Layman's Terms: 10/10, would r8 again, IGN.

Team Fortress 2 is an interesting game at best, It has a better verity, than, your average FPS and one game that does not release a new game each year. A prime example would be the Call Of Duty franchise, it started out as a casual FPS, than, turned into a very complex game and it keeps getting complex each year. However, TF2 has been out for about 8 years now and still is considered to be a better game than COD do to the fact the franchise COD franchise has been out long than TF2, it has a game each year. However, with TF2, it just has an update for a certain event or celebration that is planned and not just made into a new game. An example of this update is the Mann vs Machine update (MvM) which was made into a gamemode and not made into a different game altogether. Plus, the weapon machanic in COD and TF2 are drastically different in terms of gameplay, COD's weapon machanics are sometimes unbalanced, it creates fun for some people. While in TF2, It has a Pro and Con system for their weapons, let's say that there is a weapon that can gives you a better attack range, but, it would also decrease the wearers overall health. I think i rembled on long enough to reach a point. All in all, do I recommend TF2 to any one who is intereseted playing something new? Yes. Plus, TF2 is a great game to play and worth the time.

It's F2P where you can win without paying (despite the term F2P still being used to indicate a lack of skill). You play as one of 9 classes, each of which plays very differently, you will almost definitely find one that suits your style of gameplay. Sometimes a class' gameplay will change completely depending on what weapons you have e.g. The Demoman who usually launches grenades and sticky bombs becomes the demoknight who charges at enemies and decapitates them with a single swing. You can receive items at random and while these are quite often crates, you can just receive items on their own, without the need to pay. If you open a crate, you will be rewarded with a rarer weapon, of at least strange value.
The only downside I can think of is that sometimes, in fact quite often the players can be utter bellends, but of course there are just as many if not more great players who will tolerate and maybe even teach newcomers the ropes.

It's F2P where you can win without paying (despite the term F2P still being used to indicate a lack of skill). You play as one of 9 classes, each of which plays very differently, you will almost definitely find one that suits your style of gameplay. Sometimes a class' gameplay will change completely depending on what weapons you have e.g. The Demoman who usually launches grenades and sticky bombs becomes the demoknight who charges at enemies and decapitates them with a single swing. You can receive items at random and while these are quite often crates, you can just receive items on their own, without the need to pay. If you open a crate, you will be rewarded with a rarer weapon, of at least strange value.
The only downside I can think of is that sometimes, in fact quite often the players can be utter bellends, but of course there are just as many if not more great players who will tolerate and maybe even teach newcomers the ropes.

The short answer is, it's holding up very well. The core action pits two teams of players against each other in a battle to capture points, move a cart, or steal a briefcase. The objective is always very straightforward; it's the interplay between the nine playable classes that makes things so varied and interesting. The speedy scout, the militant heavy, the diligent engineer, the conniving medic, the pesky sniper, the sneaky spy, the feisty pyro, the explosive soldier, and the even-more-explosive demoman all have unique weapons, attributes, and abilities that complement each other and clash in myriad ways. Encounters can vary widely depending on the match type and the makeup of each team, and this unpredictability is crucial to TF2's long-standing appeal.
When you come out of the gate as a heavy with a medic in tow, you're a formidable offensive force, but if a spy loops around to backstab the medic and you round the corner on a pyro, it can all come undone in a matter of seconds. Snipers can cover expected enemy paths, but rocket-jumping soldiers have a knack for finding alternative routes and raining explosive death from above. You may think you have a comparatively weak scout dead to rights, only to be stunned by a baseball and beaten to death. As you watch your giblets splatter on the ground and see a freeze-frame of your gleeful killer, it's hard not to chuckle at the sheer variety of ways you can meet an untimely demise. And the humorous quips, ridiculous outfits, and histrionic announcer help cultivate this lighthearted tone.
Of course, this core dynamic has persisted for most of TF2's life span, so if you stopped playing it a few years ago and come back for a few matches, you'll find things are very familiar. Learning the ropes and getting the hang of your chosen role is still a gratifying experience, and mastering advanced techniques doesn't just make you deadlier; it gives you more options for how to approach combat. Keeping your options open is still valuable too, because being flexible with your choice of character can help you avoid ending up on a catastrophically imbalanced squad. It is Team Fortress, after all.
But though there is much that has remained constant about the core game, there have been some notable changes over the years, as well as regular infusions of new weapons and items. Of the hundreds of things available in the online store, some can be unlocked through play, while others must be purchased with actual money. From small doodads that cost less than a dollar to massive bundles that cost hundreds, there's a wide range of ways to customize your experience.
Many of the items offer nothing more than a playful twist on the game's already cheeky cartoon aesthetic. You can buy hats, shirts, shoes, and other cosmetic gear to dress up like a character from Adult Swim or don spooky seasonal garb that you can wear only during Halloween or a full moon. Even if you don't fancy shelling out for any of this stuff, it's fun to see some visual variety as you try to light your opponents on fire.
Other weapons have more of an impact, like the ones that give your character a new chargeable and expendable power. The scout can build hype, which turns his usual double jump into a triple, quadruple, or quintuple jump, and the soldier can build rage, which allows him to rally his nearby teammates to do extra damage. Skills like these have more of a meaningful impact on the action, bringing something new to the table that your enemies must contend with. And then there are the totally out-there loadouts, like the one that turns the grenade-launching demoman into an extra from the movie Braveheart.In addition to the cosmetic options, there are a lot of weapons and items that offer small buffs or subtle tweaks to your attributes. Depending on which healing gun the medic equips, for example, he can imbue himself and his targeted ally with extra damage resistance or enable himself to match the speed of his target. Differences like these don't do much to change the core action, but they do give experienced players substantial room for strategic variation.
These options broaden the field of viable strategies, which helps keep combat lively and varied. And fortunately, none of the purchasable weapons or items tip the scales unfairly towards those willing to pay. Buffs and bonuses usually come with caveats, and the weapons that bestow new abilities are usually unlocked for free. For this review, I spent some money on goofy hats and some of the stranger weaponry on offer, like the pyro's flamethrower that actually shoots bubbles and rainbows. It was fun to play with the new gear, but I still found myself switching my loadout between free and paid weapons regularly to adapt to the match situation.

Team Fortress 2 is a class based shooter with 9 classes, each with there own unique strength's and weakness's.
The Scout Is a fast class(that can run)
with a shotgun-like weapon named "The Scattergun", one of the best quality's of the game is you can have other weapon's instead of the deafult's. such as the Force-A-Nature, which has 2 which when fired makes your target go flying!
His secondary is a pistol, which... is a pistol... that can be switched with the "Bonk! Atomic Punch" when drank gives you invincability for 8 seconds.
His Melee Is a bat. The bat can be swiched with many thing's, such as a Ham, a frying pan, A Fish, or a sign :P
The Next class is The Soldier. To sum it up you have a rocket launcher... use it. One of the best uses for the Rocket Launcher is that if you shoot at your feet you can start flying in the air (P.S. if you want to you can use the Rocket Jumper to practice.)
His Secondary is a Shotgun, It can be switched with The Buff Banner, when you have done a certin amount of damage to the enemy team, you are granted Mini-Crits for a couple of seconds, also it affects your sourrounding team mates, so they have Mini-Crits as well.
His melee Is a shovel XD, this can be swiched with The Market Gardener, that deals crits when the weilder is rocket jumping.
The Third Class is the pyro, no one know's where this pyromaniac came from, all anyone really know's is he/she likes fire.
as the pyro you wield a Flamethrower...this can be switched with a tuba that shoot's rainbow's...(now that is original)
you also wield a Shotgun that can be switched with The Flare Gun to set people a-flame from a distance.
The Pyro's melee is the Fire Axe, it can be switched with a lollipop...(This game is killing me XD littraly.)
The next class is The Demoman, this black, scottish, cyclops has 1 eye and grenade's. What's more scary then that?
His Primary Is a Grenade Launcher... that can be switched with boot's (well then STAY IN STYLE)
His Secondary is a StickyBomb Launcher, that can be switched with a sheild...
His Melee isa beer bottle, This can be switched with a sword, when the sword, Sheild, And boot's combine they make a Demo-Knight
The Class after that Is The Heavy, He's Fat and has a machine gun... (well i'm locking my window's tonight.)
His Primary is The Mini-Gun, It can be switched with other mini-gun's such as the tomislav.
His Secondary is a shotgun (WOAH) this can be switched with a sandwich XD.
His melee is... his fist (FIST MEH DADDY) these can be switched with gloves. :P
The next Class (my personal favorite) The Engineer, He's a texan that sit's around...(ooo so scary!)
He Has A shotgun
A pistol
and a wrench...
HE CAN BUILD TURRET'S
those shoot people for you.
He's fun that's all he is... FUN (also don't forget to put up teleporter's and dispencer's NEVER FORGET)
The next class is the sniper, first things first, if you're coming from a diffrent Fps game don't immidiatly go for sniper, you can't quickscope/noscope (i mean you can but not kill the person)
His Primary is a sniper rifle, (what else could it be?) it can be switched with other rifle's such as the♥♥♥♥♥♥rifle, you shoot people and there covered with♥♥♥♥♥♥.. XD
His secondary is an SMG it can shoot people, It can be switched with with the "Can Of♥♥♥♥♥♥quot; you throw it at people and there covered with♥♥♥♥♥♥:D
His Melee is a Kukri... uhhh not much to say about it
The next class I also love, The Medic, You bassicly Heal people
you're the extreme Defense class.
The last class is the Spy he is very eligant with the way he talk's, and moves, and fuc- I MEAN SHOOTS YOU!
His Primary Is A Revolver, This can be switched with The Ambassador, which can get headshot's :D
His secondary is a Sapper, this can blow up the engineer's turret's :D
he also has a knife...(stab people in the back see what happens :D)
He can also be invisable by using the Right-Click, as the Spy you can also desguise as the enemy team (but be carful, act as if you're on the enemy team)
And that is all of the class's In team fortress 2, but I guess im not done yet.
If you go to Co-Op mode, you can fight robot's and get reward's at the end (if you pay 99c)
Every few month's there will be an update, It can very to what the update add's it can add new weapon's, New Map's New Gamemode's you name it.
there are 8 Gamemode's In Team Fortress 2, the first is payload, where the blu team pushes the cart to the red team's base to blow it up.
The 2nd is King Of The Hill, where each team fight's to capture the center control point.
The 3rd Is Attack/Deffense where one team fight's through the other team's defense's to get to the other team's point and win the game, but if they don't get there in time they loose.
The 4rth Is Payload Race, It's like payload, but there is two cart's both trying to get to the top while stopping the other team's cart
The 5th Is Control Point's it is like KOTH, exept both side's have control point's.
The 6th Is Capture The Flag, where both side's have a breaf case at the bottom of there base, you try to defend your's while getting the other team's.
The 7th Is Special Delivery it currently has only 1 map but the premise is you get the rocket thing from a place and put in a big missile and it goes to space I guess...

Wow.
Even silly old me, who is, like, the most pessimistic, despicable, and downright uncomfortable person to be with in all of history is amazed at how cancerous this game and its community have become.
Good thing that you can find out people's IDs via consolecom status and then BLOCK THEM.
Also, great job at microtransactions, Valve.
If only you could use that money to, I don't know, fix stuff?
Numerous models and animations have errors or inconsistencies.
The engineer still inserts the magazine of his pistol the wrong way.
Holding many special melee weapons still looks completely wrong on ALL classes.
Grenade launcher still hasn't been updated for the new ammo count.
Do I have to say more about the 2-barreled grenade launcher that miraculously holds 3 grenades?
Clipping occurs, and is quite visible on the Awper Hand.
Lord ♥♥♥♥♥wain's NMCAP:Helmet does clip with ANY other hat.
World models of non-stock-weapons are sometimes held incorrectly.
Until recently, the red-tape recorder didn't reset its animation correctly - for at least 6 months.
Quick-Fix or Vaccinator plus any Medic backpack = Eye cancer.
The netcode has become a mess, which is largely attributable to aforementioned microtransactions, and the incredible amount of content that came with it.
Due to this... AddOn-frenzy, the game's code is a very interesting ecosystem.
Prepare for two more bugs if one is squished in a patch.
Also, lag compensation seems to have become sporadic, and so it seems off for both the giving, as well as the taking side.
Game balance, which was already flawed in the original build, has been purged completely since mid-2009.
Rockets don't feel like the long-range support they should be, sentries knock you into the nearest orbit, and the multitude of mediguns destabilizes the game even further.
It is IMPOSSIBLE to balance such a content range properly, and attempts to do so have mostly resulted in a fiasco.
Microtransactions/Drops/Trading are stupid, although it impresses me that Valve managed to create a functioning, fictional economy.
One with uncontrollable inflation, but an economy nonetheless.
Crates and the likes are the final addition of insult to injury, as not everything can be achieved by solely playing the game.
This would be a moot point, if keys could actually drop, even with a minimal chance, and if any tickets could be achieved via crates, or as drops.
The latest "improvement" is the addition of skinned weapons, which bring absolutely nothing new to the table.
While strange weapons still had some kind of appeal, the megalomania of skinned, customized, killstreak-enabled, collector's weapons is baffling.
Speaking of which: The visual style of the game was very appealing. "Was" in the past tense, because the art direction has changed for the worse.
In-house graphics take on outlandish designs, as seen in MvM, and the inclusion of community created content has led to such things as the... "Potassium Bonnett".
This completely undermines the original concept of focusing the player's attention on the opponent's held weapon for quick, tactical reactions, and instead causes missed shots and visual clutter in general.
The score is good, if not excellent.
I can NOT recommend this game AT ALL anymore. Not in its current state.
Of course you could download the game for its music, but the size of the download could discourage you from that.

I love changing. I can't stand doing the same thing over and over again, and that's why I love Team Fortress 2.
This game can't be described as anything else but an endless, ever-changing hole of fun that will brutally murder your social life, if you let it do so. Otherwise you can play with your friends, idk.
So, let me level it out for a second.
You know how awesome games like Call Of Duty have weapons with very specific stats? I don't know, fire rate or damage per bullet for example.
Well, TF2 makes a step further. It introduces incredibly fun and addictive mechanics, like stats that ease the rocket jumping (born as a bug, improved to be a game-changing mechanic) or that turn an explosives-based class into a charging knight with a head-hungry sword.
The key of this game is the variety.
We're talking about rocket launchers that heal you when an enemy is hit or with rockets that fly fast as lightning and deal a ton of damage if they hit directly the target.
About miniguns that slow the enemy at each hit or that spin silently to ambush them.
About shotguns that don't need reload, and will continue shooting as long as you continue hitting, or that will shoot projectiles that heal your team's buildings.
Multiply this amount of variety for 9, the number of classes in this amazing game. Then for 3, which is the number of weapon slots (for primary, secondary and melee weapons). And then for about 10, which is more or less the number of weapons avaiable for EACH slot for EACH class.
Look at how many hours I played of this, and consider that I've never been bored once. I felt mad, accomplished, happy, but never bored.
This game didn't survive 8 years for nothing, and I highly recommend at least trying it out.
