Wow.
Even silly old me, who is, like, the most pessimistic, despicable, and downright uncomfortable person to be with in all of history is amazed at how cancerous this game and its community have become.
Good thing that you can find out people's IDs via consolecom status and then BLOCK THEM.
Also, great job at microtransactions, Valve.
If only you could use that money to, I don't know, fix stuff?
Numerous models and animations have errors or inconsistencies.
The engineer still inserts the magazine of his pistol the wrong way.
Holding many special melee weapons still looks completely wrong on ALL classes.
Grenade launcher still hasn't been updated for the new ammo count.
Do I have to say more about the 2-barreled grenade launcher that miraculously holds 3 grenades?
Clipping occurs, and is quite visible on the Awper Hand.
Lord ♥♥♥♥♥wain's NMCAP:Helmet does clip with ANY other hat.
World models of non-stock-weapons are sometimes held incorrectly.
Until recently, the red-tape recorder didn't reset its animation correctly - for at least 6 months.
Quick-Fix or Vaccinator plus any Medic backpack = Eye cancer.
The netcode has become a mess, which is largely attributable to aforementioned microtransactions, and the incredible amount of content that came with it.
Due to this... AddOn-frenzy, the game's code is a very interesting ecosystem.
Prepare for two more bugs if one is squished in a patch.
Also, lag compensation seems to have become sporadic, and so it seems off for both the giving, as well as the taking side.
Game balance, which was already flawed in the original build, has been purged completely since mid-2009.
Rockets don't feel like the long-range support they should be, sentries knock you into the nearest orbit, and the multitude of mediguns destabilizes the game even further.
It is IMPOSSIBLE to balance such a content range properly, and attempts to do so have mostly resulted in a fiasco.
Microtransactions/Drops/Trading are stupid, although it impresses me that Valve managed to create a functioning, fictional economy.
One with uncontrollable inflation, but an economy nonetheless.
Crates and the likes are the final addition of insult to injury, as not everything can be achieved by solely playing the game.
This would be a moot point, if keys could actually drop, even with a minimal chance, and if any tickets could be achieved via crates, or as drops.
The latest "improvement" is the addition of skinned weapons, which bring absolutely nothing new to the table.
While strange weapons still had some kind of appeal, the megalomania of skinned, customized, killstreak-enabled, collector's weapons is baffling.
Speaking of which: The visual style of the game was very appealing. "Was" in the past tense, because the art direction has changed for the worse.
In-house graphics take on outlandish designs, as seen in MvM, and the inclusion of community created content has led to such things as the... "Potassium Bonnett".
This completely undermines the original concept of focusing the player's attention on the opponent's held weapon for quick, tactical reactions, and instead causes missed shots and visual clutter in general.
The score is good, if not excellent.
I can NOT recommend this game AT ALL anymore. Not in its current state.
Of course you could download the game for its music, but the size of the download could discourage you from that.

Team Fortress 2 was launched in 10/10/2007.
As years went by,Valve made more and more hats,and people complained that too much effort was given into cosmetic items and less into the gameplay,the game was turning into Hat Fortress 2,and people claimed the game was dying,even though Valve constantly updates their game with gameplay content,like maps,modes,new weapons,and bug fixes.
As years went by,Valve made more and more promotions for pre-ordering a game and getting items for TF2,and people claimed the game was dying,even though you usually can get these items without paying and most are just cosmetic items.
As years went by, new gameplay content was being made more by the community, while Valve focused more into the cosmetic content, and the game was dying because Valve left the game for us to improve.
Pretty much everytime the game gets a balance patch, with classes and weapons being nerfed or buffed, people say the game is dead, usually people that loved that weapon that was nerfed.
5/21/09,the game got its first 9 hats,people probably marked that day as when the game became a "Hat Simulator",and the game died.
To get those hats, many people started idling,don't play the game and just wait for the hats to come with the new item drop system, some players, even made programs designed especially to idle, but in 9/2/09, Valve decided to take away all the items from players that used those programs, and reward the players who didn't with a halo for you to wear, people that got their items taken were infuriated, and the community was really divided, servers started banning people who weared the halo, and there were other servers banning those who didn't, and the game, was dead for many, many people, also, idling persists to this day.
In 6/10/10, the game got the Mac Update, that made TF2 playable on MAC OS X, this angried many people, especially Apple haters, but what made the biggest complaints, were the Earbuds, earbuds similar to those made by Apple, and you got one by playing the game on MAC OS X during some days, just that item made the community rage and ban players that used it, there was a petition to remove the item, and the game was dead again, most people just logged into a Mac to get the item and continue playing on Windows.
On 9/30/10 the game got a store for microtransactions, people claimed the game was dead, because now we had to pay to win the matches, even though we never had, getting weapons that change gameplay is easy, you can easily trade weapons you don't want for one you want, expensive and rare weapons are just reskins, and the cosmetic items don't change anything, they're just decoration, there was a time where some hats combined with some weapons gave you bonus stats, but that stopped a long time ago.
On 6/23/11, the game became Free to Play, people claimed the game was dead because now the game would be full of noobs and annoying players, like if other multiplayer games didn't have the same issue, and like everyone started a good player,some people even asked for refunds like they deserved their money back,people raged because your only reward for paying for the game was an ugly hat that proves it,when you also were instantly given a premium account, that has some advantages over free players,but no advantages in actual competition.
On 9/6/11,Steam Trading came,and people complained that Valve was going too far into allowing people to trade games for hats,and the game was dying.
On 6/27/12, came the Meet the Pyro short along with the Pyroland mode,and people again claimed the game was dead due to Valve making the game cute and cuddly and making the Pyro even more crazy than we thought.
On 8/15/12,the game got the Mann vs. Machine mode,and people claimed Valve was being greedy because there was a mode that required a paid item to play,the Mann Up mode,and the game was dying,even though the only difference in that mode is that you get exclusive cosmetics and reskin weapons.
On 1/10/13,it was announced that the original 9 hats from 5/21/2009 were going to be retired,so no one could get new copies of them anymore (Except from old crates),but you could keep the ones you had and trade them,and you could still buy the hats for two weeks before that,the game was dead because Valve was desperate to sell items that weren't selling well,also, Valve never did that again.
On 10/29/13, the game got a unicorn hat called "The Magical Mercenary", and people claimed the game was dead just because one single hat.
On 5/17/13, the Robotic Boogaloo update was released,a community update,and it was just a bunch of robotic versions of cosmetics that the game already had,people claimed Valve didn't care for the game anymore,again,and the game was dying.
On 6/17/14, people claimed the game was dead again,because of the Conga,a taunt where players can dance around the map instead of shooting each other.
On 10/29/14,the game got some bumper car minigames,people claimed Valve was running out of ideas,the game was turning into Mario Kart,and the game was dead.
On 12/8/14,the game got the End of the Line Update,another community update,it was kinda boring,it was heavily focused on ducks,and the map Snowplow was cut because Valve thought it was too complicated,and people claimed the game was dying,also,Snowplow was added later.
On 7/2/15,the game started having painted weapons just like CS:GO,and people claimed Valve was adding more and more ways to get easy money,the game was turning into TF:GO,and you had to pay for an item to get these weapons and crates to get them, you were paying to get crates and pay to open them,and the game was dead.
On 10/6/2015, the game got the Invasion Update, again made by the community, people claimed the update was boring, not much new content, and again the game was dead, even though it had a new mode.
I made this review 12/3/15, and the game didn't look like dead back then, the peak that day was 56,632 people playing.
TF2 is set to die again with Blizzard's Overwatch,let's see how that goes,people said the same about World of Warcraft and its clones.
12/9/15 came, and the new thing that made the game dead is the trade holds,also called the ESCROW,where you're going to wait 3 days to trade items if one of the two traders don't protect his account on a phone and confirm every trade on it,people even claimed they were leaving Steam.
12/17/15 came with the Tough Break Update, and the the game is dead again because of two things I mentioned earlier, because it's just like the Gun Mettle Update where you have to pay to get the reskin weapons and also pay to get crates and then pay to open them, and because of nerfing the Pyro and Demoknight, when you could argue that the Pyro was actually buffed.
Well,now it's 6/25/16,Overwatch is been on for a while,and the peak today is 64,208,the game is still not dead,maybe I'll update again next year about that.
7/7/16 came with the Meet Your Match Update, and Valve removed their public servers from the game, and their servers only exist in matchmaking, they also removed the quickplay mode, and the game is dead, even though you can still play on community servers and search them with the old server browser.
Well, 10/10/17 came, and Team Fortress 2 is now 10 years old, and I admit, the complaints that the game is dead, were never that valid, it's been more than 1 year, and no major updates, but the game is still not dead since many people still play it, let's just wait for the next update, and see how that goes.

This game was absolutely fantastic when it first came out back in 2007. The art style, the tactical TEAM combat, the unique characters, just doesn't exist anymore. The game now is full of narcissistic hat-worshipping basement dwellers that make you question your existance. The developers just don't really give a flying f'uck about it anymore and just want to milk the huge cash cow teets of useless pixels that people just drool ponds over. The scale of skill amongst players is so huge, that it drastically changes the way the game is played. Any chance of fun in this game is ulitimately ruined by people who are so good at a game, that you want to take pity on because of how unpopular this game is to the entire internet community. Every time I go back into the game, I want to expect something drastic has changed, but, I end up coming out with frustration and disappointment. The side-grades to the stock weapons are mostly useless but sometimes are necessary upgrades. Players in every game always want to WIN, if they cant win, then they try and scramble the teams. If they can't scramble the teams, then they leave, making it even more frustrating when playing the game with less players.
On the other hand, if you do manage to be good enough in the game somehow. There are competitive scenes in this game and in a sense, can be fun. But, this is something that the game doesn't want you to find out, it wants you to be a useless drone that will just pour out money for hats that you cant see literally 90% of the time.
So if you are interested in not having any fun, losing faith in humanity, and wasting space on your hard drive. Then Team Fortress 2 is the game for you!

Team Fortress 2 was launched in 10/10/2007.
As years went by,Valve made more and more hats,and people complained that too much effort was given into cosmetic items and less into the gameplay,the game was turning into Hat Fortress 2,and people claimed the game was dying,even though Valve constantly updates their game with gameplay content,like maps,modes,new weapons,and bug fixes.
As years went by,Valve made more and more promotions for pre-ordering a game and getting items for TF2,and people claimed the game was dying,even though you usually can get these items without paying and most are just cosmetic items.
As years went by, new gameplay content was being made more by the community, while Valve focused more into the cosmetic content, and the game was dying because Valve left the game for us to improve.
Pretty much everytime the game gets a balance patch, with classes and weapons being nerfed or buffed, people say the game is dead, usually people that loved that weapon that was nerfed.
5/21/09,the game got its first 9 hats,people probably marked that day as when the game became a "Hat Simulator",and the game died.
To get those hats, many people started idling,don't play the game and just wait for the hats to come with the new item drop system, some players, even made programs designed especially to idle, but in 9/2/09, Valve decided to take away all the items from players that used those programs, and reward the players who didn't with a halo for you to wear, people that got their items taken were infuriated, and the community was really divided, servers started banning people who weared the halo, and there were other servers banning those who didn't, and the game, was dead for many, many people, also, idling persists to this day.
In 6/10/10, the game got the Mac Update, that made TF2 playable on MAC OS X, this angried many people, especially Apple haters, but what made the biggest complaints, were the Earbuds, earbuds similar to those made by Apple, and you got one by playing the game on MAC OS X during some days, just that item made the community rage and ban players that used it, there was a petition to remove the item, and the game was dead again, most people just logged into a Mac to get the item and continue playing on Windows.
On 9/30/10 the game got a store for microtransactions, people claimed the game was dead, because now we had to pay to win the matches, even though we never had, getting weapons that change gameplay is easy, you can easily trade weapons you don't want for one you want, expensive and rare weapons are just reskins, and the cosmetic items don't change anything, they're just decoration, there was a time where some hats combined with some weapons gave you bonus stats, but that stopped a long time ago.
On 6/23/11, the game became Free to Play, people claimed the game was dead because now the game would be full of noobs and annoying players, like if other multiplayer games didn't have the same issue, and like everyone started a good player,some people even asked for refunds like they deserved their money back,people raged because your only reward for paying for the game was an ugly hat that proves it,when you also were instantly given a premium account, that has some advantages over free players,but no advantages in actual competition.
On 9/6/11,Steam Trading came,and people complained that Valve was going too far into allowing people to trade games for hats,and the game was dying.
On 6/27/12, came the Meet the Pyro short along with the Pyroland mode,and people again claimed the game was dead due to Valve making the game cute and cuddly and making the Pyro even more crazy than we thought.
On 8/15/12,the game got the Mann vs. Machine mode,and people claimed Valve was being greedy because there was a mode that required a paid item to play,the Mann Up mode,and the game was dying,even though the only difference in that mode is that you get exclusive cosmetics and reskin weapons.
On 1/10/13,it was announced that the original 9 hats from 5/21/2009 were going to be retired,so no one could get new copies of them anymore (Except from old crates),but you could keep the ones you had and trade them,and you could still buy the hats for two weeks before that,the game was dead because Valve was desperate to sell items that weren't selling well,also, Valve never did that again.
On 10/29/13, the game got a unicorn hat called "The Magical Mercenary", and people claimed the game was dead just because one single hat.
On 5/17/13, the Robotic Boogaloo update was released,a community update,and it was just a bunch of robotic versions of cosmetics that the game already had,people claimed Valve didn't care for the game anymore,again,and the game was dying.
On 6/17/14, people claimed the game was dead again,because of the Conga,a taunt where players can dance around the map instead of shooting each other.
On 10/29/14,the game got some bumper car minigames,people claimed Valve was running out of ideas,the game was turning into Mario Kart,and the game was dead.
On 12/8/14,the game got the End of the Line Update,another community update,it was kinda boring,it was heavily focused on ducks,and the map Snowplow was cut because Valve thought it was too complicated,and people claimed the game was dying,also,Snowplow was added later.
On 7/2/15,the game started having painted weapons just like CS:GO,and people claimed Valve was adding more and more ways to get easy money,the game was turning into TF:GO,and you had to pay for an item to get these weapons and crates to get them, you were paying to get crates and pay to open them,and the game was dead.
On 10/6/2015, the game got the Invasion Update, again made by the community, people claimed the update was boring, not much new content, and again the game was dead, even though it had a new mode.
I made this review 12/3/15, and the game didn't look like dead back then, the peak that day was 56,632 people playing.
TF2 is set to die again with Blizzard's Overwatch,let's see how that goes,people said the same about World of Warcraft and its clones.
12/9/15 came, and the new thing that made the game dead is the trade holds,also called the ESCROW,where you're going to wait 3 days to trade items if one of the two traders don't protect his account on a phone and confirm every trade on it,people even claimed they were leaving Steam.
12/17/15 came with the Tough Break Update, and the the game is dead again because of two things I mentioned earlier, because it's just like the Gun Mettle Update where you have to pay to get the reskin weapons and also pay to get crates and then pay to open them, and because of nerfing the Pyro and Demoknight, when you could argue that the Pyro was actually buffed.
Well,now it's 6/25/16,Overwatch is been on for a while,and the peak today is 64,208,the game is still not dead,maybe I'll update again next year about that.
7/7/16 came with the Meet Your Match Update, and Valve removed their public servers from the game, and their servers only exist in matchmaking, they also removed the quickplay mode, and the game is dead, even though you can still play on community servers and search them with the old server browser.
Well, 10/10/17 came, and Team Fortress 2 is now 10 years old, and I admit, the complaints that the game is dead, were never that valid, it's been more than 1 year, and no major updates, but the game is still not dead since many people still play it, let's just wait for the next update, and see how that goes.

To start off, once again I have plenty more hours than this on my alternate account. I usually always start my reviews off mentioning that.
So getting into it, TeamFortress two is widely regarded as a wonderful game and I am here to confirm that by all means possible, this is mostly for the new players who don't know what exactly this game is.(Also it's for my profile.)
This first person shooter is a wild card from all the battlefield's, call of duty's and halo's in that those games you can pick up and get going with realitive ease. TeamFortress two how ever has completely destroyed the normal shooter process, there's only two automatic weapons in this game and cover serves as little to no benifit, or less than the modern FPS anyways.
There are nine set classes, and no one class can have the others loadout (Unless modded, but that's for another day.) As follow's there is scout, pyro, soldier, heavy, engineer, spy, sniper, medic and demo in no order at all. I guess we can through all of them as well.
Scout: A fast moving and hard hitting class at close range, with medium to long engagements being very rare for this class. Stay moving and use your footing, that's how you stay alive as a scout. This class uses a scattergun basiclly a small shotgun, a pistol and a melee weapon.
Pyro: Pretty much a walk forward and hold Mouse one type of character, unless your good enough to know how to use the flare gun and stuff like that. Not exactly sure how to explain this class. This class obviously uses a flamethrower, and a shotgun as well as a melee weapon.
Heavy: A large russian support class with a mini-gun, he is very slow and usually has a medic healing him at all times. That being said without a medic (And depending on player skill, with a medic.) the heavy is farthest from a tank class. Seeing as how slow he is he has a multitude of dangers presented to him.
Demo: The demo man, is at best a damage output class. He can be useful in almost any situation but takes alot of time to master, he has a pipe grenade launcher and a sticky launcher along with the melee that every class gets.
Soldier: The easiest class to play but also the hardest to master, the soldier is basiclly your front lines guy he's always leading the charge and he can put out some serious damage. He has a rocket launcher and usually a shotgun unless your going to be rocket jumping.
Medic: Simply put the healer, that about sums up the medic. Learn to dodge your spam and this class should be a cake walk. This class has a medic gun that heals, a syringe gun that is used for defense and small amounts of damage and a melee weapon.
Engineer: This class is made for camping, he recieves a shotgun, PDA, destroyer button thingy, and a pistol. The PDA allows you to build turrets, dispensers which heal your teammates, provide them with ammo, and provide you and other engineers with scrap to build said things.
Spy: This class is pretty much what it sounds like, you recieve a knife, revolver of sorts, Scrambler or whatever and a disguse mechanic. The knife is best when used to backstab someone as it grants an instakill. The pistol is good for those medium to long range engagements and the scrambler is used to sabotage the Engineers buildings. The disguise mechanism allows you to become anyone on the enemy team(Or your own team.) Class wise. When disguised you're not allowed to shoot or you will drop your disguise, all attacking while disguised will cause you to drop your disguise. This class is the most complicated and also comes with a invisible watch that allows your character to become invisible for a short amount of time, while moving with some watches the time will drain faster.
Sniper: Click on heads and have good accuracy, the sniper has a charge up rate. The longer you are scoped in the more damage your shot will do. Simple enough, this class recives the sniper rifle, a SMG and a melee as per stander to every other class.
It's a very fun game and if you haven't tried it yet I would recommend it for anyone, unless your one of those call of duty players in which case I'd say stay away from this game, the lack of automatic weapons and ADS will most likely make you cry. Or rage quit, and for the love of god stop playing combat medic it's stupid....Seriously.

Team Fortress 2 is a game. This game offer micro-transactions. Now, there is no in-game currency.
What you do with your real-life money is buy virtual hats. Now what do you do with virtual hats? That's right. Trade. What do you do to trade? Make profit. What do you do when you make profit? Get more hats. What do you do when you get more hats? Trade. What do you do when you trade again? Make profit. Now what do you do when your out of money. Get more money. What do you do when you have money? Buy more hats. What do you do when you have more hats? Trade more. What do you do when you trade more? Make more profit. What do you do when you make more profit? Get more hats.
You get the idea, right?

As much as I would like to recommend this game, in its current state, I cannot.  The #1 reason why I do NOT recommend this game is due to the large amount of cheaters in every server.
I bought this game as part of the Orange Box when it was released years ago.  Back then, the community on the servers was a blast.  Nowadays, the good community servers are far and few between.  Once you do find a good server with nice players, you're bound to get hit by at least one hacker on that server.  Sure you can call them out, you can use the report feature, you can spectate them and watch the grid alignment or the wallhacking while in spectate view.  But the hackers are so brazen that once you call them out they just deny it because they know it can't get detected and/or there's nothing preventing them from not doing it.  One of my favorite games totally sucks now due to hackers.
I recommend you try it, sure, it's free!  But do NOT spend a single cent on the game until they fix the hacker problem.
Repeat: Do NOT spend a single $ cent $ on this game until they fix the hacker problem!
As an EDIT:
Let me post more about the game, in case you are new and reading this.
TF2 is team game with its core based around balance.  You have Offense, Defense, and Support.  I truly feel no single class is over powered, because when you come up against a class that keeps killing you, you can switch classes to counter.  Some consider this "raging", but I consider it a function of the game.  A good team is based around balance and your ability to assess what class is needed.  A good pyro can go a long way.
Offense:
Scout - Fast moving, caps faster, double jumps.
Soldier - Shoots rockets, can rocket jump.
Pyro - Burns players, can reflect projectiles and enemy players.
Defense:
Demo - Uses sticky bombs that you control detonation, shoots bombs, and can sticky jump.
Heavy - The machine gun guy if you like shooting from the hip.  Slow moving, easy target.
Engineer - Builds sentries, teleportes, and turrets to protect or defend areas.
Support:
Medic - Heals, proviedes healing based perks to players such as invulnerability and 100% crits.
Sniper - The most played class for aimbotters.  Headshots usually = one shot kills.
Spy - Can disguise as enemy players to infiltrate the enemy team.
On top of all of this there is a cash shop where you can buy new weapons or clothing for your classes.  You have a limited sized backpack to store items, so as it fills up you will find yourself deleting items.  You can randomly gain an item or a locked crate.  The locked crates require keys, purchased with real money from the cash shop, to unlock them.  There you might find a rare item inside.  When it's all said and done, rares mean nothing and usually the best weapons are the ones you have by default.  You can juggle your weapons based on the needs of your team, but the standard issue are the best in most cases.

As much as I would like to recommend this game, in its current state, I cannot.  The #1 reason why I do NOT recommend this game is due to the large amount of cheaters in every server.
I bought this game as part of the Orange Box when it was released years ago.  Back then, the community on the servers was a blast.  Nowadays, the good community servers are far and few between.  Once you do find a good server with nice players, you're bound to get hit by at least one hacker on that server.  Sure you can call them out, you can use the report feature, you can spectate them and watch the grid alignment or the wallhacking while in spectate view.  But the hackers are so brazen that once you call them out they just deny it because they know it can't get detected and/or there's nothing preventing them from not doing it.  One of my favorite games totally sucks now due to hackers.
I recommend you try it, sure, it's free!  But do NOT spend a single cent on the game until they fix the hacker problem.
Repeat: Do NOT spend a single $ cent $ on this game until they fix the hacker problem!
As an EDIT:
Let me post more about the game, in case you are new and reading this.
TF2 is team game with its core based around balance.  You have Offense, Defense, and Support.  I truly feel no single class is over powered, because when you come up against a class that keeps killing you, you can switch classes to counter.  Some consider this "raging", but I consider it a function of the game.  A good team is based around balance and your ability to assess what class is needed.  A good pyro can go a long way.
Offense:
Scout - Fast moving, caps faster, double jumps.
Soldier - Shoots rockets, can rocket jump.
Pyro - Burns players, can reflect projectiles and enemy players.
Defense:
Demo - Uses sticky bombs that you control detonation, shoots bombs, and can sticky jump.
Heavy - The machine gun guy if you like shooting from the hip.  Slow moving, easy target.
Engineer - Builds sentries, teleportes, and turrets to protect or defend areas.
Support:
Medic - Heals, proviedes healing based perks to players such as invulnerability and 100% crits.
Sniper - The most played class for aimbotters.  Headshots usually = one shot kills.
Spy - Can disguise as enemy players to infiltrate the enemy team.
On top of all of this there is a cash shop where you can buy new weapons or clothing for your classes.  You have a limited sized backpack to store items, so as it fills up you will find yourself deleting items.  You can randomly gain an item or a locked crate.  The locked crates require keys, purchased with real money from the cash shop, to unlock them.  There you might find a rare item inside.  When it's all said and done, rares mean nothing and usually the best weapons are the ones you have by default.  You can juggle your weapons based on the needs of your team, but the standard issue are the best in most cases.

This game should probably be dead, the only reason people continue to play it is because it's free. The game used to have a lot of charm and feel to the classes but over time it's gotten dull. It's very hard to play casual mode and it's hard to find a good community server. I can only imagine what it'd be like playing this game for your first time now. When I first got it a couple years back I loved it. Pubs were the best thing to happen and the weapon balance wasn't actually too bad. Now there's a very small development team that doesn't know what they're doing. The matchmaking in the new casual mode might as well not even exist. Why even have it? Pubs were the ultimate casual mode. You could drop into a game and have your friend connect mid-game, and they were almost always full. I would not be able to tell you how many times I've been put into a game with less than 6 people. It's frustrating to hit tab and see the countless amounts of less than level 10s on your team and levels in hundreds on the other teams. Weapon imbalance is a huge issue. The team seems to be too afraid to touch stock weapons. It's fun to be rushed down by a scout that can do ~90 damage in one shot at a mid-ish range who also has 6 shots and can double/triple jump. Soldier and demo are also really fun to play against especially with damage surf.  Walking around the corner and getting hit by a rocket that launches you up helplessly into another rocket is standard for most games. Same with demoman, except he has a primary that can deal 4/5 of your health at any range with no damage fall off as long as it's a direct hit. He also has a secondary that has 8 shots that can deal up to 100 damage each. Demoknight also exists, which is a sub-class for the demoman that allows him to get close to you really quickly and two shot you. If he's using the right weapon he also has the ability to go mach speed while keeping up his resistances and still being able to two shot most classes. Map design is flawed, capping on Suijin is pretty difficult when there's an area above the point that is hard to get to unless you're a soldier and demo. Once one is up there it's extremely easy for them to spam down onto the point with explosives and there might as well be nothing you can do. It's hard to enjoy the game anymore. There's no matchmaking system, no weapon or class balancing, and the maps and the game in general isn't very well optimized. I spent a lot of money on this game but I think the thing I lost the most playing this game is time. The only way to enjoy this anymore is to play with your friends in a group.

This game is very good, here's why:
Pro's:
- The game is 9 years old, although it still gets constant updates.
- The game is Free To Play, you CAN pay for things, but you don't need to, as the stock/vanillla weapons are the best in the game and you can get virtually any item in the game through drops.
- The game has a LOT of gamemodes, not just CTF, PL etc, but also a LOT of custom community made ones.
- Speaking of the community, it is very alive and is trying to make the most of the game, although there are bad players, there are good players to make up for it.
- Some people say the game is dying, THIS IS NOT TRUE! The game is very well alive, it gets constant updates, the community is still out there and supports the game, the player count isn't that bad compared to previous years, averages: (When it started counting players, July 2012: 45,566.9) (When it was in it's "Golden State", June 2013: 50,739.9) (Present, April/May 2017: 51,179.2). Averages peaked at 60,778.7 and the players online at the same time peaked at 117,917.
-There is a wide variety in weapons, skins, hats and more.
- It's skill ceiling is very high, there's alot to learn, even for long-time players.
- Learning the game is hard but not that hard, mastering it is very hard, but can be fun. The community provides alot of guidance for learning how to play and master the game.
- The game can be serious but also fun, sometimes at the same time, there is a lot of things to do, such as being a friendly, taunting etc.
- The voice acting is MARVELOUS, it is so good and so funny sometimes
- The characters are very well "built" and are very funny sometimes.
- Sometimes you need a break, but if you come back, oh it feels good. The game pretty much is this good that it makes you come back for more if you uninstall
- There is just so much to do that there's almost no moment where you have nothing to do.
But with these pro's come cons:
- Although they do update the game, it can take ages for it to update, but the team tries very hard. Sometimes the updates dissapointing or game breaking, the team of course tries to fix the game breaking bug and almost always succeeds.
- Of course there are cheaters, although I personally don't see them to often, they are there. This game is very good, here's why:
Pro's:
- The game is 9 years old, although it still gets constant updates.
- The game is Free To Play, you CAN pay for things, but you don't need to, as the stock/vanillla weapons are the best in the game and you can get virtually any item in the game through drops.
- The game has a LOT of gamemodes, not just CTF, PL etc, but also a LOT of custom community made ones.
- Speaking of the community, it is very alive and is trying to make the most of the game, although there are bad players, there are good players to make up for it.
- Some people say the game is dying, THIS IS NOT TRUE! The game is very well alive, it gets constant updates, the community is still out there and supports the game, the player count isn't that bad compared to previous years, averages: (When it started counting players, July 2012: 45,566.9) (When it was in it's "Golden State", June 2013: 50,739.9) (Present, April/May 2017: 51,179.2). Averages peaked at 60,778.7 and the players online at the same time peaked at 117,917.
-There is a wide variety in weapons, skins, hats and more.
- It's skill ceiling is very high, there's alot to learn, even for long-time players.
- Learning the game is hard but not that hard, mastering it is very hard, but can be fun. The community provides alot of guidance for learning how to play and master the game.
- The game can be serious but also fun, sometimes at the same time, there is a lot of things to do, such as being a friendly, taunting etc.
- The voice acting is MARVELOUS, it is so good and so funny sometimes
- The characters are very well "built" and are very funny sometimes.
- Sometimes you need a break, but if you come back, oh it feels good. The game pretty much is this good that it makes you come back for more if you uninstall
- There is just so much to do that there's almost no moment where you have nothing to do.
But with these pro's come cons:
- Although they do update the game, it can take ages for it to update, but the team tries very hard. Sometimes the updates dissapointing or game breaking, the team of course tries to fix the game breaking bug and almost always succeeds.
- Of course there are cheaters, although I personally don't see them to often, they are there. Fortunately, sometimes players try to kick them and it happens, and of course they get banned most of the time. There are also ban waves, where there are a lot of hackers banned from the game. But of course, you can just create another account and start all over again as a hacker and there are no consequences.
- The game is semi-hard to learn and very hard to master, of course there are video's on how to learn and master the game.
- There are of course bad players in the game that troll, but for every bad player there are 2 good players. Sometimes the bad ones get kicked.
That's pretty much the jist of this game!
Maybe I missed some points, but this is pretty much the main bulk of it :p

TF2, In my very opinion is one of the greates ideas in the world. The mechanics and physcs of the game are just different, like rocket jumpin/stickyjumping, Scout's double jump. Having nine classes also means that you can be at least good at one class, and specialize in that class, meaning that the game could be playable for anyone. Also, having a variety of weapons means that you can change your playstyle anytime and you can be different from anyone else on the server. Plus you have hats, which define your personality. The community is  one of the bigger community, making new maps, new weapons, new gamemodes, changing the trading system in a way that you don't need to give 37$ for a virtual hat ect.
But when you DO get the game the first time, all you should remember is that yes, this is a Free To Play game, but that Free To Play part is like a demo. You get the full game in the F2P version of the game yes, but you don't get every feature. Say you cannot trade, or have hats other than like 4, you have very little inventory which means you won't be able to have all weapons. You have to pay money to get skins, unusuals, stranges ect. So please, after at least 60 hours of gameplay ( Which would Be About 1-3 Weeks) buy something cheap so you can get all the features and get into the game...

Most of the time in all of the servers there are at least 2-3 kiddos yelling at their mics at their country's language when they die (seriously though, search up some YT videos of TF2 kids, this community is getting more ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ than Minecraft's IMO) and some even cry. This is the 45% of the community, let me show you what the other 45% is. They are usually 12 year olds who buy the most expensive skins they can and farm kills at some server for random numbers on their weapon which makes them feel invulnerable. Now, if any of the♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥who are called friends of mine see this and comment/PM me "omg dont u remember last year that u were the same lmao", I wasn't totally like that, I was mostly using binds like Sensei Lenny and other ones, not farming kills on servers (hell, I haven't even really bought any StatClock weapons and if I did I sold them a month later and they didn't cost more than 2 euro) or anything. I took about a six month break from the game to do videos, and I come back to Team Fortress 2 to find it an appalling shambles. What was once a beautifully-balanced game has become a den of achievement ♥♥♥♥♥s and twinked-out, unbalanced characters. In the time I was away, Valve instituted a ton of character updates, adding X-Box Live style achievements to each class, and granting special weapons when a player got them.
The achievements themselves are hilariously over-specific, impossible to get during the course of normal gameplay. Naturally, the first thing everyone did was to set up achievement farms– servers tailor-made to facilitate the accomplishment of these achievements as quickly as possible. I’m torn between my dislike of farming achievements and the fact that I’ll never be competitive if I don’t go farming. Therein lies the problem: the game is no longer balanced, and the only way to compete is to become the very kind of achievement ♥♥♥♥♥ I hate. It goes against the whole spirit of achievements, like setting a home run record with the baseball on a tee, and then being rewarded with steroids.
The scouts are the worst right now. They were already borderline unbalanced before any updates, but now they’ve been granted a shotgun with knockback and enough damage to kill most characters in one hit, and the Sandman which can long-range stun any character for several seconds, even if they’ve been ubered by a medic. That’s just ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t. And of course, everyone and their brother is playing a scout now, so it’s not uncommon to see teams comprised almost entirely of Scouts– either maxed-out and bloodthirsty, or whoring themselves out for their own achievements.
It’s hard to explain if you’ve never played TF2, and to most of you it’s just going to sound like whining from a n00b. I’m just a believer in skill against skill. I don’t mind losing if it’s a fair fight. I played Counter-Strike for years, but I had to quit because of all the cheaters. I couldn’t be sure if I was losing because I was lousy at the game, or because people were cheating. TF2 used to be the kind of game where, as long as there weren’t any bad apples taking great pains to ruin everyone’s enjoyment, you could have a great time and be confident that the playing field was level. Now it’s rewarding achievement whoring and creating two classes of players. Casual players are no longer welcome, it seems.
TF2 is the munchkin’s playground now.
You can have it.

How to make chocolate cake
-----------------------------------------
Ingredients
1 cup white sugar
1 1/8 cups all-purpose flour
1/2 cup unsweetened cocoa powder
1 teaspoon baking soda
1 teaspoon salt
1/2 cup butter
1 egg
1 teaspoon vanilla extract
1 cup cold, strong, brewed coffee
Directions
Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease and flour an 8 inch pan. Sift together flour, cocoa, baking soda and salt. Set aside.
In a medium bowl, cream butter and sugar until light and fluffy. Add egg and vanilla and beat well. Add flour mixture, alternating with coffee. Beat until just incorporated.
Bake at 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) for 35 to 45 minutes, or until a toothpick inserted into the cake comes out clean.

Let's start.
Team Fortress 2 it's a FPS (First Person Shooter) game made by Valve and published in 2007, after the beta. The game has nine classes:
ATTACK CLASSES:
°Scout
°Soldier
°Pyro
DEFENSE CLASSES:
°Demoman
°Heavy
°Engineer
SUPPORT CLASSES.
°Medic
°Sniper
°Spy
Each class has his advantages and disadvantages. For example a Spy can kill easily a Heavy, but at the same time he can be get killed by a Pyro. Or a Scout can kill without problem a Sniper or an Engineer, but at the same time he can be killed by Demomen or Soldiers.
This system of advantages and disadvantages makes the game very funny.
The game has also a drop system, which allows to find randomly new weapons and, if lucky, new hats. Infact the game has a lot of weapons, which can be unlocked with achievements (Example: The Force-A-Nature) or can be picked randomly during a game. Each weapons has his own advantages and disadvantages, making the game balanced. For example the Phlogistinator, a Pyro weapon, can gain easily crits but it can't use the compressor (which is essential for airblasting projectiles).
The game has also a lot of hats, which makes Team Fortress 2 a original FPS. The player can use the hats for customizing his own character. Hats can be purchased by the Mann. Co Store or being traded for refined metal (Which is the "money" of the game).
The game has also a trading system, which allows players to trade weapons and hats, keeping the "TF2 economy" alive.
Now let's see what it is inside the game!
Team Fortress 2 has a lot of gamemodes, for example Attack/Defense or Capture the Flag.
In Attack/Defense the BLU must cap every RED's point. The BLU will win if they will cap every point before the time expires, otherwise the RED will win.
The TF2 community is always active, expecially on trading, but I don't refuse to say that in the community there are some disrispectful and discriminating people, often following the ideology "You have no hats? You're a noob!". Beside this the community is quite friendly.
Now my personal opinion:
I play this game since 23 May 2014 and it never tired me. I enjoy playing this game because it's wonderful how you can meet new friends and working with them for win the match. Every character has his own stereotype, and this make me laugh (in positive sense, of course).
I think Team Fortress 2 was born as team-working FPS and not "I'm the most pro player in the game!11". And that is just wonderful.
I say thanks to Valve and thanks to Gaben for making this fantastic game, which is my favorite.
Thanks a lot.
FINAL VOTE:
Gameplay: 10/10
Sounds and music: 9/10
Graphic: 9/10 (It's quite old but I like that style)

Team Fortress 2 has a key word in the name, team, that means it requires some team play. Using Z, X, and C you can call out commands to your team and try to get them to help, move, build something, or go a direction. Even though the graphics are more cartoon-ish, there is a good amount of blood when shot, cut, hit, or blown to bits. Take these into consideration before playing. Do I recommend this game? I think it's time that I put my foot down when it comes to TF2. Apparently Valve is obsessed with the inability to ADS, which is annoying. The default sniper rifle is horrific and kills only with around 3 or 4 consecutive shots to the chest. It makes for a pretty much useless weapon and I think it should be buffed to at least make the weapon useable. The spy is useless unless your enemies are blind, deaf, and stupid, the demoman has a sticky grenade launcher, which excited me. I use it, and it doesn't stick to enemies. Apparently you are supposed to sit out the whole match and wait until some unsuspecting scout walks by to press the left mouse key and do pretty much no damage to them. You may be unfamiliar with the classes, so I'll fill you in. The scout is faster than the other classes, can double jump, and dies much slower than he should considering these two traits. The pyro is for players who hate aiming. The engineer is for players who hate playing. The soldier is "cannon fodder" that can take two rpg shots to the chest. The heavy is a friggin tank that can take a sniper shot to the head. The medic is the class everyone likes, but no one uses. The spy is who no one likes, but everyone uses just to shank you in the butt. The demoman is pretty much useless due to both of his explosives having a delayed fuse and one having to be remotely detonated. Finally, the sniper. The sniper is pathetic. He has an extremely weak weapon, and frankly I would rather use the demoman. His guns are weak, his health is extremely low, and he can't move for crap. The main good part about this game is the deathrun mode and the mode with grappling hooks. I had great fun shooting a hook onto a person's face, springing towards them, and just watching from atop their head as they looked aroung to see why they were losing health. The game is fun, although the classes suck. And the maps are fresh, although they're all corners and are h3ll for snipers. Overall, this game is a good starting point for fps players and is great for a free-to-play, but just lacks the right classes for the job.

Team Fortress constantly creating new maps and new weapons. However, it's not enough to keep people interested in the game after a long constant playing in it.

Team Fortress 2, (TF2) is a very competitive and fast online or offline shooter which does not need too much of your time to play. Sometimes I will admit it is hard not to play for long periods of time, but you can quit anytime you must or want to. This game is free to download which means that they will have many items that you must buy, I fell into the ways of buying for a short time myself... it's hard not to when some things on the Community Market are only ten cents to a dollar. While playing there is rarely any language to worry about from the games part, on the other hand do not trust other players all the time. Some have dirty mouths and you will not be able to stop from really seeing it off of chat. If it is on a mic I highly suggest muting the player. Team Fortress 2 has a key word in the name, team, that means it requires some team play. Using Z, X, and C you can call out commands to your team and try to get them to help, move, build something, or go a direction. Even though the graphics are more cartoon-ish, there is a good amount of blood when shot, cut, hit, or blown to bits. Take these into consideration before playing. Do I recommend this game? Absolutely, for childern +14.

This is without a doubt the most entertaining game I have ever found. I'm not one for long story quests, the very thought of grinding away while searching for loot to wear makes me want to scream out in despair. I just don't have the patience for those games. This game is different from those and other shooter games in that it has 9 classes to choose from, each one with major differences. My favorite happens to be the soldier. Each of the classes is very different from the last and you have three basic elements at play. Fire, Explosives and Bullets. I know that may sound boring but they vary the classes enough that it feels completely different playing as a demoman or soldier. Each has their tricks, despite both being explosive. I suppose it was also the fairness which I liked. You do not pay to win in this game. My unusual rocket launcher is no different from the newbies stock rocket launcher. It does the same thing. That is critical for making a fun and balanced environment. I'll probably never quit this game. Come join me!

So this game has been consuming my life for the past 3 years, so I finally decided to write a review of it.
Now, the core of this game, the very fundamentals, the "vanilla" game, is very enjoyable. It is for anyone, I believe. But this game has so much more to it. There are thousands of whacky, crazy, and weird mods, maps and memes in this game, and to be completley honest, the majority of it really really sucks. Like really.
There are so amazingly many ♥♥♥♥♥♥ memes in this game that it's nearly tear-jerking.
You can connect to a random server and find everyone re-skinned as mlp characters and there is terrible music playing at 400 desibel in the background, while 31 out of the 32 players on the servers are screaming in to the all-talk chat and you decide after a fraction of a second that coming here was the worst idea of your life.
Or perhaps you get on a vanilla server where your team is stacked with one class, and everyone is playing like they are using their feet.
Maybe you connect to a server where whenever you try to type something in the chat, your message drowns in the countless messages from people trying to trade their ♥♥♥♥♥♥ items for ♥♥♥♥♥♥ prices.
But that's kind of the charm of this game. It has something for everyone. Maybe you find great fun in the wacky mods and maps, or maybe you are entertainted by simply relaxing in a valve pub server, playing casually. You might find joy in taking the game to the next level and moving over to the amazing competetive side of this game. (Which i strongly recommend to anyone intrested in this game)
No matter what kind of person you are, there is a place for you. A class for you. This game has something for everyone.
But please just for the love of god stay the ♥♥♥♥ away from the ♥♥♥♥♥♥ weaboo mlp servers, this cancer needs to die out.

An addictive gaming experince put into 15 mb, Team Fortress 2 is a game that has (mostly), everything, an great gameplay, unorthodox design and constant updates to keep you coming back for more. The casual gameplay in a game of tf2 still requires you to have a basic element of team work to win. But if you don't feel like playing, don't worry ! You can just be a box and walk around the map or keep dancing in your spawn room  with the finest of taunts to ever to exist in a video game.The casual gameplay of tf2 is enough to keep anyone addicted to the game for months. But, if you want to get better and playing the game, competitive game mode is for you. Competitive tf2 relies heavily on team co-ordination and your understanding of the class your playing and its role. it relies a lot on your understanding of the game itself and how it's played, providing a whole new experince.
However, it is not without it's faults. There are a considerable amount of bugs in the game.But , these bugs are constantly being fixed because of tf2's dedicated community and the dev team.

Put on your hats, strap on your rocket launchers, and prepare to fight it out in Team Fortress 2, a fast-paced, action-packed, and comical team-based first person shooter from the makers of Half-Life 2. Take your pick from nine comical classes, each with their own unique personalities and tactical uses, including a one-eyed, heavy-drinking Scotsman, a mentally unstable pyromaniac, and a host of other wacky characters. Take part in eight different game modes, including classic modes such as Capture the Flag, King of the Hill, and Deathmatch, along with unique scenarios like Medieval and Payload.
Hilarious and Wacky Characters – very creative characters with awesome lines that keep the game entertaining and lighthearted.
Awesome Maps – run around on well-designed maps that truly enhance the gameplay of this MMO shooter. Has open spaces, plenty of cover, and brilliant zones of battle.
Masterful Gameplay – not only is the game balanced extremely well, but the gameplay itself is tastefully done with familiar shooter controls and a good variety of classes.
Achievements – an achievement system keeps the replay value high, as players will want to strive to unlock and meet the challenges.
Great Tutorial System – players will ease right into the game with the help of a great tutorial system, where they will experience each class and the gameplay bits at a time.

A war-themed hat simulator, Team Fortress 2, one of the most well know FPS, and quite a fun game to play.
The game has 9 classes, divided into 3 groups, Offence, Defence, and Support.
I'll be telling you all the classes, with a brief description, and their weapons starting with Primary, Secondary, Melee, and PDAs, if the class has them.
Scout (Offence) - The fastest base speed character in the game, with a downfall being his low health (125), taking out enemies in a flash. His default weapons include the Scattergun, Pistol, and Bat. The Scattergun is capable of doing high damage in close range. The Pistol is quite good for cleaning up enemies if your Scattergun runs out of ammo, or clip. It has a much better accuracy than the Scattergun, but does lack the damage. All the stock melees are almost the same (Engineer, Spy), so I'll tell you if they change for a class.
Soldier (Offence) - Little to no aim needed, and high mobility (but slower walking speed), and 200 health. His default weapons include the Rocket Launcher, Shotgun, and Shovel. The Rocket Launcher is a 100% accurate projectile, dealing splash damage to where ever it lands. If you take time to learn, Rocket Jumping is how you'll mainly get around a map. The Shotgun is basically the same as the Scattergun.
Pyro (Offence) - Holding down W+MOUSE1, and taking out the entire enemy team, with 175 health. Their weapons being the Flamethrower, Shotgun, and Fire Axe. The Flamethrower has a short attack range, but makes up with high DPS, set the enemy on fire, and being able to deny enemy attacks. If you press MOUSE2, you can blast any enemy, and projectile back the other way, and put out your team mates.
Demoman (Defense) - The "skilled" demolition, setting traps, and being able to Sticky Jump (but has slow speed to counter), with 175 health. His weapons being the Grenade Launcher, Sticky Bomb Launcher, and Bottle. The Grenade Launcher is a projectile which can be bounced off walls to blow up the enemy. The Sticky Bomb Launcher is a projectile which can create traps around hallways, or around corners.
Heavy (Defense) - High health (300), slowest speed, high DPS. The Heavy Weapons Guy has the Minigun, Shotgun, and Fists. The Minigun is like the Flamethrower, however has a much longer range, and can mow down anyone in seconds.
Engineer (Defense) - The Texan Genius, creating buildings to help your team, and destroy the other team, and 125 health. His weapons are uniqe. He has the Shotgun, Pistol, Wrench, Construction PDA, and Destruction PDA. The Wrench is capable to upgrade and repair your buildings and fellow Engineers' buildings. The Construction PDA allows you to build your buildings, while the Destruction PDA destroys them. You can build a Sentry to kill the enemy team, a Dispenser to heal your team, and Teleporters to transport you and your team.
Medic (Support) - German madman, a healing machine, with 150 health. His weapons include the Syringe Gun, Medigun, and Bonesaw. The Syringe Gun is a low range Pistol, with less accuracy too. The Medigun, by pressing and holding MOUSE1, can heal teammates AND enemy Spies. If you heal long enough in 1 life, you can activate your Uber with MOUSE2, which makes you and your target teammate invulnerable for a few seconds. Best used to push the frontlines.
Sniper (Support) - Shooting enemies from afar, away from harm, with 125 health. His weapons include the Sniper Rifle, SMG, and Kukuri. The Sniper Rifle can be charged to instantly kill an enemy with a headshot, regardless of overheal. The SMG is the same as the Pistol.
Spy (Support) - Using trickery to sneak behind the enemy, with 125 health. His weapons include the Revolver, Butterfly Knife, Invis Watch, Sapper, and Disquise Kit. The Revolver is good to deal chip damage, or kill from a safe enough distance. The Butterfly Knife is his melee, being able to instantly kill from behind their backs. The Invis Watch makes the Spy completely invisible to the enemy team for a few seconds, which can be activated by pressing MOUSE2. The Sapper is capable of disabling and destroying a Sentry Gun if left alone. However Engineers can take off the Sapper, so it's best to kill them first. The Disquise Kit is how you can walk infront of the enemy (and Sentry Guns), and (hopefully, you still need to trick the enemy into believing you're their teammate) not get shot.
That sums up the classes. Now there are 5 main game modes that you should know of. Attack/Defense, where Blu team tries to captures all of Red's points. Capture the Flag, pretty self explanatory. Control Points, where each team tries to capture the other teams' points. King of the Hill, where one team holds one point for a total of 3 minutes. And then Payload, where Blu pushes a bomb to the enemy teams' final point, unless Red can stop them.
This, what I just explained, is the Free to Play aspect of the game. If you purchase something from the Mann Co. Store (DO NOT PURCHASE WEAPONS FROM HERE. All weapons in the game can be obtained free of charge if you play long enough), you can become premium, and be able to play Competetive, obtain rarer items from the item drop system, play Mann Up mode in Mann Vs. Machines, and more.
This concludes The Team Fortress 2 Free to Play Guide... wait this is a review... Anyways, hope you enjoy Team Fortress 2. Of course words can't perfectly explain the game. So you should play it and see how you enjoy it.

A war-themed hat simulator, Team Fortress 2, one of the most well know FPS, and quite a fun game to play.
The game has 9 classes, divided into 3 groups, Offence, Defence, and Support.
I'll be telling you all the classes, with a brief description, and their weapons starting with Primary, Secondary, Melee, and PDAs, if the class has them.
Scout (Offence) - The fastest base speed character in the game, with a downfall being his low health (125), taking out enemies in a flash. His default weapons include the Scattergun, Pistol, and Bat. The Scattergun is capable of doing high damage in close range. The Pistol is quite good for cleaning up enemies if your Scattergun runs out of ammo, or clip. It has a much better accuracy than the Scattergun, but does lack the damage. All the stock melees are almost the same (Engineer, Spy), so I'll tell you if they change for a class.
Soldier (Offence) - Little to no aim needed, and high mobility (but slower walking speed), and 200 health. His default weapons include the Rocket Launcher, Shotgun, and Shovel. The Rocket Launcher is a 100% accurate projectile, dealing splash damage to where ever it lands. If you take time to learn, Rocket Jumping is how you'll mainly get around a map. The Shotgun is basically the same as the Scattergun.
Pyro (Offence) - Holding down W+MOUSE1, and taking out the entire enemy team, with 175 health. Their weapons being the Flamethrower, Shotgun, and Fire Axe. The Flamethrower has a short attack range, but makes up with high DPS, set the enemy on fire, and being able to deny enemy attacks. If you press MOUSE2, you can blast any enemy, and projectile back the other way, and put out your team mates.
Demoman (Defense) - The "skilled" demolition, setting traps, and being able to Sticky Jump (but has slow speed to counter), with 175 health. His weapons being the Grenade Launcher, Sticky Bomb Launcher, and Bottle. The Grenade Launcher is a projectile which can be bounced off walls to blow up the enemy. The Sticky Bomb Launcher is a projectile which can create traps around hallways, or around corners.
Heavy (Defense) - High health (300), slowest speed, high DPS. The Heavy Weapons Guy has the Minigun, Shotgun, and Fists. The Minigun is like the Flamethrower, however has a much longer range, and can mow down anyone in seconds.
Engineer (Defense) - The Texan Genius, creating buildings to help your team, and destroy the other team, and 125 health. His weapons are uniqe. He has the Shotgun, Pistol, Wrench, Construction PDA, and Destruction PDA. The Wrench is capable to upgrade and repair your buildings and fellow Engineers' buildings. The Construction PDA allows you to build your buildings, while the Destruction PDA destroys them. You can build a Sentry to kill the enemy team, a Dispenser to heal your team, and Teleporters to transport you and your team.
Medic (Support) - German madman, a healing machine, with 150 health. His weapons include the Syringe Gun, Medigun, and Bonesaw. The Syringe Gun is a low range Pistol, with less accuracy too. The Medigun, by pressing and holding MOUSE1, can heal teammates AND enemy Spies. If you heal long enough in 1 life, you can activate your Uber with MOUSE2, which makes you and your target teammate invulnerable for a few seconds. Best used to push the frontlines.
Sniper (Support) - Shooting enemies from afar, away from harm, with 125 health. His weapons include the Sniper Rifle, SMG, and Kukuri. The Sniper Rifle can be charged to instantly kill an enemy with a headshot, regardless of overheal. The SMG is the same as the Pistol.
Spy (Support) - Using trickery to sneak behind the enemy, with 125 health. His weapons include the Revolver, Butterfly Knife, Invis Watch, Sapper, and Disquise Kit. The Revolver is good to deal chip damage, or kill from a safe enough distance. The Butterfly Knife is his melee, being able to instantly kill from behind their backs. The Invis Watch makes the Spy completely invisible to the enemy team for a few seconds, which can be activated by pressing MOUSE2. The Sapper is capable of disabling and destroying a Sentry Gun if left alone. However Engineers can take off the Sapper, so it's best to kill them first. The Disquise Kit is how you can walk infront of the enemy (and Sentry Guns), and (hopefully, you still need to trick the enemy into believing you're their teammate) not get shot.
That sums up the classes. Now there are 5 main game modes that you should know of. Attack/Defense, where Blu team tries to captures all of Red's points. Capture the Flag, pretty self explanatory. Control Points, where each team tries to capture the other teams' points. King of the Hill, where one team holds one point for a total of 3 minutes. And then Payload, where Blu pushes a bomb to the enemy teams' final point, unless Red can stop them.
This, what I just explained, is the Free to Play aspect of the game. If you purchase something from the Mann Co. Store (DO NOT PURCHASE WEAPONS FROM HERE. All weapons in the game can be obtained free of charge if you play long enough), you can become premium, and be able to play Competetive, obtain rarer items from the item drop system, play Mann Up mode in Mann Vs. Machines, and more.
This concludes The Team Fortress 2 Free to Play Guide... wait this is a review... Anyways, hope you enjoy Team Fortress 2. Of course words can't perfectly explain the game. So you should play it and see how you enjoy it.

It's free, so you might as well try it.
Aside from that, I haven't sunk over 500 hours into this for the hell of it. This became my go-to casual game for 4 years, and remains one of my favourites. The P2P elements can seem daunting at first, yet there is absolutely no need to invest any money at all into this game for you to enjoy yourself. And trust me, you most definitely will.
Pros:
+The classes are amongst the best designed in gaming. Each feels needed and distinct from the others, and are all great fun to play as.
+The sheer amount of gameplay to be had, both Valve-made and Community developed is massive!
+The events and updates are a great way to keep coming back for more.
+Great free source of entertainment for yourself and friends.
+The weapons are all balanced extremely well.
+The map design is up there with the best, with classics like 2Fort becoming immediately memorable.
+Different weapon sets mean classes have multiple playstyles to suit how you like to play.
+Community is usually very helpful and willing to help new players along.
+Playing with people you know is an absolute blast.
+Thankfully investing money gives you no gameplay edge over players who don't.
+Conga.
Cons:
-Non-event gameplay can get samey if you overdo the main modes.
-Community is occasionaly♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥to F2Ps (you will learn the importance of hats).
-It can be difficult at first to take down skilled players, particularly as the Spy.
-Mannpower mode still makes absolutely no sense.
-Gibus.
At the end of the day, the pros FAR outweigh the cons. This is a damn fine game to play by yourself, but with a group of friends, this is easily one of the best games on Steam.

It's free, so you might as well try it.
Aside from that, I haven't sunk over 500 hours into this for the hell of it. This became my go-to casual game for 4 years, and remains one of my favourites. The P2P elements can seem daunting at first, yet there is absolutely no need to invest any money at all into this game for you to enjoy yourself. And trust me, you most definitely will.
Pros:
+The classes are amongst the best designed in gaming. Each feels needed and distinct from the others, and are all great fun to play as.
+The sheer amount of gameplay to be had, both Valve-made and Community developed is massive!
+The events and updates are a great way to keep coming back for more.
+Great free source of entertainment for yourself and friends.
+The weapons are all balanced extremely well.
+The map design is up there with the best, with classics like 2Fort becoming immediately memorable.
+Different weapon sets mean classes have multiple playstyles to suit how you like to play.
+Community is usually very helpful and willing to help new players along.
+Playing with people you know is an absolute blast.
+Thankfully investing money gives you no gameplay edge over players who don't.
+Conga.
Cons:
-Non-event gameplay can get samey if you overdo the main modes.
-Community is occasionaly♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥to F2Ps (you will learn the importance of hats).
-It can be difficult at first to take down skilled players, particularly as the Spy.
-Mannpower mode still makes absolutely no sense.
-Gibus.
At the end of the day, the pros FAR outweigh the cons. This is a damn fine game to play by yourself, but with a group of friends, this is easily one of the best games on Steam.

Don't get me wrong, I love TF2. It's a great game. I still play often but some things are really dragging down the experience. Number one: Cheaters. Like many other shooters (especially F2P ones) TF2 suffers from a bit of a cheating problem. While most are generally kicked quickly, I've seen an influx in cheater "groups". These guys are complete♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ They go around the servers in groups, kicking anyone who calls them out on their BS and just pockets the cheater. These aren't too common, neither are cheaters in general, but the problem is still there.
2. I can never find balanced or full games. Most of the time there are only about 10 people in a game (this varies, maybe I'm just unlucky) and it really hurts the experience. The balance issue is also pretty bad. Weapon balance, aint too bad, it's team balance I'm talking about. You'll get a group of very skilled, experienced players, against a team of new players (with a few unlucky decent people). These matches are usually just a slaughter and not fun to play, even for the winning team, as there is little to no challenge.
3.The game is unoptimized. I have a Intel I5 6600K 3.5GHZ, a Nvidia GTX 1060 6GB and 32GB of RAM, and you're telling me I can't run this game at 60FPS? (This varies from person to person so don't take this point too seriously).
You should give the game a go, see how you go on. If you don't have any problems, and you enjoy it then good for you man/women/whatever. Just don't expect a perfect game. I love this game. but I can't give it a really positive review.

Team Fortress 2 is hands down the best free to play fps game. It is a game that is easy to pick up but hard to master. Having nine classes with different playstyles combined with many unlockable weapons you should never be bored playing this game. Amazingly the classes and weapons are mostly balanced and there are really no straight upgrades. The f2p model is good with cosmetics being the only thing you should really need to pay for.
I love the graphical style of this game. The pastel look makes seeing important information (class, weapons, objectives) really easy compared to more realistic graphic styles. It also contributes to how silly this game can be.
The classes are all unique with different personalities and good voice acting. Watch Meet The Classes to get a good idea about that sort of thing.
In short this game has kept me involved for multiple years without dissappointment. What do you have to lose, it's free!

Despite that i buy things for TF2 occasionally simply because it gave me so many hours of pure fun! It feels incredibly polished and maintains a near perfect balance which is astonishing if you think about how diverse the 9 classes are. To sum it up as best i can: You don't just play TF2 to see some number (your level) rise. Unlocking new weapons is fun because of the variety they bring to the game but you certainly don't play it to unlock the "best" weapons because the stock weapons may very well be the "best" ones in the game. You don't play it because there is a big message on the screen telling you that you are awesome after every kill. You simply play it for pure, old fashion FUN! It's Team Fortress 2. It's awesome. As a consequence people who dislike Team Fortress 2 truly ARE idiots- of course they wouldn’t appreciate, for instance, the humour in Engineer’s existential catchphrase “THAT PYRO IS A SPY!”, which itself is a cryptic reference to Demoman’s Scottish epic Fathers and Sons. I’m smirking right now just imagining one of those addlepated simpletons scratching their heads in confusion as Gabe Newell’s genius wit unfolds itself on their television screens. What fools.. how I pity them.
And yes, by the way, i DO have a TF2 tattoo. And no, you cannot see it. It’s for the ladies’ eyes only- and even then they have to demonstrate that they’re within 5 IQ points of my own (preferably lower) beforehand. Nothin personal kid.

Unlike other "class-based" games that offer a variety of combat classes only, Team Fortress 2 packs a wild variety of classes which provide a broad range of tactical abilities and personalities, and lend themselves to a variety of player skills. Play as the flame-throwing Pyro, the room clearing Heavy, or the Spy, a master of disguises. Other classes include: Scout, Sniper, Medic, Engineer, Demoman, or Soldier.
Team Fortress 2 was first included with the release of Half-Life 2's Orange Box. Now, each game from that pack is available as its own boxed title for gamers to pick and choose their favorites.

TF2 is a great game with perfect balancing, classes, and gameplay. It is fun and has a variety of gameplay so you never bored playing the same game. I personally have 500+ hours into it and I still get excited everyday to play this game. Now there will be times where you will think you suck while the other team is destroying you, dont give up. There is a chance that you will get Random Crits, a medic, or even a teamwork team in the next game. The community maps are phenominal and every single one I have played on was full of activity, there will be people who mic spam but you can use that mute button for good use. Now, you do not need to buy anything, I cannot stress that enough because you get all of the weapons for free by just playing the game. Most of the items are cosmetics or guns that make your eyes go crazy but all you really need is the weapons. People think that if they dont buy anything they dont feel like they are a part of the community, which in fact they are. Free 2 Play is a thing I have wanted to do from day one just to show F2P's aren't always noobs who dont know how to play the game. I of course bought things because I thought it would be so cool for my scout to have a hoodie, but then I got bored and bought more cosmetics. All I have to say is, have fun, play fair, and dont feel like you are left out not buying things. Be the first person who plays this game for 1000+ hours with only the weapons you find and we will all praise you.

Only in TF2 can you beat someone to death with a Ham Hock and then point and laugh at them during the Killcam. Only in TF2 can you wear 5 hats and russian dance infront of the enemy. Team Fortress 2 may not be techniqly superior to any games, nor graphically; but thats not the point, and it never was the point. The point is and always will be how much fun you can have with a free game.

At a first glance, one might think that Team Fortress 2 (referred to as TF2), is a completely and utterly stupid game and should never be played. Sure, throwing urine at people and then sniping them (sometimes at the same time) might sound a little strange, but it's exceptionally fun to do. Seriously.
Who WOULDN'T like a Bostonian running around shouting random remarks at the other team? He also throws milk at people and hits people with baseball bats.
The embodiment of America, this completely insane Not-Actually-A-Soldier is often found firing off rockets and hitting people with shovels. He also can fire rockets his feet to jump very high. Then he hits people with shovels.
This class is of the great unknown. No one knows what they look like. No one knows what sex/gender they are. No one knows what they're saying half the time, but despite all these attributes, the Pyro can still set people on fire. Which may or may not be a good thing.
The master of explosives (and swords...?) can fire off explosive pills (PILLS HERE) that do exactly what's on the tin; explode. Luckily, he's also got spiked bombs that he can remotely detonate. What could make this class any better? He's drunk.
The face of TF2, he is a giant. He's got a minigun, a shotgun, and his fists (which do the same amount of damage as a fire axe), so he's pretty indestructible. Oh, and he can replace his shotgun for a sandwich. What a great trade!
This Texan places down a sentry that is basically a mix of the Heavy's minigun, and the Soldier's rocket launcher. He can also make a vending machine that will heal, give ammo, and block enemy players. AND THERE'S MORE! He can also place down teleporters that can get teammates to the front lines quickly. Tip: do NOT teleport bread. Especially for three days.
This German mad scientist has a tendency to shoot people with syringes to make them die. Or to heal his teammates. Or to heal himself. It doesn't really matter what he does, but he'll do it FOR SCIENCE. Also, he has a big old tube that heals people for no cost. After a bit of time, it will be able to initiate GOD MODE *cough* I mean the Übercharge, which prevents all incoming damage.
The Australian who is actually from New Zealand, The Sniper shoots people in the head with his sniper rifle, and if that doesn't kill them, shoots them with an SMG. And if THAT doesn't work, he throws urine at them, then cuts them with a Kukri that for some reason can do more damage then his sniper rifle. Overall, he's a pretty cool guy.
Espionage has never been simpler, when you can
Overall, this game is a blast. Literally and metaphorically. I recommend this to anyone and everyone who plays on Steam. If you don't play on Steam, make an account, download Steam, download TF2, and then play TF2. It's pretty simple.
