TL:DR: It's an amazing game with a pretty easy difficulty curve and an enmourmous skill ceiling. It is technically FTP but the cosmetics, weapons (you get around random weapon drops a week), and some other things need to be bought with cash.
I've been playing Tf2 for a long time, but I've still got so much to learn. Sure I can dominate a pub or two but when faced with people high above me skill wise I can just crumple. Tf2 is a complicated game but the mechanics are only in depth if you want them to be. Meaning that you don't really need to know the specifics of an item to haul♥♥♥♥♥with it, you only need to get in-depth if you want to do better.
There are a stunning amount of maps, I know around 20 off the top of my head, there are technically around 60ish maps, but only around half are in constant use. There are usually seasonal updates as well as periodical major updates. There are 9 classes, and each have a vast array of primary, seconday, and meelee weapons.
Back to the skill ceiling, almost all of the classes have a certain aspect or aspects that require a vast amount of skill. For example if you're running a puff and sting pyro (degreaser, reserve shooter, and axtinguisher normally) it is possible to crit an enemy pyro if your timing is godlike.
Overall, the game is fun and varied and for around $20-$50 you could get all the cosmetics/weapons you normally need, just keep in mind to get the really rare (but also fortunately completely cosmetic and unessisary) unusual hats, proffesional killestreak weapons, and australium skins, along with a large array of other expensive items, it will cost you a ♥♥♥♥ ton.
Basically even if you don't think you will like it give it 20 hours and you might change your mind. This games is rad.

Not too sure what to write here so here's a recipe for Pancakes instead
Ingredients:
1 1/2 cups all-purpose flour
3 tablespoons sugar
1 tablespoon baking powder
1/4 teaspoon salt
1/8 teaspoon freshly ground nutmeg
2 large eggs, at room temperature
1 1/4 cups milk, at room temperature
1/2 teaspoon pure vanilla extract
3 tablespoons unsalted butter, plus more as needed
Now to make it
1. In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, sugar, baking powder, salt, and nutmeg.
2. In another bowl, beat the eggs and then whisk in the milk and vanilla.
3. Melt the butter in a large cast iron skillet or griddle over medium heat.
4. Whisk the butter into the milk mixture. Add the wet ingredients to the flour mixture, and whisk until a thick batter is just formed
5. Keeping the skillet at medium heat, ladle about 1/4 cup of the batter onto the skillet, to make a pancake. Make 1 or 2 more pancakes, taking care to keep them evenly spaced apart. Cook, until bubbles break the surface of the pancakes, and the undersides are golden brown, about 2 minutes. Flip with a spatula and cook about 1 minute more on the second side. Serve immediately or transfer to a platter and cover loosely with foil to keep warm. Repeat with the remaining batter, adding more butter to the skillet as needed.
6. Procedure for adding fruit to pancakes: Once the bubbles break the surface of the pancakes, scatter the surface with sliced or diced fruit, or chocolate chips, nuts, etc. Flip with a spatula and cook for 1 minute more, being careful not to burn toppings.

Team Fortress 2 is a first-person shooter with cartoon-like characters, but realistic maps. I reccomend doing the training before playing, it helps. It has 3 game modes: Offline, Multiplayer, Mann VS Machine. Mann VS Machine is where you, and other people are set to fight robots, the robots' goal is to place a bomb in your base. If the robots do deploy the bomb, you lose and need to start over. There are nine characters, with each different traits. There is a vote menu, and voice menu, but the vote menu is very serious, however the voice menu is not. Two of the voice menus have characters' names. Those to names are: Medic, and Spy. Calling Medic means you are on low health and you need to be healed, calling Spy means that there is a Spy which you need to look out for. Ways to find a spy is: Listen for strange noises, and for "Spy's sappin' my [Building]!" and basicly for anybody on your team calling Spy.

If your looking for a review on this game you've come to the wrong place, but if your looking for an outstanding pie recipe you've come to the right place.
Ingredients:
1. 6 tablespoons unsalted butter
2. 1/2 cup white sugar
3. 1/2 cup brown sugar
4. 1/4 cup water
5. 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon
6. 1 pinch salt
7. 5 apples - peeled, cored and sliced
8. 1 pastry for double-crust pie
Directions:
1. Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
2. Combine butter, white sugar, brown sugar, water, cinnamon, and salt in a saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a boil, remove from heat and set aside.
3. Roll out half the pastry to fit a 9-inch pie plate. Place bottom crust in pie plate; pour in apple slices.
4. Roll out top crust into a 10-inch circle. Cut into 8 (1-inch) wide strips with a sharp paring knife or pastry wheel. Weave the pastry strips, one at a time, into a lattice pattern. Fold the ends of the lattice strips under the edge of the bottom crust and crimp to seal.
5. Pour butter-sugar mixture over top of pie, coating the lattice, and allowing any remaining sauce to drizzle through the crust.
6. Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and bake until the crust is golden brown, the caramel on the top crust is set, and the apple filling is bubbling, 35 to 40 more minutes. Allow to cool completely before slicing.
Eat.

Team Fortress 2 is a first-person shooter with cartoon-like characters, but realistic maps. I reccomend doing the training before playing, it helps. It has 3 game modes: Offline, Multiplayer, Mann VS Machine. Mann VS Machine is where you, and other people are set to fight robots, the robots' goal is to place a bomb in your base. If the robots do deploy the bomb, you lose and need to start over. There are nine characters, with each different traits. There is a vote menu, and voice menu, but the vote menu is very serious, however the voice menu is not. Two of the voice menus have characters' names. Those to names are: Medic, and Spy. Calling Medic means you are on low health and you need to be healed, calling Spy means that there is a Spy which you need to look out for. Ways to find a spy is: Listen for strange noises, and for "Spy's sappin' my [Building]!" and basicly for anybody on your team calling Spy.

Team Fortress 2
What a wonderfly crafted game.
This game is so addicting ive already "wasted" over a thousand hours of my life playing this masterpiece.
There are 9 balanced classes each with their own interesting strategy. Mastering each of these takes time and patience.
My 2 favorites, Sniper and Demoman, each have a very different playing style.
Sniper sits back and picks enemies off from a distance, he has the ability to hit a powerful critical hit on his enemies just by landing a headshot. Its a wonderful feeling hearing the ding seeing that 150-450 fly over the poor sucker as you pop his head with lead.
Demoman has the most diverse capibilities out of every class. He can be an explosive specialist or a sword wielding samurai. His sticky bomb launcher has one of the highest dps rates in the game. The notorious M1+M2 can tear through any defence, sentries, heavy medic peirs and can even stop an uber in its tracks. As a demo-knight he has great defensive and offensive power. He can charge through a crowd and take an enemy out with a single hit and live with most of his health.
There are also unlockable weapons.
These are earned through achievements or after every 45 minutes or so of play. Each weapon, just like the classes, is balanced, with the exception of a few junk weapons and some overpowered weapons *cough* *cough* gunslinger. These can add alot of diversity to your game and make it just that bit more unpredictable.
There are many gamemodes and maps that each have something great or terrible about them. My favorite map is King of the hill_Harvest. Its a map that has something for every class and is always a joy to play. Koth_Nucleus is great as well, the close combat fighting makes each battle more intense.
Finially, hats.
Team Fortress 2 also has another name granted by its community: Hat Simulator.

Pros -
* It's very diverse, using unique gameplay mechanics and other gamemodes to make it say "I am not like those other    hundred thousand FPS's, look this way".
* People complain a lot about the game's balance, myself included, but when you think about it, with that many weapons and nine different classes, I think they balanced counters, weaknesses, strengths, and gameplay style very well.
* Each class has completely different styles to master, and each class has many weapons that can change the way you play it. Usually with COD or other FPS's most of the guns don't really matter because there's that one overpowered weapon in each class or maybe two, but all the weapons can be used is some unique way, most of the time.
* Like I said, the game focuses on being diverse and unique, both of which are represented in the many weapons. Theres a medi gun, which heals targets, for god's sake. You'd think you would usually find like a bandaider as a medic but valve took the medic and made him stand out. Same with the other classes.
* Many more reasons lots of people will tell you

Sniper sits back and picks enemies off from a distance, he has the ability to hit a powerful critical hit on his enemies just by landing a headshot. Its a wonderful feeling hearing the ding seeing that 150-450 fly over the poor sucker as you pop his head with lead.
Demoman has the most diverse capibilities out of every class. He can be an explosive specialist or a sword wielding samurai. His sticky bomb launcher has one of the highest dps rates in the game. The notorious M1+M2 can tear through any defence, sentries, heavy medic peirs and can even stop an uber in its tracks. As a demo-knight he has great defensive and offensive power. He can charge through a crowd and take an enemy out with a single hit and live with most of his health.
There are also unlockable weapons.
These are earned through achievements or after every 45 minutes or so of play. Each weapon, just like the classes, is balanced, with the exception of a few junk weapons and some overpowered weapons *cough* *cough* gunslinger. These can add alot of diversity to your game and make it just that bit more unpredictable.
There are many gamemodes and maps that each have something great or terrible about them. My favorite map is King of the hill_Harvest. Its a map that has something for every class and is always a joy to play. Koth_Nucleus is great as well, the close combat fighting makes each battle more intense.
Finially, hats.
Team Fortress 2 also has another name granted by its community: Hat Simulator.
These are customisable cosmetics that make each class look different. Its just so addicting getting new hats to make your pyro look like an idiot or your soldier look like a raindeer. There are also a special variation of hats: Unusuals. These add special affects to normal hats like fire or electricity. I personally only have one of my own (an aces high glangarry bonnet) and honestly, for some unknown reason, they are amazing.
In conclusion, Team Fortress 2 is an incredible, addicting game that sucks all of your money away with amazing hats, gameplay and characters. Definately the best gaming experiance i have ever hat. Everything about it just brings me back, every day, for more. I definiately recommend this to anyone who is looking for a fun, online shooter.

If there's one game that has become a favorite faster than any other, it's Team Fortress 2. What I like about it is how it stands out: it's a war game, but nowhere near as hardcore as games like CoD or Battlefield 4. Its arsenal is large and diverse, but weapons are easy to tell from each other by skinss and textures, like the Powerjack, the YER, and then some. The gamemodes are easy to understand, like Payload, where one team pushes a cart to an objactive and the other must stop them, Capture the Flag, not much to say there, and Control Points, where the first team to capture all points wins. Heck, 9 classes sounds like a lot, but they're pretty easy to tell one from another, from lead-hailing Heavies to the speedy Scout. Really, this game is just christmas light-wrapped Soldiers battling Demoman with shiels and katanas, while Pyros shoot lasers at Spies who murder people with magical icicles, and even more.
So if I haven't convinced you yet to play this game, here's something: when I posted this, Team Fortress 2 was the only game I had well over 300 hours on. Seriously, you can play a saxaphone, breakdance, flex, hide in a cardboard box, and best of all, quickscope. And believe me, 360 quickscopes are even more incredible in this game. Just play it already. It's worth the 4 hours it took me to download it.

If there's one game that has become a favorite faster than any other, it's Team Fortress 2. What I like about it is how it stands out: it's a war game, but nowhere near as hardcore as games like CoD or Battlefield 4. Its arsenal is large and diverse, but weapons are easy to tell from each other by skinss and textures, like the Powerjack, the YER, and then some. The gamemodes are easy to understand, like Payload, where one team pushes a cart to an objactive and the other must stop them, Capture the Flag, not much to say there, and Control Points, where the first team to capture all points wins. Heck, 9 classes sounds like a lot, but they're pretty easy to tell one from another, from lead-hailing Heavies to the speedy Scout. Really, this game is just christmas light-wrapped Soldiers battling Demoman with shiels and katanas, while Pyros shoot lasers at Spies who murder people with magical icicles, and even more.
So if I haven't convinced you yet to play this game, here's something: when I posted this, Team Fortress 2 was the only game I had well over 300 hours on. Seriously, you can play a saxaphone, breakdance, flex, hide in a cardboard box, and best of all, quickscope. And believe me, 360 quickscopes are even more incredible in this game. Just play it already. It's worth the 4 hours it took me to download it.

Cons
1. The matchmaking can be imbalanced occasionaly

3. There are (occasional) hackers which we all know are people who dont choose to play correctly and fair.
Other than that my opinion is that this game is amazing (being a spy main people criticize me for being a "weaboo") and most everything is balanced so yes, i would suggest it to all that read this.

This game is amazing.  All weapons have balancing effects, so old players don't have a massive advantage over new ones.  Sidegrades, not upgrades.  The different classes are set up in a way that keeps any one class from dominating the game, since every class had a counter.  The countless weapons and 9 classes alow for peerless customization of your playstyle.  This is like the only game ever with no capability for PTW, since every weapon can be found, except for some reskins.  Large amounts of the game's content come from the community, which is amazing in and of itself.  The detail is amazing, and everything looks amazing, even on the lowest settings.  The holiday events are loads of fun.  I could go on for hours, but lets face it, long reviews are boring!  Recommend 10/10.

Also, if you are playing a class and don't know how to play [without dying], then try going through your mind the name, stats, and role the name implies. Oh boy, I remember my old review, when the game started going the way it has been, and I was optomistic that the game would stay where it was. Boy, I was wrong.
I've clocked in a little over 1000 hours on TF2 (Including my old account) and I stopped playing for quite awhile after that previous review. I played a bit with my friend recently, and goddamn, the new systems are displeasing to say the least. Valve has doubled back on all of the class based shooters coming out today, seeing the new features they implimented, and said "Oh, let's do that". So now there's ranked gameplay, and weapon skins, and all that garbage. It's Counter Strike, but it isn't genaric. TF2 used to be all about comunity play, with the community server list front and center like "Ha, you can do matchmaking, but we all know you wanna trade and play stupid minigames" but now, the button to browse community servers is behind the matchmaking one. Community servers are dying on TF2, and their ranked system is the main thing now, and frankly, it's not very good. It's the same as all the other ones, and we all know how that goes.
Now to review the actual game now. I'm not too fond of ranked play. It is only availible on official maps, and everyone always picks the same few maps. The core gameplay of TF2 is very, very fun, everything is balanced, and visually appealing. So yes, I have to recommend the game, because it is good, but not AS good anymore.

Ingredients:
1. 6 tablespoons unsalted butter
2. 1/2 cup white sugar
3. 1/2 cup brown sugar
4. 1/4 cup water
5. 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon
6. 1 pinch salt
7. 5 apples - peeled, cored and sliced
8. 1 pastry for double-crust pie
Directions:
1. Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
2. Combine butter, white sugar, brown sugar, water, cinnamon, and salt in a saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a boil, remove from heat and set aside.
3. Roll out half the pastry to fit a 9-inch pie plate. Place bottom crust in pie plate; pour in apple slices.
4. Roll out top crust into a 10-inch circle. Cut into 8 (1-inch) wide strips with a sharp paring knife or pastry wheel. Weave the pastry strips, one at a time, into a lattice pattern. Fold the ends of the lattice strips under the edge of the bottom crust and crimp to seal.
5. Pour butter-sugar mixture over top of pie, coating the lattice, and allowing any remaining sauce to drizzle through the crust.
6. Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and bake until the crust is golden brown, the caramel on the top crust is set, and the apple filling is bubbling, 35 to 40 more minutes. Allow to cool completely before slicing.

So, TF2. What can be said?
Is it overrun by 6-year-old FTP snipers? Yep.
Do players spam the most overpowered weapons in the game? Uh huh.
Is it trolled frequently by players using hax? Totally.
Spawn camping? Certainly.
Is the game's RNG your absolute worst nightmare when it comes to opening crates and Mann Up drops? Definitely.
Does it update with more hats than actual patches? You know it.
Is the trading system nothing more than a glamorized version of bitcoins? Absolutely.
Is there no hope at all in saving this game from becoming a hollowed 564gb husk of it's former self? Probably not.
So why did I put in nearly 1400 hours playing it, and why should you do the same? Because in spite of the most irritating aspects of Team Fortress 2, it is just too much freaking fun. Combining a selection of great, team-based, game modes with a cartoonish and totally irreverent style and personality, TF2 overcomes its shortcomings and becomes an all around entertaining online FPS for those of us who have enjoyed it for years now and will continue enjoying it for the years to come.

TF2, best game I've ever played in my life. It's so much fun, the community is amazing, hats are everything.
What makes it so good? Hoovies, spycrabs, taunts, hats, Gaben, crates, community. Just, everything about this game is perfect, except the bugs that are still in the game for some reason.
Gameplay: I have no complains about it, the game runs really smoothly for me and the only time it lags is when I have a bad ping on the server. There are 9 classes in the game (<- No♥♥♥♥♥♥ Sherlock) and every one is a huge amount of fun, depends where you play and how you play. Everyone probably has their main classes because they are good with it, and enjoy it a lot. And the fact that you can have so many weapon selections is awesome. The best games I've had is when both teams are active and trying to win. I once got into a 1.5 hour game where we were just trying to capture the points.
Graphics: Well, it depends on what PC you have and how can it run the game. Some people need to run the game on the lowest quality which is not too bad, you just need to get used to it and everything should be fine. I don't think graphics matter too much, I love the game because of the gameplay, not because of how it looks.
Community: Best community ever. Everyone is nice and supportive. Everyone is so friendly (Unless they decide to rage) I bet some of who is reading got into a server where both teams are taunting to eachother and does random things to make the game better. People are really creative here as well, they make taunts, hats, weapons, maps. Just everything that could possibly make the game better.
Problems: Well, the bugs and glitches can be a problem sometimes but it's TF2...You would always expect a bug. There is no such thing as TF2 with no game breaking glitch. (<- which is fine of course) Maybe the TF2 shop...Some stuff are stupidly expensive which some people find annoying. (Like me, 1-2$ for the machina? (I think) Come on, i can get that for free by going afk...)
One thing that I can't understand is that if you're an F2P (free to play.(Hasn't payed for anything in the game)), it might be a bit hard to fit in with the others and some people might laugh at you as well because you might be a bad player. Or because you're wearing the Gibus (But come on guys, gibus is the best hat in the game). Hats do not give you skill.
A mistake that I've done and you shouldn't...I spent a "bit" of money on the game...It was worthless. If you want some cool items just try trading, yes, it's the long way, but it's better than wasting money just like that.

If your looking for a review on this game you've come to the wrong place, but if your looking for an outstanding pie recipe you've come to the right place.
Ingredients:
1. 6 tablespoons unsalted butter
2. 1/2 cup white sugar
3. 1/2 cup brown sugar
4. 1/4 cup water
5. 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon
6. 1 pinch salt
7. 5 apples - peeled, cored and sliced
8. 1 pastry for double-crust pie
Directions:
1. Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
2. Combine butter, white sugar, brown sugar, water, cinnamon, and salt in a saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a boil, remove from heat and set aside.
3. Roll out half the pastry to fit a 9-inch pie plate. Place bottom crust in pie plate; pour in apple slices.
4. Roll out top crust into a 10-inch circle. Cut into 8 (1-inch) wide strips with a sharp paring knife or pastry wheel. Weave the pastry strips, one at a time, into a lattice pattern. Fold the ends of the lattice strips under the edge of the bottom crust and crimp to seal.
5. Pour butter-sugar mixture over top of pie, coating the lattice, and allowing any remaining sauce to drizzle through the crust.
6. Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and bake until the crust is golden brown, the caramel on the top crust is set, and the apple filling is bubbling, 35 to 40 more minutes. Allow to cool completely before slicing.

Team Fortress 2 is a solid FPS game. It has many different game modes to keep you well entertained along with the ability to run custom maps while hosting servers. It gives a unique cartoonish spin to the genre and defies physicis in a few ways other FPS games wouldn't. The game also has its own set of comics that deliver an interesting backstory to a seemingly silly game. It runs well on most computers and the graphics (all though not realistic) are pretty good. The new Gun Mettle update is a little too similar to CS:GO, which would be okay if valve didn't own both of the games, and its physics aren't realistic, but there not intended to be. The largest downside this game has is the community that plays it. Like many older games TF2 has had a lot of the same people playing it since its realese with 500 hrs+, so if you're new to the game the majority of the players will be tremendously better than you. But don't let that discourage you, TF2 is a great, well built game, and IT'S FREE. How can you complain about a good free game?!?!?! So, if you like the FPS genre and haven't tried this one out I highly reccomend it. It is a Valve game so take off that cheat engine!

Once upon a time there was a player who called himself "The Chicken Hype is Real" just for kicks and giggles. Now, Chicken really enjoyed his gaming on ocassion, and his favorite was the cartoonish, goofy, fun-loving Team Fortress 2. That man was me. I enjoyed this game. I liked it a lot. I played it a lot. In fact, I couldn't get enough of it. Well, not true, but it was still fun. So one day an update was employed to TF2 and I was excited...as I opened it up and looked through it all I heard the song "American Pie", by Don McLean playing in my head, but with the lyrics "Them good old boys was playing TF2 tonight, but this was the day the game died!" It was heartbreaking. I remember all the memories we had, all the stuff I burned as pyro, all the times my friend and I ran around being dumb, all the times we laughed hysterically whilst being Heavy's and shooting at nothing, all the times we sneaked up on each other as spies, all the snipes, all the fist fights, all the trades, all the capturing, all the running around as scout-having a blast, all the healing as medic, all the times I tried rocket-jumping as soldier, all the demoman charging, all the engineering, all the fun maps, the 2Fort, the halloween, the haked ones, oh the fun! I remember having tough, even matches and hearing everyone say, "Good game!" Now, no one says "Good game." In fact, no one speaks at all. This game used to be a fun game, it become one of the few reasons I hated video games again, the reason my friend (who actually wanted to become a video-game designer) choose a different career, the reason my dad left my mom, the reason my wife left me at the alter, the reason the Government took my kids from me, the reason I became a drunk, the reason I became depressed, and the reason my coworker lost their job. I'm still steady in job though. You may ask what I do in my free time now that it's gone. Sometimes I just take a walk in the park and look at the "outdoors", it isn't easy, but it's better than GUN METTLE. I just look around and remember what used to be, and what now is. TF2 is dead. Let us all say goodbye to it. And move on to better lives. Goodbye, old friend. The one I once liked so much, who I now, for the first time, will vote "no," to.

Whats to say about this game that noone else has?
It's the greatest example of a free to play game. It's fun, extremley well balanced, and very "Video gamey".
What do I mean by video gamey?
How about the fact you can, while playing as a bostonian, drink soda to become invincible and bypass sentries made by a texas gunslinger.
Or the fact you can rocket jump and smack someone in the air with a shovel as a stereotypical american patriot.
OR the fact you can be a black-scottish man with one eye and decapitate your enemies with a fantasy blade named after highlander.
OR the fact you can be a mad german scientist who has a healing gun and can make people glow and allow them to become an incarnation of death itself.
OR the fact you can play as a russian who weilds a machine gun, and screams in joy when plowing down foes.
Every class is not only unique, but has it's own character. And unlike other class based shooters,
you can actually tell which class is which.
Heavies are big, towering, slow, death machines.
Scouts are small, puny, fast, and die in two hits.
To top it all off, there are a bunch of ways to play each class.
You'll get items for each class the longer you play.
Think of it like this, every item has a set of rules it follows.
Each item alters the rules, and adds new ones. Like buffs, or debuffs.
Point is, its a really ♥♥♥♥ing good game. 9/10

It might be obvious from the 1400+ hours I have on record, but I play the♥♥♥♥♥♥out of this game. So YES I do have a bias towards it being good. This game is a blast, it takes the good old FPS formula and tosses in the dynamic aspect of classes. Not classes like in bfbc3 where you're just the same♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥with slightly different weapons. Classes in this game make a huge difference in play style. There are other games that do the whole class based gameplay as well, but TF2 just seems so much more polished than most of the others. Maybe it's because it has been around since 07, maybe it's because valve pretty reliably puts out quality games. Regardless, if you like killing other people ion a game in fun and interesting ways, this is the game for you. Like shotguns? go for it! Love to burn people to death while mumbling incoherently? good for you! like the traditional point at a head and click thing? go snipe someone mate. whatever you like from shooting to smashing a face in with  a shovel while riding a rocket blast, this games got it.
Now thats not to say there aren't some bad things here and there. No game is perfect. My only real gripes are these few.
1) Script Kiddies - Also called "hackers" by some (I feel that's too generous a term for these people most of the time) Obviously people who cheat at a game are god damn irritating, and unfortuantely due to TF2 being Free to Play people can make a dummy account, hack, get it banned, make another dummy and repeat. When I first started playing the game I could only use Pyro, Heavy and Engie. Scout was too fragile, Soldier fired and moved too slow, I couldn't hit anything with Demoman, I felt Medic relied too much on teamates. I was getting picked off before I could shoot as Sniper and constantly throwing myself into bad situtations as Spy.
Then as the hours go by and you play you start learning map layouts, you will notice the classes you think are terrible start killing you, you will begin to pay attention to where people from, you will try new modes and levels and notice which areas classes excell.
I learned to control my aim with Scout's frantic movement. Now I can rocket jump with haste as Soldier and predict movement patterns. I began to realize it's not Medic that relies on his team, it is the team that relies on Medic. I learned where the Sniper could better position himself and to not stay in one spot too long. I played Spy more patiently, not just to figure out who I could kill but more  how could I get away after doing so.  I still absolutely suck with Demoman. F#*! Demoman.
After about 20 hours logged and a realization that I spent more time on this game then games I actually spent decent coin on I decided to try out and buy a cheap weapon to get the premium membership so I could get more varied weapon drops which helped open up even more class variety. It's not required to have fun, like I said I put in over 20 hours before doing so but it definitely adds to the experience.  I have not spent any coin on cosmetics or anything else besides the cents for premium but I have to admit I love when I play with people that are dressed up.
I recommend this game to any FPS fans, there is definitely something for everyone not matter your playstyle.

TF2 is a class based first-person shooter consising of 9 classes with 2 teams, RED and BLU, that work together in a variety of game modes, and compete against each other to win.The game is about 10 years old, but is still alive and kicking ( or at least up to this very point ). The main reason it is not only so strong yet so old, but has held a remain one of my favorites is mainly for two reasons which are the constant updates the developers make overtime to the game, and the big, supportive community the game has aquired over the years. The updates usually consist of cosmetics which you use to stylize your classes, weapons, although at times can be very unbalanced, open new doors to how you can play the classes, and many more things that help contribute to the longevity of this game. The community majorly contributes to this longevity by voicing and expressing their thoughts, opinons, and love for this game, so the developers movitate the developers and community as a whole to keep coming back to this game. Without these two main things that keep the game alive, the game would have fallen into obscurity years ago. This game definitly earns the title of "most balanced game" seeing as how each class plays it's own part and all weapons have a debuff fitting thier buff. Scout has low health but makes up for it in speed, Heavy being the oppisite as his bulk and minigun can be perfect for taking out large groups of enemies should they come close. The spy can be a fun class to choose if you are willing to take things slow he is fast but when disquising he will go at the speed of any character slower then him but it is all worthwhile when you can backstab multiple people before they realise their mistake. The medic is by far a savior if used correctly and can turn the tide of a match with a single ubercharge but like the spy and scout he is pretty frail. soldier and demon use explosives for the most apart(aside from a demoknight "sub class") and both rely on a technique called "rocket jumping/sticky jumping" to launch themselves great distances becoming deadly melee rockets themselves. Sniper is the most noob friendly class since  thier job is to keep a distance and pick off oppentes that are a huge threat with items like the razorback preventing the spy from backstabing to help keep it that way. And finally the Pyro a close quaters person who can either airblast people of cliff or burn them in the flames of rainbows. Thier personalities are never side lined to just taunts and domination as each quick voice option is different per class and not some copy paste. The multitude of weapons with different stats make for an abundent source of combinations and with the gun mettle update skins where added to the stock weapons.
There are problems with the game and they can be a very big issue to newcomers or those with high ping: hit detection can be very poor at very random times, at least for me it is. I run around with 30-50 ping and for the most part its fine but every now and then the hit detection just shuts off at very crucial moments like with a heavy I was about to burn takes no damage. the revolver seems to get the worst of this and I know I am not the only one. the spreads fine but when you miss at point blank range and the enemy fills your entire screen then thats just inexcusible. Also the lack of a report abuse button (despite "helpful tips" claiming there is one) is really frusterating. I know Valve relies on VAC but if VAC isn't up to date it won't do anything. If these issues could be fixed I would give this game a perfect score but since these issues can make a break matches should hit detection stop working or a hacker with no sense of fun join it ruins a near perfect experience.

Team Fortress 2 is an Extremely fun first person action-shooter game. Thier are 8 different gamemodes on the pc version including capture the flag, king of the hill, and capture points. The game has a very cartoony graphical feel, very unrealistic. But I like that. The game has 8 different balanced classes, each with there own unique talents, such as the fast running Scout, the walking tank of the Heavy, or the explosive master of the Demoman. After coming back to tf2 from a 2 years long break, I thought I'm going to change my mind on this game. However, i guess valve discouraged me from doing so.
From upgrading pyro to keeping random crits, I honestly don't understand what is wrong with valve. As every tf2 player knows, pyro is one of the most unbalanced classes and it should definitely be nerfed in order to balanace the game. But instead of doing so, valve added a freakishly overpowered flamethrower and a jet pack that allows pyros to perform jumps similar to soldier's rocket jump but TAKE NO SELF DAMAGES. Now pyros can take down heavies (possibly their only counter) with 3 blasts from that flamethrower and they can get away scot-free using that jet pack when they're caught in a firefight. After that update, it's not uncommon to jump into a server with 8 pyros on both your team and the other team. Seriously, what the ♥♥♥♥ is this? I honestly doubt that valve understands what balance is. Instead of buffing underpowered classes, valve decided to improve an already overpowered class. Valve, i suggest you to read the comments from the community before making stupid updates. Just look at the successes like cs go. In that game there are unfair weapons too, but the game responds to the community quickly and now those unfair weapons are all fair and balanced. I really hope tf2 can do that too.
Secondly, I am still surprised to see how many times I died to random crits. I was once bored and decided to count how many of my deaths were caused by random crits. The result wasn't surprising, 70% of my deaths were from them. Seriously, who in god's name came up with this idea. I can't come up with any other explanations except that they are meant to help noobs. With them, a noob can take down a pro with simply a burst of luck. Overall, random crits decrease the overall skill floor of this game and they are really frustrating.

This game has been going strong for quite some time (10 years cough cough) and it's still doing well.  If youre interested in TF2, but aren't sure, test it out! Don't let the edgy, mean, and other kind of people ruin your fun.
TF2 has alot of fun custom servers from the community, and lots and lots of cool maps!
There is alot of cool and fun custom gamemodes, such as DeathRun, Zombie Survival, VS Saxton Hale, Randomizer, and a bunch of other.
The good side of community is very nice and amazing, but don't even get me started on the bad side. You've probably seen/heard of them IF you've already played the game.
The Salt levels in TF2 are quite high currently, and the F2Ps are frowned upon, even tho F2Ps bring life to this game, as theyre needed for the game to succeed. I myself have played this game for now about 4 years, and i am not tired of the game. You can encounter lot's of funny moments, Ie. being blasted thru an open window, see a whole server turn friendly, or maybe even see a dance party, or maybe, JUST maybe, everyone in the server following a drunken scotmann while dancing. (Yes these are very specific, and yes, ive encountered them all. Fun times, yo!)
I do recommend this game, as it is fun, has a simplistic art style (which shouldn't be a plus, because the game is from 2007, but screw it) and the weapons are lots of fun if used in the right way.
I'm gonna give the game a solid 8/10.

Team Fortress 2 is my most played game on steam, not due to religiously playing for hours everyday, but picking it up now and then since its release back in 2007. The game has
not changed much in those 8 years, except from adding maps, weapons and cosmetics, although the biggest change was turning it into a F2P game with microtransactions. Some TF2 veterans frown upon "TF2P" and its onslaught of gibus rocket jumpers, but the microtransactions is arguably what has kept the game alive, and the development team in action for these last years.
The game itself is a class- and team-based FPS, with competitive undertones [spoilers]which are hidden under layers of comedy and ridiculousness[/spoiler]. The game has 9 Classes and (soon) 9 game types to choose from. With the addition of hundreds of items and weapons, each class have access to a great amount of variation of playing style and tactics. If you're not very interested in spending money in this free game, you can gain items from either random drops, trading or crafting. Besides, the stock weapons are arguably the best
, which means that though the game is F2P, it is not Pay 2 win.
The following is a list and description of the classes, which is more of a beginners guide; irrelevant if you just wanted a review. My review is: Try this game, preferably with a friend or two!
The Scout is one of my favourite classes, mostly because he is a force to be reckoned with, despite his appearance. This little guy is the most agile class; with the fastest movespeed and the ability to double-, triple, or with some practice and the right gear; quadra-jump. His role is, not surprisingly, to scout the battlefield, and alert his team of sentry nests or incoming enemies. He has the least health in the game, and doesn't do a lot of damage, which means he must rely on his agility to dodge enemy fire and outmanouver them to win a fight.
Required of the player: Reflexes, Tactical Awareness.
Another one of my favourites: The Soldier mostly relies on his rocket launcher to deal AoE damage (shoot feet bois). He can take a punch, but is the second slowest class in the game. His role is usually to deal damage at mid- to long range, focusing on enemy buildings and groups of players, but if played well, he can show an impressive amount of skill, showmanship, and absurd comedy. His lack of movespeed can be circumvented by learning how to "Rocket jump", which is a bizarre way of getting around, based on a
feature from older fps, such as quake.
Required of the player: Practice, Tactical Awareness.
The Pyro is hated by many, and i must admit I only started playing him for real the last year or so. The Pyro's purpose is as you might guess; to set fire to one or more of the following: Enemies, spies, friends, buildings, furniture, the rain etc. The reason why people hate facing a pyro is because he's gonna♥♥♥♥♥♥on you, regardless of your class, and his and/or your skill. You might kill him, but you'll still die from the afterburn. On a more serious note: his role is to check for spies (he can ignite disguised spies to ruin their day), deflect projectiles away from friendlies, douse teammates who are on fire and immobilize ubered enemies. The pyro doesnt have much health, and has to get up real close to do his thing, so you will die a lot as him, but after a while you'll start taking more and more people with you to the respawn screen.
Required of the player: Reflexes, Teamwork.
The Demoman is the demolitions expert of the team. His role is usually to take out enemy sentry nests or defend chokepoints or other areas of interest. He is a high damage, mid-health and mid-mobility class, but if played well can singlehandedly stop a push and/or win the game. The Demo is also a kind of two-fold class, and can with certain loadouts choose to be either a demoman or a demo
. The demoknight equips some sort of shield as his secondary weapon, which allows him to charge towards (or away from) enemies, and kill them with his melee weapon.
Required of the good player: Tactical Awareness, Intelligence/Practice depending loadout..
The "Heavy Weapons Guy" is one of the most underrated classes of the game, not because people think he's bad (which is not the case), but because he apparently is boring to play, which is ironic, because being a huge russian bone-head carrying a minigun sounds like the definition of fun to me.
At a first glance he seems straightforward; walk towards the enemies while firing $400,000 worth of ammunition over 12 seconds, but a good heavy has a lot on his mind: Being a large and slow target, he must constantly look around for spies and snipers who may instantly kill him if he's not careful. He also has to protect his teammates, especially the medic, either by blocking shots for them or healing them with his Sandvich™. He also has to maximise what little options for mobility he has, and know when and where to strike/retreat.
Required of the good player: Tactical Awareness, Teamwork.
I think I have clocked the most hours as Engineer, not because I like him a lot, but because he is a neccessity for a good team. His role is to build, upgrade and repair buildings which help his team in various ways: The sentry gun defends an area by making the shooties, the dispenser dispenses health and ammo for teammates, and the teleporter teleports teammates from a to b.
The Engineer is not a combat class, and usually needs teammates or buildings present to survive a direct confrontation.
It's important to note that anyone can play engineer, but playing engineer
relies on one's timing and placement of buildings.
Required of the player: Patience, Intelligence.
The medic heals people, and it's usually enough to point your medigun and a friendly heavy and grab something to eat while he cleans house. Like the heavy, however, there are subtle amounts of things to be aware of when playing medic: It's your responsibility to look backwards while your teammates fire forwards, in other words; be a mini-scout, warn your teammates of ambushes or spies. You can of course choose to be a "Combat medic" who only heals people when you have nothing to shoot at/stab, which is fine, because the medic melee weapon has some uncanny ability to always crit when you need it to.
The most noticeable effect of a medic on a battlefield is however not that he heals people, but that his various medi-guns have various "ubercharge"-effects, which he can activate after reaching 100% uber by healing teammates:
Required of the player: Tactical Awareness, Teamwork.
The xXMLG1337DeathReaperElfXx of TF2. Point and click adventure to dispose of teammates, more or less useless in close combat. This is not CS, you will not carry your team.
Required of the player: Patience, Aim
Rain on everyone's parade with an instant-kill backstab, disabling and subsequent destruction of buildings, and the ability to cloak or disguise as enemies.
Required of the player: Intelligence, Sadism

Oh, Team Fortress 2... formerly one of my favorite PC games, now it's just sitting there collecting virtual dust. A shell of its former self.
When I first joined Steam back in 2009, this was one of the games I started out with. It truly was the most fun I've had online. For the longest time, it was my go-to game for online multiplayer. The last few times I played, though, have been met with nothing but frustration and disappointment. However, before I get into my grievances with what the game's became, let me go over what I did like about it.
The weapon variety and character customization helped make each otherwise-identical class feel unique from player to player. The wide variety of combinations between items and weapons helped open up a wide variety of play styles, and no two players are going to play one class the same way. The humor is also great, parodying late '60s cliches and stereotypes, and there's a surprising amount of backstory for a game like this. It almost makes it feel like there's a reason behind all the otherwise meaningless violence the game has to offer.
However, since the game went F2P back in 2011, I've felt the community has grown more infantile, both figuratively and literally. The amount of kids I've encountered since then is insane; it's as if parents don't care that this game is rated Mature (as in, ages 17 and up). As of this writing I am 22, so age ratings don't mean much to me anymore. But still. Parents, be mindful of what your kids are playing and saying online. As for the "figuratively" part, I've noticed a sharp decline in the maturity of the game's playerbase; half of the people I played with didn't even want to play the game, they just dicked around on their own while I tried to do the objectives on my own. What happened to teamwork in a game with "team" directly in the title?
Server-wise, it really depends. Some are serious and have client-side mods disabled for the purest experience possible, others have server-side mods but usually to enhance the gameplay in some way or do silly things like add in Super Smash Bros. to TF2, while others have annoying ad-walls that play either at the beginning of a new map, a new round or whenever they want to, which gets annoying REAL fast and completely breaks the flow of gameplay (e.g. BLU can plan out their attack while RED is unable to set up their defense in time for the game to begin, assuming all the players are on the same page.) I can understand wanting to support your favorite servers but forced ads are not the way to do it. Rules or donation incentives on some servers are also highly questionable, and admins are free to abuse their power how they see fit. One time I got kicked from a server for daring (hue) to have a MLP avatar, back when I was in that fandom. I didn't even do anything wrong, I just had an MLP avatar. The hell.
Also, after 8 years and new gamemodes and maps being released in incomplete states, it's quite obvious Valve has put TF2 on life support. The last Halloween update paled in comparison to past ones (although Merasmus was a pretty good announcer), and there wasn't even a Christmas 2014 update. They're just gonna keep releasing half-baked content or even forget about annual, holiday-themed updates until it finally dies. How sad.
If this were 2009 - 2012, would I recommend this game? Yes, I would. But now? No. It's a shell of its former self, and I don't like the direction it's going in. The memories of when I really enjoyed this game are still around, but now I just can't look at this game as it is today without feeling frustration and disappointment.

Oh, Team Fortress 2... formerly one of my favorite PC games, now it's just sitting there collecting virtual dust. A shell of its former self.
When I first joined Steam back in 2009, this was one of the games I started out with. It truly was the most fun I've had online. For the longest time, it was my go-to game for online multiplayer. The last few times I played, though, have been met with nothing but frustration and disappointment. However, before I get into my grievances with what the game's became, let me go over what I did like about it.
The weapon variety and character customization helped make each otherwise-identical class feel unique from player to player. The wide variety of combinations between items and weapons helped open up a wide variety of play styles, and no two players are going to play one class the same way. The humor is also great, parodying late '60s cliches and stereotypes, and there's a surprising amount of backstory for a game like this. It almost makes it feel like there's a reason behind all the otherwise meaningless violence the game has to offer.
However, since the game went F2P back in 2011, I've felt the community has grown more infantile, both figuratively and literally. The amount of kids I've encountered since then is insane; it's as if parents don't care that this game is rated Mature (as in, ages 17 and up). As of this writing I am 22, so age ratings don't mean much to me anymore. But still. Parents, be mindful of what your kids are playing and saying online. As for the "figuratively" part, I've noticed a sharp decline in the maturity of the game's playerbase; half of the people I played with didn't even want to play the game, they just dicked around on their own while I tried to do the objectives on my own. What happened to teamwork in a game with "team" directly in the title?
Server-wise, it really depends. Some are serious and have client-side mods disabled for the purest experience possible, others have server-side mods but usually to enhance the gameplay in some way or do silly things like add in Super Smash Bros. to TF2, while others have annoying ad-walls that play either at the beginning of a new map, a new round or whenever they want to, which gets annoying REAL fast and completely breaks the flow of gameplay (e.g. BLU can plan out their attack while RED is unable to set up their defense in time for the game to begin, assuming all the players are on the same page.) I can understand wanting to support your favorite servers but forced ads are not the way to do it. Rules or donation incentives on some servers are also highly questionable, and admins are free to abuse their power how they see fit. One time I got kicked from a server for daring (hue) to have a MLP avatar, back when I was in that fandom. I didn't even do anything wrong, I just had an MLP avatar. The hell.
Also, after 8 years and new gamemodes and maps being released in incomplete states, it's quite obvious Valve has put TF2 on life support. The last Halloween update paled in comparison to past ones (although Merasmus was a pretty good announcer), and there wasn't even a Christmas 2014 update. They're just gonna keep releasing half-baked content or even forget about annual, holiday-themed updates until it finally dies. How sad.
If this were 2009 - 2012, would I recommend this game? Yes, I would. But now? No. It's a shell of its former self, and I don't like the direction it's going in. The memories of when I really enjoyed this game are still around, but now I just can't look at this game as it is today without feeling frustration and disappointment.

Team Fortess 2.
An extremely addicting, action-packed, colorful and slightly maniacal game jam-packed with hats, loads of weapons that vary in playstyle, and 9 Fun Classes. Welcome to the world of TF2, where two teams; RED and BLU fight to the death over wastelands to the death. I totally reccomend this to people who are NOT willing to spend on a "pixelated" game, though this game is a pretty good deal due to F2P, and has restrictions and makes you want to go P2P; in which you probably will.
All the classes have about 100 playstyles and loadouts each, which results in over 900 playstyles as you have 9 classes.
Fun gamemodes and a really awesome community, if you ignore the judgemental P2Ps who judge people by hats. Community created currencies, exciting unboxing/uncrating, trading, and so much more. I totally reccomend this to anyone who enjoys a fun "unrealistic" game with a lot of possible outcomes in messing aroudn with the loadout. Weapons also vary a lot, we even have a Frying Pan for a melee weapon. What other games have Frying Pans? (L4D2 and L4D I guess) You should totally go download this right now and go enjoy the game. A rating from me of about 9.5/10 as it still has some minor flaws like some-terrible people on the community as stated before.
Do I love this? : Yeah, totally.
Should You Play This : Yeah, go ahead. IT'S FREE :D
Will You Probably Get Around 100+ Hours? : If this is your kind of game, yeah you would probably.

Absolutely one of the best games I've ever played.
There's so much diversity and randomness that playing never gets old. Every class has its role and when played correctly, they fit together perfectly.
Even new players should have no trouble getting the hang of any given class, and because of weapon balance, no player has an unfair advantage over another. Sure, scouts will almost always win a 1v1 with a sniper at close range, but a sniper will almost always win a 1v1 with a heavy at a distance. No unlock is objectively better than what you start out with, but promote different playstyles.
A Dear Ringer spy doesn't have to be as careful as a Cloak and Dagger spy. Gunslinger engineer won't usually be in one spot for too long.
Overall, 10/10. I wholeheartedly recommend this game.

Well this is will be my first review for a pc game ever so here goes. I currently have 213 hours on this game(and hopefully many, many, many more) and I can say I have enjoyed every hour of it. First off let me just say that I love the classes. They all have their own personality, taunts, and most importantly, hats. They all have advantages and disadvantages against every class. They are hard to get used to, and I personally could not play demoman for the life of me in my first few hours of play. He was my least played class and I had pretty much given up on his class, but then I discovered the beautiful elegance of "demoknight". It changed everything about the class and it's another reason I love this game. There are tons of ways to play different classes and you never know what will happen.
I'm not going to dwell on the recent update that much but I think it's great! Don't believe people that say this has turned into a copy and paste of csgo. But anyway getting off topic. There is also a co-op section of the game called mvm and it's pretty fun when you are not put in a server with a bunch of rocket jumper gibbus noobs. You get upgrades and it's pretty team based so you have to think about what class you should be.

To sum this up I love everything about this game, except for the occasional crashes and endless hordes of soul consuming gibbuses. I would definately recommend you pick this up and it's free to play so I don't see why you don't have it. Team Fortress 2 is an FPS titan that has had a huge playerbase that's lasted for eight years. If nothing else, the game is unique. Throwing realism out the window, the game instead focuses on face paced gameplay that revolves around movement and the environment. The game has a low skill floor with public servers filled with new players, and an incredibly high skill ceiling with tournaments featuring pros who have been improving for years. The classes are all very unique, and for the most part, very intuitive.
However, the game is slowly losing strength. Many players feel that Valve is abandonning the game to work on CSGO and Dota, which are currently two of the most popular games out there. The neglect has started to make the community leak out. Valve outsources the updates to the community by adding new maps and cosmetics made by dedicated players. While it is fantastic that they are allowing community content, it's made them lazy in making new updates that only they can do. It took 6 years to fix a major bug on a weapon, and we're still awaiting matchmaking. The addition of community maps is too slow to really be thankful for. With hundreds of fantastic maps waiting to be added, we only get a few per year.
If you haven't tried TF2, I suggest you give it a try. The game itself is great, but it won't be the staple it has been for a whole lot longer. With Overwatch on the horizon, TF2 may take a major blow unless Valve breathes new life into a game that's received incredible amounts of love for eight years.

INTRO:
This game is a really good shooter, it dosen't punish you for being a noob, but does have a pretty high skill cap. The different classes really effect the game (sometimes ruining it for me when i want to play the Scout or the Spy and like always everyone plays Pyro ) its a very well done game and the cartoonic characters are very iconic as well. Overall i HEAVILY recommend this game.
Play this if you are looking more for a fun and funny game and not a heavily stratigic and serious game.
It's just so fun playing a soldier with "The Rocket Jumper" and just hitting them with a shovel after launching yourself into the air with rockets and then smashing the little health they have left with your boots.
There are a lot of stuff like this in the game.
PROS:
1) Very funny, a lot of *interesting* stuff can happen (wink wink)...
2) A lot of variety with having 9 very different classes AND a lot of weapons.
3) Objective based game - you dont just run around and kill people.
4) A variety of game modes - there are a lot of objectives and maps that you can play.
5) The characters are very funny - the sniper cursing everyone and being an ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, the scout and heavy eternal hatred for the other, the soldier annoying everyone, and obviously... the Pyrovision goggles.
CONS:
1) The random crits can really be annoying when the enemy gets a lot of them
2) The huge amout of weapons can sometimes be a bit scary to new people.
SUMMARY:
A funny shooter that keeps itself fresh with a lot of variety and funny characteristics and moments,
objective based though being a bit scary for new people with having maby for them too much variety and being annoyed when the enemy gets a lot of rrandom crits.

TF2 or Team Fortress Two is a FREE (mostly) game where you can play as a handful of characters to complete your missions. This game is about killing people, capturing posts, pushing carts, taunting, and much much more. The Scout; a fast cocky baseball player at heart. The Soldier; a blasting American if I ever saw one. The Pyro; an arsonist who loves to watch the world burn with rainbows and lollichops. The Demoman; a Scottish swordsman/kabllewwie with a strong lip. The Heavy; A sandwich numming minigun lover who is fat and slow as sh*t, but what did you expect? The Engineer; a countryfolk who knows a thing or two about technology and solves his problems by "Use more gun". The Medic; a healer, nuff said (Try a Heavy and Medic combo). The Sniper; an Australian marksman who is known for making the weather funky, lots of small red clouds. The Spy; a backstabbing invisible invincible Frenchman who is stealthy and silent. Each class can use a bundle of different weapons that have their perks, and not so cool perks. Almost 10 years in the making and still going strong! Keep up the good work, still pretty cool how it is a free game.

Alright, so i decided to come back and re-do my review.. and well, here's my thoughts..
Long ago, on august 25th of 2014 i got "Team Fortress 2" and it became one of my favorite games.. sometime during january of 2015 i upgraded to premium, this game is one of the most fun games i've ever played.. and its practically the defining game of class based shooters.. however, many times during my gameplay i was thinking of just quitting, until gun mettle was released i found TF2 REALLY boring at times.. so now.. onto the pros, and cons,
PROS:
Lots of cosmetics, something that lets you customize your character like you cant in any other game!
A nice variety of weapons!
Custom sprays!
So much more that i cannot list!
But its also got a lot of.
CONS:
Someone on your team is ALWAYS afk, the day your team can actually have a non-afk member is the day half-life 3 is out
On trade servers, someone always sprays up ecchi or hentai, which is just ew,
You will be f2p for almost all of your tf2 career,
ADMIT IT, you couldnt get an aussie so you bought one,
And thats really all for cons.. but there is neutrals
NEUTRAL POINTS:
You meet alot of people, good AND bad,
You meet alot of weebs, can be good or bad
You meet alot of FNaF fanboys, can be good, but is normally BAD
You meet alot of tryhards, who just bought everything on the market they could afford,
You met me, and begged for my aussies, and i said no, and declined your friend request
Scout may as well be the new best class, good for me, bad for you!
Sniper gets the machina, one of the most stupidly op weapons in the game..
The AWPer hand is not the bodyshot king it's cs:go brethren is,
and most importantly.. SO MANY CHILDREN!!! some of them are good, and are actually funny, but most of em just suck at the game and had a bad day at school, so they cry into the mic and get banned within their 2 seconds online,
OVERALL I RATE THIS GAME 8.5/10

Longevity is tough for competitive shooters. Hardly a month goes by without new virtual arenas cropping up and enticing you into some fresh conflict, and only a few popular games manage to sustain active player bases even a year after their initial release. And then there's Team Fortress 2. Released in 2007, this class-based classic is still going strong well into its seventh year, thanks largely to its lively and creative community. Since GameSpot's original TF2 review, the game has benefited from numerous updates and made the jump to a free-to-play business model. So how well is Team Fortress 2 faring in 2014 among the current crop of competitors for your time and money?
The short answer is, it's holding up very well. The core action pits two teams of players against each other in a battle to capture points, move a cart, or steal a briefcase. The objective is always very straightforward; it's the interplay between the nine playable classes that makes things so varied and interesting. The speedy scout, the militant heavy, the diligent engineer, the conniving medic, the pesky sniper, the sneaky spy, the feisty pyro, the explosive soldier, and the even-more-explosive demoman all have unique weapons, attributes, and abilities that complement each other and clash in myriad ways. Encounters can vary widely depending on the match type and the makeup of each team, and this unpredictability is crucial to TF2's long-standing appeal.
When you come out of the gate as a heavy with a medic in tow, you're a formidable offensive force, but if a spy loops around to backstab the medic and you round the corner on a pyro, it can all come undone in a matter of seconds. Snipers can cover expected enemy paths, but rocket-jumping soldiers have a knack for finding alternative routes and raining explosive death from above. You may think you have a comparatively weak scout dead to rights, only to be stunned by a baseball and beaten to death. As you watch your giblets splatter on the ground and see a freeze-frame of your gleeful killer, it's hard not to chuckle at the sheer variety of ways you can meet an untimely demise. And the humorous quips, ridiculous outfits, and histrionic announcer help cultivate this lighthearted tone.
Of course, this core dynamic has persisted for most of TF2's life span, so if you stopped playing it a few years ago and come back for a few matches, you'll find things are very familiar. Learning the ropes and getting the hang of your chosen role is still a gratifying experience, and mastering advanced techniques doesn't just make you deadlier; it gives you more options for how to approach combat. Keeping your options open is still valuable too, because being flexible with your choice of character can help you avoid ending up on a catastrophically imbalanced squad. It is Team Fortress, after all.
But though there is much that has remained constant about the core game, there have been some notable changes over the years, as well as regular infusions of new weapons and items. Of the hundreds of things available in the online store, some can be unlocked through play, while others must be purchased with actual money. From small doodads that cost less than a dollar to massive bundles that cost hundreds, there's a wide range of ways to customize your experience.
Many of the items offer nothing more than a playful twist on the game's already cheeky cartoon aesthetic. You can buy hats, shirts, shoes, and other cosmetic gear to dress up like a character from Adult Swim or don spooky seasonal garb that you can wear only during Halloween or a full moon. Even if you don't fancy shelling out for any of this stuff, it's fun to see some visual variety as you try to light your opponents on fire.
Other weapons have more of an impact, like the ones that give your character a new chargeable and expendable power. The scout can build hype, which turns his usual double jump into a triple, quadruple, or quintuple jump, and the soldier can build rage, which allows him to rally his nearby teammates to do extra damage. Skills like these have more of a meaningful impact on the action, bringing something new to the table that your enemies must contend with. And then there are the totally out-there loadouts, like the one that turns the grenade-launching demoman into an extra from the movie Braveheart.In addition to the cosmetic options, there are a lot of weapons and items that offer small buffs or subtle tweaks to your attributes. Depending on which healing gun the medic equips, for example, he can imbue himself and his targeted ally with extra damage resistance or enable himself to match the speed of his target. Differences like these don't do much to change the core action, but they do give experienced players substantial room for strategic variation.
These options broaden the field of viable strategies, which helps keep combat lively and varied. And fortunately, none of the purchasable weapons or items tip the scales unfairly towards those willing to pay. Buffs and bonuses usually come with caveats, and the weapons that bestow new abilities are usually unlocked for free. For this review, I spent some money on goofy hats and some of the stranger weaponry on offer, like the pyro's flamethrower that actually shoots bubbles and rainbows. It was fun to play with the new gear, but I still found myself switching my loadout between free and paid weapons regularly to adapt to the match situation.

I absolutly love this game, but i want to send in some harsh opinions that it needs.
The game has terrible performance optimization, people with average to good computers report having fps drops forcing some to use graphic-deminishing fps configs made by the community to bypass these problems. I personally have to play on the lowest possible resolution, downgrade the direct x level to 8, use an fps config to lowered the game settings as much as possible and lowered the graphic's card LOD bias to the lowest possible value. Basically, the game requires alot from your CPU and it came out in 2007.
Players have been begging for years now, that valve implements the most common competitive modes, 6v6 and 9v9 as official game modes, with proper matchmaking so we don't have to rely on external unstable websites that take half an hour to get a lobby filled. It's been announced that they are working on it...but not on the official website, so the common player wouldn't know, it was on a live-stream that talks speciffically about competitive tf2. But even then we know they won't gives us what we want because 6v6 excludes classes and that was labeled "counter-productive" apperantly.
Last but not least, random critical hits. Getting a critical hit using a weapon effect is fine, because it takes at least some agility withing the game: getting headshots, burning a player on his back, backstabbing, hitting a flair on enemies that are on fire, melee the enemy while rocket jumping, all of these are fine and can be really hard to pull off, depending on the weapon but random crits feel like getting betrayed by the game when you get killed in one shot at full health because the enemy was lucky when you clearly had the upper-hand on the situation and turned off alot of people from playing public games.

Team Fortress 2 is one of the most customizable First Person Shooter games where you can truly express how you want to play the game at heart. There are nine playable classes, each following a type of gameplay. Whether you enjoy sneaking in the shadows to eliminate targets, moving at incredible speeds to evade bullets or simply running into a huge crowd of enemies as a big, brute monster with a behemoth gattling gun, Team Fortress 2 has a playstyle for you. The classes themselves can also change what weapon they want to equip, so you don't have to use their default weapons. You can always replace your bomb launcher for a defensive shield, or replace your shotgun for a health-restoring food pack. If you want to go beyond gameplay, you can pay real money to purchase cosmetic stuff in the in-game store, decorating your lovely character with fedoras, robot arms, tuxedos, coats and more - both cheap and expensvie. Considering there are already hundreds of wearable items in the game, you'll also have fun making your character look good.
Gamemodes in Team Fortress 2 come in a very large variety. They follow some traditional gamemodes such as Arena Deathmatch and Capture the Flag while also containing some original gamemodes such as Special Delivery, Mann VS Machine and most iconically, Payload, which has been used by other games such as Paladins and Overwatch for being so fun. Sometimes, fighting can get reppetitive though, so if you want, you can always join a friendly server where you can simply relax and meet new players - while also showing off your awesome loadout - if you even have one...
If none of these maps satisfy you, you can try out Custom Servers which are ran by people rather than the game's servers itself. Try out some stupidly funny gamemodes such as hide and seek, or 30 players versus one super player.
In-game bugs are not commonly crossed upon, though there are some that could be devestating once discovered. Luckily they're patched once found at an alarming rate - provided it's ruining the gameplay.
Do I recommend this game? Yes, definetly.

If your looking for a review on this game you've come to the wrong place, but if your looking for an outstanding pie recipe you've come to the right place.
Ingredients:
1. 6 tablespoons unsalted butter
2. 1/2 cup white sugar
3. 1/2 cup brown sugar
4. 1/4 cup water
5. 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon
6. 1 pinch salt
7. 5 apples - peeled, cored and sliced
8. 1 pastry for double-crust pie
Directions:
1. Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
2. Combine butter, white sugar, brown sugar, water, cinnamon, and salt in a saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a boil, remove from heat and set aside.
3. Roll out half the pastry to fit a 9-inch pie plate. Place bottom crust in pie plate; pour in apple slices.
4. Roll out top crust into a 10-inch circle. Cut into 8 (1-inch) wide strips with a sharp paring knife or pastry wheel. Weave the pastry strips, one at a time, into a lattice pattern. Fold the ends of the lattice strips under the edge of the bottom crust and crimp to seal.
5. Pour butter-sugar mixture over top of pie, coating the lattice, and allowing any remaining sauce to drizzle through the crust.
6. Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and bake until the crust is golden brown, the caramel on the top crust is set, and the apple filling is bubbling, 35 to 40 more minutes. Allow to cool completely before slicing.

If there is one thing better than online class-based gunplay it is online class-based gunplay with hats.
Hats; as we well know, are what elevate a game from the lowly levels of commonplace to the lofty heights of the AAA title, and Team Fortress 2 certainly provides more than enough of them to satisfy even the most fashion-concious player. The best part of all is that its completely free on PC and Mac.
Now for those amongst you who (for some reason?!) aren't fussed about hats, you might be wondering what else this game has to offer. Team fortress 2 is a class-based online multiplayer FPS that places two teams in various arenas of battle. With nine classes to choose from and a plethora of weapons for each class equip, you certainly have enough goodies to keep you occupied.
You probably have played your share of shooters and by now have likely found you have a specific style of play, Team Fortress 2 caters to this fantastically with the class system. For those who like to find themselves on the frontline there are many options.
Heavy: Big gun, lots of health, slow moving.
Scout: Small gun, little health, very quick.
Pyro: Flamethrower, medium health
Demoman: Explosive weapons, medium health
Soldier: Lots of health, big rocket launcher.
Spy: Able to disguise as the enemy, destroy buildings and stealthily remove the enemy
If you prefer a support role:
Medic: Medi gun (for healing your own team), medium health
Engineer: Ability to build offensive and defensive structures
Sniper: Does what it says on the tin i.e. snipes
The game has a very characteristic, almost cartoony art style and is set in a 1950s/1960s America (or America-like country). This art style doesn't go for the realism of the CODs and Battlefields but has a definite charm too it and though simple, is very pretty. Character models emphasise the traits of the specific class and the guns are really cool, being a good mix of realistic and cartoony over-the-top. New weapons and items; and of course the all important hats, are consistently gained throughout play and are awarded for both achievement completion and play time (and according to strange and complex equations).
Control is very easy, with simple WASD for movement and mouse for aiming. Other controls like team chat (which has useful presets) are also set handily on the keyboard. The camera sits behind the player and tracks nicely, I've yet to experience any major camera glitching after several intensive hours of play.
Sound is something which TF2 does really well. Gun sounds are designed to fit with the slightly cartoony image of the game with guns making slightly larger than life sounds, though this sits nicely in line with their look. The soundtrack is also built nicely to fit with the 50s/60s look and has also been extensively remixed by fans with several fan-made albums available.
Final Thoughts
If you don't own it already there is really no excuse not to go right from here and download it through Steam. It is free and I guarantee it will provide several hours of fun. The classic charm, huge range of customisation options and constant updates from Valve make this a game that never grows old and will continue to entertain long into the future.
