Well I think its time I made an Actual Review for this game.
Team Fortress 2 in my opinion is one of the most team based FPS shooters asides from Counter Strike and others. It has 9 classes with a wide range of strengths and weaknesses but together as a TEAM they can overcome their weaknesses and use their strengths to acheive a certain goal. Though you could destroy entire Valve servers by your self without the use of teamwork (AKA Pubstomping). But wheres the fun in that?
As of typing this review Offical Competitive Matchmaking is in a Beta and only currently has 6V6 Which is one of the competitive modes I will go in to further depth in the next paragraph. But normally competitive TF2 is ran by the community who give up their free time to let others play Comp TF2 (They the TRUE MVP'S)
The following are competitve formats:
1. 6V6 usually teams are 2 Soldiers 2 Scouts 1 Demo and 1 Medic but offclassing is done sometimes. This one is my favorite tied with 9V9
2. 9V9 is one of every class on one team which I think is great because ALL classes can bring something to the table which makes for great games.
3. 4V4 is 1 Soldier 1 scout 1 Demo 1 Medic I don't take much interest in 4v4 though it is a very fun and interesting mode because its like 6's but with 1 less scout and 1 less soldier
4. 2V2 Ultiduo is 1 Soldier and 1 Medic I have played this a few times as both medic and soldier and it is a very fair and fun gamemode I don't play it often but sometimes I grab my soldier friend and play it (or I play soldier cause they can't protect a medic for♥♥♥♥♥♥
5. 1V1 (MGE) 1v1 or MGE is not something that I have played a lot only twice as a matter of fact. Its any class I think and usually if you wanna be "competitive" both of you will say for example play sniper to see which one is "better" usually first to 20 wins.
Every format is played on different gamemodes to suit that format. Example Payload is a staple of the 9v9 format. King of the hill is played on both 9V9 and 6V6 (I think 4V4 and 2V2 Ultiduo too but not for sure) 5 CP Is a staple of 6V6 4V4. 1V1 is played on an empty map but with no objectives other then to defeat your opponent.
As of this review these are the following gamemodes:
1. CTF (Capture the Flag/Intelligence)
CTF has been apart of TF2 for a long time even the Grandfather of maps 2Fort is a CTF gamemode map. On offical Valve servers first to 3 flag captures wins the round. This gamemode is not really played competitively but does have the potential too but when it is its usually played by 6V6 or 4V4
2. King of the Hill (KOTH for short)
KOTH is a great gamemode played by lots of competitive formats. At the beginning of the round the 1 and only control point (the hill) is locked but after a few seconds it will become neutral and available for capture by either RED or BLU. One team must hold the point for 3 minutes to win the round. This is played competitvely by 9V9,6V6 and I think 4V4 and 2V2
3. Control Points (5 CP)
Ah 5 CP as I mentioned before it is a staple of 6v6 format and 4v4. At the start of the round both teams have 2 control points locked and owned to them leaving the middle point Neutral for both teams. Capturing the middle control point is important as it unlocks the next point for you to capture. If all control points are in your teams possesion then you win the round.
4. Payload
Payload is a classic for 9v9. Just like 5 CP is a staple of 6v6. Payload is a staple of 9v9. At the start of the round RED team has about 1 minute to set up defences and prepare to stop the BLU team who are pushing the cart to the RED base. For RED to win they have to hold off BLU for however long they have to (5 minutes before they capture the first point if RED loses a checkpoint BLU gains time to push). For BLU to win they have to push the cart all the way to the RED base while capturing checkpoints along the way to gain more time to push. Payload is mostly played by 9V9
5. Payload Race and Arena Mode and Special Delivery
The reason I put these 3 together is because Arena mode is basically dead so is Special Delivery and Payload race is not really a good gamemode for comp (so is Arena mode and Special Delivery) lets start with Arena Mode. Arena is any class and any amount of people fight to the death there is no respawning in arena until the next round starts. If both teams are still alive by a certain time a control point will open and whatever team captures it they win no matter how many people are alive thats one way to win another is just to kill the entire enemy team. Payload race is just both teams have 1 cart and they have to push it to each others base. First team to get the cart to the enemy base wins. Special Delivery is basically 1 flag CTF both teams have to take the flag to one point of the map whoever gets it first wins the round.
None of these gamemodes are played competitvely.
6. Attack and Defence (CP)
Attack and Defence is like Payload but with Control points its usually played by 9V9. RED team has 1 minute to set up defences to stop BLU. BLU has to capture all the controls points to win but everytime they capture a point they gain time. For RED to win they have to defend for a certain amount of time ranging from 5 to 20 minutes. This one is weird because maps such as dustbowl are not played competitvely but maps like Steel are.
This game does have trading but the economy is kinda ♥♥♥♥ed at the moment (Check Backpack.tf) but hey Hats are cool amirite?
Overall Team Fortress 2 is a great game I love the game and it is my favorite of all time. I suggest if you don't play it to try it.

This is one of the few games that I can agree aged beautifully. I'd been a player since I was twelve years old up until I turned sixteen, and now that I've finally moved on I think it's a good time to put in my final two cents.
Team Fortress 2 is a game that is literally life-changing in how fun and social it is. The people I've met through the game have shaped me into who I am today, and indulging in the fanbase TF2 created made some of my fondest memories. The game is far more fun and nonthreatening than any other FPS I have ever played; It encourages trading and investing, friendliness, and ridiculousness. The characters are hilarious and easy to identify on the battlefield, the gameplay is clear-cut with no unnecessary complications, and the customization is so. much. fun., and the lore is the most cohesive and most silly in any F2P first person shooter I've ever seen!
The playerbase has gone down in recent years and sometimes it feels that Valve has given up on this game, but don't let that deter you. The game as I left it was a game full of love, life, and friendly sandwich-wielding heavies. Some things never change, and that can be a good thing; TF2 will tell you that.

Well I think its time I made an Actual Review for this game.
Team Fortress 2 in my opinion is one of the most team based FPS shooters asides from Counter Strike and others. It has 9 classes with a wide range of strengths and weaknesses but together as a TEAM they can overcome their weaknesses and use their strengths to acheive a certain goal. Though you could destroy entire Valve servers by your self without the use of teamwork (AKA Pubstomping). But wheres the fun in that?
As of typing this review Offical Competitive Matchmaking is in a Beta and only currently has 6V6 Which is one of the competitive modes I will go in to further depth in the next paragraph. But normally competitive TF2 is ran by the community who give up their free time to let others play Comp TF2 (They the TRUE MVP'S)
The following are competitve formats:
1. 6V6 usually teams are 2 Soldiers 2 Scouts 1 Demo and 1 Medic but offclassing is done sometimes. This one is my favorite tied with 9V9
2. 9V9 is one of every class on one team which I think is great because ALL classes can bring something to the table which makes for great games.
3. 4V4 is 1 Soldier 1 scout 1 Demo 1 Medic I don't take much interest in 4v4 though it is a very fun and interesting mode because its like 6's but with 1 less scout and 1 less soldier
4. 2V2 Ultiduo is 1 Soldier and 1 Medic I have played this a few times as both medic and soldier and it is a very fair and fun gamemode I don't play it often but sometimes I grab my soldier friend and play it (or I play soldier cause they can't protect a medic for♥♥♥♥♥♥
5. 1V1 (MGE) 1v1 or MGE is not something that I have played a lot only twice as a matter of fact. Its any class I think and usually if you wanna be "competitive" both of you will say for example play sniper to see which one is "better" usually first to 20 wins.
Every format is played on different gamemodes to suit that format. Example Payload is a staple of the 9v9 format. King of the hill is played on both 9V9 and 6V6 (I think 4V4 and 2V2 Ultiduo too but not for sure) 5 CP Is a staple of 6V6 4V4. 1V1 is played on an empty map but with no objectives other then to defeat your opponent.
As of this review these are the following gamemodes:
1. CTF (Capture the Flag/Intelligence)
CTF has been apart of TF2 for a long time even the Grandfather of maps 2Fort is a CTF gamemode map. On offical Valve servers first to 3 flag captures wins the round. This gamemode is not really played competitively but does have the potential too but when it is its usually played by 6V6 or 4V4
2. King of the Hill (KOTH for short)
KOTH is a great gamemode played by lots of competitive formats. At the beginning of the round the 1 and only control point (the hill) is locked but after a few seconds it will become neutral and available for capture by either RED or BLU. One team must hold the point for 3 minutes to win the round. This is played competitvely by 9V9,6V6 and I think 4V4 and 2V2
3. Control Points (5 CP)
Ah 5 CP as I mentioned before it is a staple of 6v6 format and 4v4. At the start of the round both teams have 2 control points locked and owned to them leaving the middle point Neutral for both teams. Capturing the middle control point is important as it unlocks the next point for you to capture. If all control points are in your teams possesion then you win the round.
4. Payload
Payload is a classic for 9v9. Just like 5 CP is a staple of 6v6. Payload is a staple of 9v9. At the start of the round RED team has about 1 minute to set up defences and prepare to stop the BLU team who are pushing the cart to the RED base. For RED to win they have to hold off BLU for however long they have to (5 minutes before they capture the first point if RED loses a checkpoint BLU gains time to push). For BLU to win they have to push the cart all the way to the RED base while capturing checkpoints along the way to gain more time to push. Payload is mostly played by 9V9
5. Payload Race and Arena Mode and Special Delivery
The reason I put these 3 together is because Arena mode is basically dead so is Special Delivery and Payload race is not really a good gamemode for comp (so is Arena mode and Special Delivery) lets start with Arena Mode. Arena is any class and any amount of people fight to the death there is no respawning in arena until the next round starts. If both teams are still alive by a certain time a control point will open and whatever team captures it they win no matter how many people are alive thats one way to win another is just to kill the entire enemy team. Payload race is just both teams have 1 cart and they have to push it to each others base. First team to get the cart to the enemy base wins. Special Delivery is basically 1 flag CTF both teams have to take the flag to one point of the map whoever gets it first wins the round.
None of these gamemodes are played competitvely.
6. Attack and Defence (CP)
Attack and Defence is like Payload but with Control points its usually played by 9V9. RED team has 1 minute to set up defences to stop BLU. BLU has to capture all the controls points to win but everytime they capture a point they gain time. For RED to win they have to defend for a certain amount of time ranging from 5 to 20 minutes. This one is weird because maps such as dustbowl are not played competitvely but maps like Steel are.
This game does have trading but the economy is kinda ♥♥♥♥ed at the moment (Check Backpack.tf) but hey Hats are cool amirite?
Overall Team Fortress 2 is a great game I love the game and it is my favorite of all time. I suggest if you don't play it to try it.
EDIT* (22/11/2017) TF2 is a timeless masterpiece.

The game itself is 26 gb, and your steam local files can be up to 15 more gb. That's 41 gb for a game in which you have to pay thousands to even get every bit of it's content. Large chunks of that content that is installed ARE UNACCESSABLE, and rarely even alive if it's active at the time (take any halloween map for example). Meet your match was a flop, and still is, XP is a waste of time and casual is full of completely oblivious noobs that need a tutorial run, mind you that the ingame tutorial is BARE BONES to the core and hasn't been updated since game release and it'd be better to play a completely different game to get a feel for TF2 than its own tutorial. The Ingame economy that was a "team decision" has been and will continue to spiral out of control until the TF2 team decides to make non-tradable keys craftable or at least some sort of ref sink to lower the prices of keys and balance out the rest of it, however considering only around 16 developers on the Tf2 team actually currently exist (or less, we don't know), they're going to keep focusing on a long-overdue update that was promised mid-late summer, and neglect the rest of the problems they've already created or are forming. Hit-register is still finicky, and can only be trusted when you're on a high tick community server with good connection, and even then, any lagging player will make hell on earth for snipers, scouts, and pyros. Pyros themselves are another topic on their own, they've powercreeped over the last 2 updates (last year) and since then have been dominant when played by a moderately to well skilled player. This creates a conflict considering the next update will be all about the pyro, and it'd be wrong/weird to nerf the pyro in its namesake update, so you have to expect that pyros will become even more powerful in the next update, driving away players of classes that are vulnerable to pyro (demo, scout, soldier, medic, spy, sniper, engy, heavy, hell even other pyros). You can see that the game has been gradually wearing thin on its playerbase as well, when running casual can drop you in empty servers 1/4th of the time, and it takes longer than 20-30 minutes to even get additional players in a half full server. Currently, as well, ranking up/staying in casuals for XP is virtually useless as you're not rewarded for leveling, which begs the question why even bother? Not just for the player to rank up, but also for the team to even implement the system, it doesn't do anything with matchmaking, and it certainly doesn't really bring you pride or thankfulness. This game has many flaws, and open doors that the team just won't take, and for that, it's still a nonrecommended game in my book, even after 2500+ hours (i'm counting the several months I didn't have internet as well) I've put into this game, and don't even get me started on how many keys I've purchased.

This is a well made, stylized, team based first person shooter. Teamwork is needed to win at higher levels of play, though lone wolfing is fine on lower skill levels such as on most public servers. There are 9 classes to choose from. Each class has unique weapons and abilities that allow each to fulfill a unique roll as part of a larger team. This provides for a challenging and rewarding experience when faced against opponents of similar or better skill levels. The game has an active dev team that continues to release updates to the game that add new content such as weapons or game modes.
At the time of this review, there are two official modes of play: player versus player and 'Mann Versus Machine'.
Player versus player is a mode where one team of players battles against another team of players. Within this mode, there are different types of maps. Each type of map has it's own objective or objectives for each team to achieve.
'Mann Versus Machine' is a mode where a team of up to 6 players battles against waves of bots. Players collect money from destroyed bots. The money is divided equally among players in the team and can be used to purchase upgrades and abilities for the next wave of bots. The pay to play sub-mode, "Mann Up", gives rewards upon completing a "tour".
In addition to the official modes of play, there are several player made mods that introduce other modes of play such as 'Versus Saxton Hale', where a team of players battles against a player playing as a character named Saxton Hale; 'Dodge Ball', where two teams of players playing as Pyros must airblast rockets and other projectiles back and forth in order to stay alive; 'Zombie Mod', where a team of players must make it to the end of the map without dying to zombies that are played by other players; to name just a few of the many player made mods available.
In addition to game play, players will randomly receive free items from the game. Some of the free items given out are weapons, hats and crates. Hats can be worn by a class to change the appearance of that class. Crates can be opened with a key. Keys can be purchased from the Mann Co Store or from the Steam Community Market or traded for from another player. Most crates will list which items can be found within them.
The game has several communities for a player to choose from if a community is what you are looking for. The game is easy to pick up and play, either alone or with friends, yet has a depth of play that will keep you from becoming bored too quickly. The dynamics between the different classes, weapons, play styles, skill levels, modes and maps provides content for many hours of play. I have been playing since November 2007 and I still return to the game on a regular basis.

The original point of the game revolved around playing game modes such as capturing the enemy intelligence, pushing a bomb to the enemy base, or controlling a whole map by Scout-rushing control points, but now all this is nothing more than a small minigame to pass the time with while you wait for more weapons and rare items to magically drop into your inventory while doing fu-ck all on Achievement, Trade, Idle or non-serious, fun-oriented servers.
Once played by and cherished by many gamers, now the game is only played by weeaboos, bronies, furries, meme loving morons from 9gag and Reddit, basement dwelling social justice warrior trannies from Tumblr, 12 year olds, and girl gamers. Comes with a flamethrower, burn everything!. Shotgun = Shotgun. Melee is pretty useful, does more damage after you light someone on fire
Demoman
Demoman comes with a grenade launcher, sticky bomb launcher and a bottle... all i got to say here
Heavy
Minigun, Shotgun, and his own fists. 300 health
Engineer
Comes with a shotgun, a pistol, a wrench, construction PDA, And destruction PDA. The construction PDA can be used to build 4 buildings. However to build these things costs metal. Metal is shown in the bottom right corner of your HUD and starts at a max of 200 but can't go any farther then that. The sentry gun is a sentry that starts at level one, but can be upgraded to level 2, then to 3 but no farther then that. it costs 200 metal to upgrade a single sentry and 130 to make one.You have to smack your buildings with a wrench in order to upgrade them. On level one it shoots very slowly and can be destroyed easily. on level 2 it gets two miniguns on it and starts doing some buissness, however it is still very weak and does little damage. On level 3 it can launch 4 rockets at a time and gains much more health. Then there is the dispenser which heals people and gives the engineer more metal over time. costs 100 metal. on level one it only gives out 40 metal per dispense and heals people very slowly and does not give that much ammo to the player's weapons. Level 2 gives 50 metal on dispense and is much faster at healing and giving ammo. level 3 the dispenser range is increased and the healing and ammo give out take 3 seconds and gives out 60 metal per dispense. The teleporter entrance is a building that can be created in conjunction with the exit teleporter to teleport players from point A to point B. first level it is very slow to work and once someone has teleported it takes a century to be able to teleport again. Sniper

Medic

Spy
Spy comes with a revolver, sapper, knife, and a disguise kit. The revolver is a revolver. The sapper is used to remove the engineer's buildings however not automaticly, The engineer can come over and remove the sapper. However over time the building will eventually destroy itself. The knife is interesting, it does low damage, however on a successful stab in the back the target will instantly die. Control Points.

The red team must defend the blue team from capturing the control points until time runs out and vice versa. once a control point has been captured the enemy team gains time. Playload

Playload Race.
Same concept but two playloads and no time. Enjoy!

Hold the single control point till time runs out.

Team Fortress 2 isn't anywhere close to your average FPS. Sure, there are some shooters with some rather interesting attributes, but Team Fortress 2 blows all of that out of the water. This FPS has some of the most unexpected attributes ever introduced into a shooter. You have hats, and I'm not talking about Shields or Exo-Suits. I'm talking about real hats, fedoras, trilbies, batting helmets, and then some. With those hats come some Unusual variants. Unusuals are those kinds of hats but with a special effect added to them, like Scorching, Burning, Nuts-n-Bolts, Terror-Watt, Bubbles, etc. These hats are incredibly rare and pricy, so don't expect to get them on your first try, by either trading or unboxing crates.  You also have interesting weapons. Some of those weapons used to be overpowered in many ways, but with the recent update, the Gun Metelle Update, it rebalanced almost all of the weapons in TF2. Another thing worth noting about TF2 is the classes and the variety of them. You have your Generic ones, Soldier, Sniper, Heavy, Engineer, and Demoman, but you also have interesting ones like the Medic, Scout, Pyro, and Spy. What makes the generic classes seem so interesting is that they have amazing personalities. There is some depth to them, but you don't really see a lot of personality depth with your average FPS protagonist, do you? The gamemodes have been seen before, Multiplayer, which consists of Payload, Control Points, King of the Hill, Capture the Flag, Special Delivery, Attack/Defense, and offline training. But then, a new gamemode arised that seemed new, but isn't. It was Mann Vs. Machine, which is pretty much Call of Duty's "Zombies" mode. Now, I'm not trying to say that this game was perfect, no. I'm saying this game was different, in a good way. This opened the FPS genere to be unique, innovative, and show a little color. Not to mention changing the way FPS games work with their gameplay, changing it from just killing to team-based objectives.
All in all, Team Fortress 2 is a very astounding FPS and should be remembered for its unique feel and humor.
My verdict: 97/100.

Cons-

Team Fortress 2. One of the most action-packed and well-balanced shooters out there. "Get out and fight" is the rule, not "hide in cover and wait for someone else to act". A good balance to other shooters which rely mainly on cover-based shooting. The game was (WAS!) one of my favourite shooters of all time and I honestly did not mind any game changes so far.
SO. FAR.
Because then came the gun mettle upgrade which brought tons of new stuff (thanks valve) and, by the way, misfigured the gameplay. Balance was regularly worked on in the games long history, sometimes for the better, sometimes for the worse, but never it even posed a serious threat in any way to the overall balance. But now, many of the weapons are totally useless (Loch ´n Load, Baby Faces Blaster... ) while others (Big Earner, Tomislav, Deadringer...) are way stronger (sometimes not bad, making a bad weapon useful, but often it made strong weapons immensely overpowered, especially soldier and spy epuipment). The Changes are so big that even the Weapons that remained unchanged are now often much worse compared to the buffed ones.
Until Valve fixes this issue the game gets negative review, because balance is very important to me and was a strong point of the games for a long time.
Update: Matchmaking was improved considerably by patches but I would still prefer the old system where i can select the server myself and won´t have the trouble to search a new match each round.

How does one describe the experience of Team Fortress 2?
"The #1 War-Themed Hat Simulator" - borrowing this apt description.
This game has unique characters with vivid personalities and quirks, and enough crazy hats to give the Kentucky Derby a run for its money. The fun doesn't stop at hats, there are goofy weapons and maps to keep your interest piqued. Want to decapitate someone with a golf club? Easy. Want to jump across chasms by blasting a rocket at your feet? Done.
Trading can be a bit difficult, but there are plenty of interesting servers with community-made game modes outside of the normal gamestyles. Dodgeball, TF2Ware, and Upgrade Shops are a few examples of some server mods. The game is free to play now, so give it a try. Just be sure to watch out for DemoPans and BoxSpies!

Team Fortress 2 (commonly abbreviated as TF2) is a team-based first-person shooter multiplayer video game developed by Valve Corporation. It is the sequel to the 1996 mod Team Fortress for Quake and its 1999 remake. On April 8, 2008, it was released for Windows. The game was updated to support OS X on June 10, 2010, and Linux on February 14, 2013.
In Team Fortress 2, players join one of two teams comprising nine character classes, battling in a variety of game modes including arena, capture the flag, and open beta gamemodes such as mannpower. Team Fortress 2 has cartoon-like visuals and is powered by Valve's Source engine.
Team Fortress 2 received critical acclaim for its art direction, gameplay, humor, and use of character in a multiplayer-only game. Valve continues to release new content, including many hats, weapons, maps, and game modes. (Such as the recent "Gun Mettle Update")

Team Fortress 2 is a first person fast-paced team-based shooter developed by Valve Software that combines the fun of killing people with colourful animated graphics. Still going strong after 8 years, TF2 offers an easy way to lose time in multiple game modes and collecting hats.
* Gameplay
Following an old school Quake based formula of having multiple distinct classes in a FPS, TF2 gives everyone something to play:

Classes have an interesting synergy and counters which are expressed through various game modes such as Capture the Flag, Attack/Defend, Special Delivery and achievement_idle. Personally, I prefer most Payload and Control Points. With a healthy variety of maps, games can last from 2 minutes to 2 hours, if your local Engineers feel particularly lazy. If the default game modes aren't your thing, there's always Mann vs. Machine, a mode reminiscent of Killing Floor (Tour of Duty tickets recommended), except with ever predictable robots, or you can download custom mods such as Dodgeball, Trade Plaza, Prop Hunt and so on.
* Weapons and balance
All classes have a variety of unlockable weapons that change the way a class is played in an interesting/infuriating way or simply switch some subtle numbers. While there's no blatantly overpowered weapons, although certain classes become very powerful for a short time, until Valve brings back the righteous balance. Sometimes, they don't even do that, for the cases of Gunslinger and Splendid Screen. I do not have an issue playing with or against slightly overpowered items, as learning to counter is the reward itself. Classes maintain synergies and counters despite unlockable weapons, although the average public server heavily favours stacking certain classes such as Scout rush, Soldier/Demoman explosive spam, Heavies, Engineer camps or the ever deadly Sniper squads. For a more fair play, there's plenty of competitive leagues and matches.
* Trading and economy
It is impossible to mention TF2 without bringing up the many ways you can customize your classes, from the fairly simple kill counting weapons to the classy/garish/charming/pretentious hats that alter the way your class looks, to the amazement/scorn of other people. The most valuable items are the tacky unusuals, which cost a sizeable portion of your disposable income, but they ensure a pocket Medic wherever you go (not to be confused with a cosmetic). I find that collecting hats is one of the more enjoyable things you can do, if the shooting becomes slightly boring. The economy is simple to grasp, although don't expect to get a discount from other people. Furthermore, it might be difficult to start because of the high key price, which is at time of the writing 19.33 refined metal, which equates to 174 scrap or 348 weapons.
* Closing comments
While being somewhat neglected in favour in comparison to Dota 2 and Counter Strike: Global Offensive, TF2 has remained a great way to spend Summers, one ctf_2fort match at a time. Newcomers should be vary of fairly high system requirements (due to outdated Source code) and slightly hostile environment for newbies. I recommend it as a first game for people starting on Steam, as you can find great friends, have fun and being exploring the community.

Team Fortress 2 (commonly abbreviated as TF2) is a team-based first-person shooter multiplayer video game developed by Valve Corporation. It is the sequel to the 1996 mod Team Fortress for Quake and its 1999 remake. On April 8, 2008, it was released for Windows. The game was updated to support OS X on June 10, 2010, and Linux on February 14, 2013.
In Team Fortress 2, players join one of two teams comprising nine character classes, battling in a variety of game modes including arena, capture the flag, and open beta gamemodes such as mannpower. Team Fortress 2 has cartoon-like visuals and is powered by Valve's Source engine.
Team Fortress 2 received critical acclaim for its art direction, gameplay, humor, and use of character in a multiplayer-only game. Valve continues to release new content, including many hats, weapons, maps, and game modes. (Such as the recent "Gun Mettle Update")

Performance. This is also a complaint on the engine's performance in general, it should be re-optimized for the modern age, but this is never going to happen.

Before I made this account, I had a small account I used to play TF2, and it was smalltime. But, it introduced me to the world of TF2. One of the finest FPS experiences I'd ever seen. With 9, vastly different, varied playstyles, personality and charm; TF2 was a gem, and it was free. Fast forward to: July 11; 2012, when I made this account, and joined TF2 with an account where I actually knew how to play better.
TF2 is still a wonderful experience, through all the changes; from the best new content, to the most minor updates; there is generally a shred of care thrown in... but sadly, here in 2017; things have changed drastically. And I can safely say, playing this game for so long; I've loved every moment... but it's time to face facts: TF2 is having trouble, and nobody could care less.
TF2 has a myriad of problems; ranging from an unclear identity (Is it a casual shooter? Cause it does nothing to teach new players; is it a comp shooter? Cause it's certainly not well balanced enough for it.) to the massive amounts of grief caused by the dark side of the community (Hackers ruining games for fun, Hijackers trying to steal rare backpacks, and griefers just trying to ruin the experience for everyone); it's a tough call to find TF2 anything but lazy nowadays. Especially in regards to the team; which has been confirmed by many people who have visited Valve; to be under staffed and run in an ineffective way.
Why does this matter? Because the fate of TF2 hangs in the balance; and until people start caring, the game will see a lapse in players who care. Bigger TF2 players who were respected and loved the game have moved on to other games; there are other games just like TF2 that offer the same experience and sometimes more. Paladins and A Fistful of Frags offer a similar shooter feel; and are also F2P. TF2 still comes recommended, but until Valve shows us they still care; it's a hard game to stomach anymore.
The Jungle Inferno finally dropped. The Pyro has been rebalanced, and we've seen many, many new additions to the game. It's an exciting time to play TF2.

So after a meme review , I've decided to make a serious one.
This game affected my life in a huge way. Not only that it got me to invest more than 3000 hours into it, but It also got me to meet a lot of other people whom I now consider close friends. The game got me to really expand my personality and meet other people , friends  and my now-ex-girlfriend.
This game also changed the way I look at other games , how I choose them and how I play them , and I'm really, really thankful for all these things.
But now It's time for the actual review.(Prepare for wall of text , TL:DR at the bottom)
This is a Free-To-Play game , in fact , a TRUE FTP game. Even though there is an In-game store where you can buy In-game items , all of those Items are purely cosmetic and do not affect your or other's gameplay at all . You won't get an In-game advantage just because you bought a hat in the store , it'll only make your character look better , give them a unique look.
The game has 9 playable classes, all of them are completely different from eachother , with different personalities . They are categorized into 3 sections : Offense , Defense , and Support , each section consisting of 3 characters . Some may argue that a few of them belong to other sections , but their core gameplay is related to their sections . I'm going to give a few quick impressions of all classes , and recommend some for new players:
Offense
Scout: Probably the highest base mobilty in the game ( fastest running speed , doublejump) , quick burst-damage scattergun , but very low health (Not very recommended for new players)
Soldier: Rocket launcher capable of huge damage potentional , high health , low base speed , and great mobilty with rocket jumping(This requires hours of practise)(Recommended for new players , due to high damage and good amount of health)
Pyro:Strong , recently buffed close range class , average speed (good speed with the new jetpack) and decent health (Recommended , BUT ONLY PLAY AS HIM IF THERE IS NO ONE  ELSE PLAYING WITH HIM , otherwise you'll create a living hell on the server.)
Defense
Demoman: Incredibly high burst damage , low base speed (can be overshadowed by sticky jumping , which is similar to rocket jumping) , capable of defending multiple areas at once , decent health(Not recommended , due to tricky aiming )
Heavy: Very high close-mid range damage , Highest health in the game (300HP) , but the slowest movement speed at the same time , makes a deadly combo with a Medic (Recommended to new players , very new player friendly class.)
Engineer: Very weak by himself (low base damage , low hp) , but he can build buildings(sentries , dispensers and teleporters , which can be very useful to the team. (Maybe recommended , because he is easy to play , but also easy to lose all your 'hard' work )
Support:
Spy: Low hp , but can go invisble for a few seconds with the invis watch (Almost for eternity with an other watch if he stands still) , and he can insta-kill enemies by backstabbing them. (Not recommended , especially if your team already has 2 other Spies)
Medic:The weakest class by himself ,but he wasnt meant to be a combat class anyways . He can heal and even overheal teammates , while collecting charge to use an ability called Übercharge , which gives him and the player he's currently healing invulnerability , which can completely change the tide of the battle ( Not recommended to new players , due to high skill ceiling )
Sniper: Low health , not very strong at close range, but the strongest class at long range (His Sniper Rifle is capable of killing any class with full charge with only one shot!) (Not recommended for new players , because you need good aiming skills and positioning to be effective with him , and for God's sake , DON'T play with him if there are more than 1 snipers on your team!)
The game has 14 different game modes , with 86 maps to play on  , and many more on community servers ,so there's always something new to play!
The gameplay is very good , considering this is a 10 year old game . It's fun , entertaining ,and sometimes unpredictable , so there will always be suprises , even for experienced players. It might have some bugs here and there , but none of them are game breaking, and they get fixed pretty quickly .
Probably the strongest aspect of the game is the Community . After being part of many different Gaming communities, I can safely say , that this is the most passionate , caring , and strongest community I've ever been part of . Sure ,some players are pretty toxic , but tell me a game without toxic players . Exactly , and the toxic part of the community is in the minority , so there's nothing to worry about .
Even though Valve shown the weakness of their development ways , the small team behind Team Fortress 2 is very hard-working and passionate about the game's future .Even though they can't release updates as quickly as they used to do , they are still updating this game with new content .
Some might say that the updates are getting worse and worse , and that the game is dying (Every game and everything is dying , just not very quickly) , but I enjoyed every major update in my total gametime (except for the Community Robotic Boogalo update , I didnt like that one).
TL:DR
Do I recommend this game ? Absolutely . This game is completely free , so even if you dont like it , there's nothing to lose if you delete it . The updates are not very frequent , but they are good.
This is my review for the game , thank you for reading ,and I hope you'll have fun with this classic!

I absolutely loved this game! The characters, the art, the themes! I loved it!
But that's "Loved", not "love".
Before I get any hatred towards this, I am a guy who needs motivation to play a game for an extended amount of time, such as Call Of Duty (pls no hate) which gave me motivation to play multiplayer and level up, but as soon as I reached that higher level, I got bored and stopped playing (which is when I moved onto PC gaming). A multitude of my most played games consist of this motivational mechanics, like Payday 2, Terraria, BF3/BF4. And Team Fortress 2's approach to this motivational mechanic was the addition of hats and weapons, crates and keys, and item effects. This developed the community in a whole and kept the game alive way past other multiplayer shooters (8 years!). And the community in this game is beautiful; As they create immense amounts of artwork, models and maps. They also made the TF2 economy which was my motivation to play this game for over 1,000 hours. For two years, I was estatic to hop on my favorite "Trade_" map and get me some profit! I even got myself my first unusual which made me thirst for more! It made me lust for those very rare pixels! But as time goes by I see the inevitable problem that all economies face. Inflation. As more and more people play the game, the more weapons drop, and as more weapons drop, more metal get created and pushed into the system and as metal was the main economic currency for trading unique hats things started to change. Keys were worth more and more refined metal everyday (from 2.33 to 15.77!!!) which didn't really affect me that much as I had moved onto unusual trading. However, the same problem goes for buds, the main currency for unusual hats. Inflation strikes again. For people who don't know, duping is the act of getting your items replaced by steam support after they've been stolen from a hacker, now, I think you can see where this goes but if the account dupes their items, that means there's a whole inventory that's been put in circulation twice which has a very negative effect on the rarity and price of the items. This leads onto a lot of buds being duped that the price has gone from 20 keys to 4 keys. This deeply affects the prices of my inventory and I fear for the overall worth of my inventory so as a last resort I trade in my unusuals for a CS:GO knife. And as the economy countinued to downfall I lose my motivation and my interest in the game. I miss the ecstacy of getting a sweet new hat. It breaks my heart, but I have to part ways with this beauty of a shooter.
TL:DR - I'm a materialistic prick that uses hats as motivation and I lose interest as my materialistic properties become worthless.

Team Fortress Two is a fun, popular multiplayer Shooter that has an entirely different gameplay style and look than other shooters, like Call of Duty or Battlefield. It has 9 classes. The Scout, The Soldier, The Pyro, The Demoman, The Heavy, The Engineer, The Medic, The Sniper and the Spy. All classes have their pros and cons, and all their weapons have them as well. It also adds fun into the game with cool-looking weapons, funny hats and enjoyable taunts for all classes! (Thank god valve finally added a heavy taunt into the game!) I've been around for not too long, but I have 700 hours on TF2. It's an addicting game with multiple gamemodes and servers. I recommend downloading it, for its been Free-To-Play since the Uber Update.
P.S: Some of the players hate on people who are Free-To-Play. Ignore them for a better experience, because some Pay-To-Plays (like me) like to help the Free-To-Plays in TF2.

Alright, I think I've played this game long enough (1,600+ hours) to provide a fair and objective review of it purely from a technical perspective. Keep in mind that this is a cautionary review, as TF2 will by no means appeal to everyone.
Without further adieu, let's get into it.
+ Pretty much the smoothest and most satisfying gameplay offered by any FPS. Every class feels vital to securing victory and the controls are extremely fluid, as to be expected in a Valve game. The gameplay nails that "easy to pick up, hard to master" vibe that keeps me coming back every time; a notable example of this is the seemingly simplistic and straightforward gameplay of the Soldier that is enhanced 10x when you get the hang of rocket jumping.
+ Generally speaking, the graphics are pleasing to the eye and the game will run exceptionally well, even on older hardware. With certain tweaks to the game's config files, I get 120+ FPS on almost every map (with the notable exception of the recent Gun Mettle maps, which are suffering from some noticeable performance issues that will probably be patched very soon).
+ What seems like a shallow and greedy microtransaction system on the surface actually contains an insane amount of depth and value. Don't like the hats you're wearing? Simply toss a trade request towards somebody wearing a hat that you want and behold the wonder of a bartering based economy. Tired of battle? Simply tap "G" and dance to your heart's content; with luck, the enemy team will put down their weapons and join you. The silliness and fun that oozes from this game is palpable.
+ The community definitely makes this game a gem. If you're bored of the maps that come with the game, simply fire up the server browser and explore a completely community created map. Looking for some great deals or wanting to sell your old junk? There are thousands of servers designed solely for trading at your fingertips. Have you mastered a specific class to the point of dominating everyone on public servers? Fire up your favorite server browser and play with people of equivalent skill in competitive matches.
+ You can kill people with ham and a frying pan. Let that sink in.
- The game has a habit of being abandoned by Valve for prolonged periods of time, starving the community of much needed updates. A recent example of this was the vacuum of time between the Christmas 2014 update and the Gun Mettle update, the latter being released a couple weeks ago. That's nearly
of the game existing without any major updates, which is curious given how popular it still is.
- Some maps, especially the ones made by the community and later added to the official roster by Valve, have some glaring glitches and technical issues that have still not been fixed. A great example of this is koth_suijin, a map shipped with Gun Mettle, that causes HUGE FPS drops even for players with powerful rigs.
- Major balance issues tend to pop up from time to time. The Loch n' Load, an alternative to the Demoman's primary weapon, was completely and totally overpowered for months upon months with no sign of Valve nerfing it until the aforementioned Gun Mettle update. Be wary of players exploiting these balance issues and playing with loadouts that are totally broken and difficult to counter.
If you like shooting things, play this game. Yes, there are issues, but the amount of fun and depth that this game exudes definitely compensates for it. I've spent 1600 hours in the world of TF2, and I couldn't be happier about it.
